1.x: Milk is rich in calcium and potassium but poor in iron, so 'calcium and potassium' is right; any option with iron is wrong.

1.s: Which one among these is related to the deficiency of potassium ?
1.x:
Book key: low blood pressure. Strictly, low potassium is better known for muscle weakness/paralysis and tends to raise blood pressure; hypotension is only an occasional sign (NORD, Hypokalemia; PMF General Science Part 3).
The book key is low blood pressure. Muscle weakness and paralysis are the best-known signs of potassium deficiency, so option (a) is tempting; anaemia is iron and blurry vision vitamin A.

1.s: Iodised salt is useful because it–
1.x: Iodised salt is table salt mixed with a minute amount of various salts of the element iodine. Iodine deficiency can cause thyroid gland problems.

1.s: Which of the following species possesses a corymb inflorescence?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Gulmohar (Delonix regia) bears flowers in corymbs, where lower flower stalks are longer so the flowers come to one level. Mango and teak have panicles; Gliricidia has racemes.

1.s: Which of the following is not a chemical fertilizer?
1.x: Urea (N), superphosphate (P) and potassium nitrate (K, N) are fertilisers. Sodium sulphate supplies no major plant nutrient, and sodium is not essential for most plants.

1.s: Gaseous exchange takes place in leaves through tiny pores for the purpose of photosynthesis. What are these pores ?
1.x: Stomata are the tiny pores in leaves through which gases are exchanged. Chloroplast and chlorophyll are involved in photosynthesis, and the vacuole is a storage sac.

1.s: The ultimate cause of water movement in a plant stem against gravity is
1.x: Transpiration from leaves creates a suction (transpiration pull) that draws water up the xylem against gravity, so it is the ultimate cause.

1.s: In which one of the following physiological processes, excess water escapes in the form of droplets from a plant ?
1.x: Guttation is the loss of excess water as liquid droplets from leaf margins. Transpiration loses water as vapour.

1.s: Which type of plants are very tall and have hard and thick brown stem?
1.x: Trees are very tall plants with a hard, thick, brown woody stem (trunk). Herbs have soft green stems and shrubs are shorter and bushy.

1.s: Who propounded the theory of evolution?
1.x: Charles Darwin propounded the theory of evolution by natural selection (On the Origin of Species, 1859). Wallace independently proposed a similar idea, but Darwin is credited.

1.s: What is the basis of classifying various plant tissues as meristematic tissue and permanent tissue?
1.x: Meristematic tissues are classified as such because their cells keep dividing, while permanent tissues have lost the capacity to divide. So the basis of classification is dividing capacity.

1.s: Which one among the following produces seeds but not flowers ?
1.x: Pine is a gymnosperm and bears naked seeds in cones without flowers. Cashew, coffee and groundnut are angiosperms that flower.

1.s: Who was written book named ‘Origin of Species’?
1.x: Charles Darwin wrote 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), presenting natural selection.

1.s: Smallest flowering plant is
1.x: Wolffia (duckweed) is the smallest flowering plant known.

1.s: Mangifera indica is the scientific name of
1.x: Mangifera indica is the binomial name of the mango; guava, amla and jackfruit have different scientific names.

1.s: In the names Mangifera Indica (mango), Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion). The terms Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera represent the higher level of
1.x: The genus names Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are taxa, i.e. units of classification; the specific epithet is the second word (indica, tuberosum, leo).

1.s: Which one of the following denotes a ‘true’ fruit?
o: When only the thalamus of the flower grows and develops into a fruit.
When only the receptacle of the flower develops into a fruit.
When fruit originates only from the calyx of a flower.
When only the ovary of the flower grows into a fruit.
1.x: A true fruit develops only from the ovary of the flower; fruits that develop from other parts such as the thalamus or receptacle are false fruits.

1.s: If the xylem of a plant is mechanically blocked, which of the following functions of the plant will be affected?
1.x: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals (solutes) upward, so blocking it affects the transport of both.

1.s: Which one of the following is not a component of conducting tissue in plants?
1.x: Pericycle is a layer of cells just inside the endodermis and is not a conducting element; xylem (tracheids, fibres) and phloem (sieve tubes) are the conducting tissues.

1.s: What is the shape of the two guard cells which enclose stomata ?
1.x: Guard cells enclosing a stoma are kidney (bean) shaped in dicots.

1.s: The only living tissue in plant xylem is
1.x: Xylem parenchyma is the only living cell type in xylem; tracheids, vessels (trachea) and fibres are dead at maturity.

1.s: Which element is specifically required by plants for the synthesis of amino acids and proteins?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Nitrogen is needed for amino acids, proteins, chlorophyll and nucleic acids. C, H and O are in all organic compounds, and iron is for chlorophyll synthesis.

1.s: The element not present in fertilisers is
1.x:
Printed key: hydrogen (not a fertiliser nutrient). Strictly, urea and ammonium fertilisers contain hydrogen atoms, so the stem means 'nutrient element'.
Fertilisers are sold for their nutrient elements N, P and K, and chlorine comes in muriate of potash (KCl). Hydrogen is not a fertiliser nutrient: plants get it from water.

1.s: Which of the following is not a Primary function of a green leaf?
1.x: Food making, gas exchange and transpiration are leaf functions; conduction of food and water is mainly done by the vascular tissue of the stem.

1.s: What is the yellow dust present in the middle of a flower called?
1.x: The yellow dust in the middle of a flower is pollen, made in the anthers of the stamens.

1.s: A Parenchyma cell which stores ergastic substance is known as
1.x: Idioblasts are specialised parenchyma cells that store ergastic substances such as crystals, tannins or oils.

1.s: What is thick vein present in the middle of the leaf called?
1.x: The thick central vein of a leaf is the midrib; venation is the pattern of veins.

1.s: Pollens are produced in
1.x: Pollen grains are produced in the anther of the stamen; the stigma only receives them.

1.s: In which part of the female flower, fertilisation take place?
1.x: Fertilisation takes place in the ovule inside the ovary; the pollen tube grows down from the stigma through the style.

1.s: Which among the following is a male part of a flower ?
1.x: The stamen (anther + filament) is the male part; stigma, style and the whole pistil are female.

1.s: Damage to the apical meristem of a growing young plant will affect the
1.x: The apical meristem at shoot and root tips causes growth in length, so damaging it affects the length of the plant.

1.s: Any one parameter is not good enough to demonstrate growth through the life of a flowering plant because
o: lateral meristems appear later in life.
apical meristems contribute to elongation while lateral meristems increase girth.
increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly.
1.x: NCERT: growth is basically an increase in protoplasm, which is difficult to measure directly, so proxies (weight, length, area, cell number) are used and no one of them suffices.

1.s: Which one of the following tissues is responsible for increase of girth in the stem of a plant?
1.x: The lateral meristem (vascular and cork cambium) adds girth; intercalary meristem adds length at internodes.

1.s: Which of the following pair represent the Correct pair of reproductive parts of a flower ?
1.x: The reproductive whorls are the stamens (male) and carpels (female); sepals and petals are accessory whorls.

1.s:
Statement I Complex tissue is made up of more then one type of cells. Statement II Meristems are examples of permanent tissue.
Codes
o: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Both Statements I and II are correct.
Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
1.x: Complex tissues (xylem, phloem) have more than one cell type (I correct); meristems are dividing tissues, not permanent tissues (II incorrect).

1.s: Arrangement of leaves in a plant is called as ……… .
1.x: The arrangement of leaves on a stem is phyllotaxy (alternate, opposite, whorled).

1.s: Which one of the following features is an indication for modification of stem of a plant?
1.x: Potato is a stem tuber – its 'eyes' are nodes with buds, proof it is a modified stem. Onion scales are leaves, pea tendrils are modified leaflets and carrot is a root.

1.s: Fruit of which of the following plant is found in the underground soil?
1.x: The peanut flower stalk (peg) pushes the ovary into the soil, so the fruit (pod) ripens underground. Potato and onion are stems, carrot a root – not fruits.

1.s: Flower in which pollination takes place through insect, their pollen grains are
1.x: Insect-pollinated flowers have rough, sticky pollen that clings to insects. Smooth, dry, light pollen is typical of wind pollination.

1.s: To study meiosis in plants, the best part would be
1.x: Meiosis occurs in reproductive tissue, so young anthers are best. Root and shoot apices and leaf cells divide by mitosis.

1.s: Intercalary meristems are found in
1.x: Intercalary meristems lie between mature tissues at the base of internodes (and leaves), as in grasses. Apical meristems occupy terminal and lateral buds.

1.s: Most of photosynthesis process occur in
o: blue and red region of light.
in the green and yellow region of light.
in the blue and orange region of light.
in the violet and orange region of light.
1.x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red light, so most photosynthesis occurs there. Green and yellow light are largely reflected.

1.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Annual rings are distinct in plants which grow in temperate region.

II. growing rings of plant is consist of spring wood and autumn wood.
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct about annual ring?
1.x: Both statements are true: annual rings are clear in temperate trees with marked seasons, and each ring has spring wood and autumn wood.

1.s: Which of the following plants is carnivorous ?
1.x: The Venus flytrap traps insects to get nitrogen. Cypress vine, amaryllis and hyacinth are ordinary flowering plants.

1.s:
Consider the following fuction of xylem.

I. Conduction of water

II. Conduction of minerals.

III. Mechanical support.
Which of the function (s) of xylem given above is/are correct?
1.x: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals, and its lignified cells give mechanical support. All three are correct.

1.s: Role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis is
1.x: Chlorophyll's role is to absorb light energy. Water is absorbed by roots and CO2 enters through stomata.

1.s: Which one of the following gas comes out during photosynthesis?
1.x: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 and gives out oxygen. Hydrogen and chlorine are not released.

1.s: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from splitting of
1.x: The oxygen given off in photosynthesis comes from splitting (photolysis) of water, as isotope (O-18) experiments showed, not from CO2.

1.s:
Match the structures given in column
(A) with the functions given in column (B). Column A Column B
A. Stomata
1. Absorption of water

B. Xylem
2. Transpiration

C. Root hairs
3. Transport of food

D. Phloem
4. Transportion of water
Codes A B C D A B C D
1.x: Stomata – transpiration (2), xylem – water transport (4), root hairs – absorption of water (1), phloem – food transport (3): code 2 4 1 3.

1.s: Which botanist is credited with creating one of the first widely used natural systems of plant classification ?
1.x:
Official key: August Wilhelm Eichler (wording from Britannica). NCERT Biology XI Ch3 credits the natural system of flowering plants to George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker, so Hooker is also defensible.
Britannica describes August Wilhelm Eichler's system as one of the first widely used natural systems of plant classification (it was the first phylogenetic one and the base of Engler's system). Hooker, with Bentham, gave the other famous natural system, which is the tempting option; Robert Brown and Joseph Banks did not create such a system.

1.s: Which of these is the energy conversion that happens in the process called photosynthesis?
1.x: In photosynthesis, plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

1.s: Which one of the following statements about transport mechanism in plants is correct?
o: Diffusion of ions and small molecules across cell membrane requires energy.
Active transport of ions and small molecules across cell membrane against concentration gradient requires energy.
Cells conserve energy and no energy is required for transport of ions and small molecules against concentration gradient.
Cells do not transport ions across their membrane as these are charged molecules.
1.x: Active transport moves ions against the concentration gradient and requires energy (ATP); diffusion is passive.

1.s: Which of the following is not a process of asexual reproductions?
1.x: Syngamy is the fusion of gametes, a feature of sexual reproduction; budding, gemmulation and fragmentation are asexual methods.

1.s: The corner of the cells of collenchyma tissue in plant are thickened due to deposition of
1.x: Collenchyma has cell corners thickened with cellulose and pectin, giving flexible support; lignin is characteristic of sclerenchyma.

1.s: Which one of the following is active transport?
o: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient without the use of energy.
It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from photosynthesis.
It is the movement of a substance along a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
1.x: Active transport moves a substance against its concentration gradient using energy (ATP) from respiration; movement along the gradient or without energy is diffusion or passive transport.

1.s: Process by which plant prepare their food is
1.x: Plants prepare their food by photosynthesis, using light, CO2 and water in chlorophyll-containing cells.

1.s: Which of the following organelles of a cell is/are involved in photosynthesis ?
1.x: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll; mitochondria are for respiration.

1.s: The increase in length of stems and roots in plants is due to
1.x: Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots cause increase in length (primary growth); lateral meristem increases girth.

1.s: Which one of the following organisms has vascular tissues ?
1.x: Marsilea is a pteridophyte and has xylem and phloem. Cladophora and Anabaena are algae and Penicillium is a fungus, so none of them has vascular tissue.

1.s: Marsilea, fern and horse tail are examples of which one of the following plant groups ?
1.x: Marsilea, ferns and horsetails (Equisetum) are all seedless vascular plants, so they belong to Pteridophyta.

1.s: In the plant kingdom, ferns and fern allies belong to which group ?
1.x: Ferns and fern allies (horsetails, club mosses) make up the Pteridophyta.

1.s: Which of the following is/are the main absorbing organ/organs of plants?
1.x: Roots are the main absorbing organs of plants, taking up water and minerals from the soil through root hairs.

1.s: Which one of the following statements about classification of plants is correct?
o: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design.
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes.
1.x: Bryophytes lack a vascular system (xylem and phloem). Thallophytes lack a differentiated body, Funaria is a moss, and pteridophytes are cryptogams, not phanerogams.

1.s: Pteridophytes are also known as
1.x: Pteridophytes have vascular tissue but no seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams.

1.s: The nature of stele in primitive vascular plants was
1.x: Primitive vascular plants had a protostele, in which the xylem forms a solid core surrounded by phloem.

1.s: A flower is a modified
1.x: A flower is a modified shoot, formed from the shoot apical meristem, with its parts as modified leaves.

1.s: Gymnosperms are characterised by
1.x: Gymnosperms (e.g., pines, cycads) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary or fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.

1.s: First compound which is fixed during photosynthesis is
1.x: In the Calvin cycle CO2 combines with RuBP to give 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), the first stable product of carbon fixation. Glucose and starch form later.

1.s: Which one of the following is not used as fertiliser?
1.x: Ammonium nitrate, phosphate and sulphate supply nitrogen or phosphorus to crops and are fertilisers. Ammonium sulphide is not used as one.

1.s: An element present in Chlorophyll is
1.x: Chlorophyll has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.

1.s: Double fertilisation occurs among
1.x: Double fertilisation, in which one sperm fuses with the egg and the other with the polar nuclei, is unique to angiosperms.

1.s: The technique of the development of fruits without fertilisation is known as
1.x: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruit. Parthenogenesis is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg, not of a fruit.

1.s: The development of a fruit without fertilisation is called …
1.x: Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation. Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, so it is not the answer.

1.s: Which of the following is correct sequence of the events occurring during sexual reproduction in plants?
o: Seedling, Embryo formation, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Embryo formation, seedling, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote, Embryo formation, Seedling
Seedling, Embryo formation, Division of zygote, Pollination, Fertilisation
1.x: In plant sexual reproduction, pollination is followed by fertilisation, then division of the zygote, embryo formation and finally the seedling.

1.s: Which one of the following statements about meristematic tissue in plants is correct?
o: These are dead tissues and from wood.
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls.
These are present is the bark of a tree only.
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues.
1.x: Meristematic tissue is made of actively dividing cells, and its cell division drives plant growth. It is not dead and is not limited to bark.

1.s: Which one of the following plant tissues has dead cells?
1.x: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity. Epidermis, parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues.

1.s: The hormone related to drought tolerance is
1.x: Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata and so helps the plant tolerate drought.

1.s: Which one of the following agents does not contribute to propagation of plants through seed dispersal ?
1.x: Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals. Fungi do not disperse seeds.

1.s: The maximum amount of water, which plants need to grow, is absorbed by the following?
1.x: Root hairs are the main water-absorbing part of the root; water enters them by osmosis from the soil, so they absorb the most water for the plant.

1.s: Which among the following is an example of dicot seed?
1.x: Pulses (legumes) have two cotyledons so they are dicots; rice, wheat and maize are monocot cereals.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding vegetative propagation of plants ?

I. Vegetative propagation produces clonal population.

II. Vegetative propagation helps in eliminating the virus.

III. Vegetative propagation can be practised most of the year.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
1.x: Vegetative propagation gives clones (I) and can be done through much of the year (III). It does not eliminate viruses, since the virus passes on to the offspring, so II is wrong.

1.s: The by-product of photosynthesis is
1.x: In photosynthesis, water is split and oxygen is released as the by-product; sugar is the main product, and CO2 is a raw material.

1.s: Essential requirements for a seed to germinate
1.x: A seed needs water, air (oxygen) and a suitable temperature to germinate. Soil and sunlight are not essential; seeds sprout on wet cotton in the dark.

1.s: Siphoning type of mouth parts are present in:
1.x: A butterfly has a long coiled proboscis for siphoning nectar. The mosquito pierces and sucks, the cockroach chews and the housefly sponges.

1.s: It is harmful to sleep under a tree at night because the tree releases :
1.x: At night trees cannot photosynthesise but keep respiring, so they release carbon dioxide. They do not give out carbon monoxide or sulphur dioxide.

1.s: Which light is most effective in photosynthesis?
1.x: Red light (~655 nm) gives the highest rate of photosynthesis. Blue is also absorbed, but green is mostly reflected.

1.s: Chlorophyll absorbs ____ wavelengths of the sunlight.
o: More than one of the above
1.x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. Options with green are therefore wrong.

1.s: Which of the following has the shortest gestation period?
1.x: A goat carries its young about 150 days, less than a cow (~280), a buffalo (~310) or a camel (~390). The cow is the tempting option, but its gestation is nearly twice as long.

1.s: Which animal can not digest fibres properly ?
1.x: The pig is a monogastric omnivore and cannot digest fibre well. Goats and cows are ruminants, and elephants are hindgut fermenters, so their gut microbes break down cellulose.

1.s: Desert plants have longer root system because :
o: High temperature of the soil stimulates the growth of
Roots grow in search of water
Soil does not contain water, hence becomes compact
Roots moves opposite to the solar heat
1.x: Desert plants have long roots because roots grow towards water (hydrotropism), and in deserts the water lies deep. Soil heat does not cause it.

1.s: The range of pH of urine of herbivorous animals
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Herbivores have alkaline urine (pH about 7–8) because of their plant diet. Carnivores' urine is acidic, so the lower ranges are wrong.

1.s: In a bisexual flower, if androecium and gynoecium mature at different times, the phenomenon is known as
1.x: Dichogamy = anthers and stigma of a bisexual flower mature at different times, which favours cross-pollination. Herkogamy is a physical barrier between them.

1.s: Which of the following elements is not essential for plant growth ?
1.x: Sodium is not essential for most plants; potassium, calcium and magnesium are essential macronutrients.

1.s: Eight nucleated female gametophyte is found in
1.x: The typical angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) is 7-celled and 8-nucleate (Polygonum type).

1.s: Among living organisms, which one of the following is the most responsible factor for bringing about the origin of a new species?
1.x:
Official key / most books: mutation. Strictly: mutation supplies variation, while reproductive isolation is what actually completes speciation (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and keys give mutation (de Vries) as the source of new heritable variation that leads to new species.

1.s: World first Camel hospital is located in which city?
1.x: The Dubai Camel Hospital (opened 2017) is billed as the world's first dedicated camel hospital.

1.s: In the context of organic evolution, the loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of
1.x:
Official key / most books: use and disuse of organs (Lamarck). Strictly: modern biology explains it by natural selection; Lamarckism is rejected (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and the key explain limb loss in snakes by Lamarck's use and disuse of organs.

1.s: Which one of the following elements is present in the green pigment of leaves?
1.x: Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at the centre of its porphyrin ring (haemoglobin has iron).

1.s: Solar energy is converted into ATP in
1.x: In chloroplasts the light reactions convert solar energy into ATP (photophosphorylation) and NADPH; mitochondria make ATP from food, not from sunlight.

1.s: World’s first camel hospital is located in which city?
1.x: The Dubai Camel Hospital (opened 2017) is billed as the world's first dedicated camel hospital.

1.s: The reason of large scale diversity among the organisms is
1.x:
Official key / most books: adaptation. Strictly: diversity results from long-term evolution – natural selection acting on variation that mutation creates (NCERT Biology XII ch.6; Byjus NEET answer 'long-term evolutionary change').
Books and the BPSC key give adaptation – organisms adapting to varied environments – as the reason for large-scale diversity.

1.s: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to stigma of another flower of the same plant is called ?
1.x: Geitonogamy = pollen to another flower of the same plant; autogamy – same flower; xenogamy – a different plant.

1.s:
Consider the following statements

I. Homologous organs are common origin with different functions.

II. Analogous organs are different origin but perform similar function in different organisms.

III. Vestigial organs are non-functional and rudimentary organs in an organism which are fully developed and functional in phylogenetically related organisms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: All three are correct definitions: homologous – same origin, different function; analogous – different origin, same function; vestigial – rudimentary organs functional in relatives.

1.s: Which of the following is poisonous for dogs?
1.x: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs metabolise slowly, so it is toxic to them.

1.s: The broad, green part of the leaf is called
1.x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad green part where most photosynthesis occurs; midrib – central vein, petiole – stalk, stipules – basal outgrowths.

1.s: The broad , green part of the leaf is called
1.x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad green part; the petiole is the stalk, midrib and veins conduct and support.

1.s: At what age does bamboo flower?
1.x:
Printed key / books: 30 years. Strictly: it depends on the species – Melocanna baccifera (Mizoram mautam) flowers about every 48 years; PMF Part 3 p.34 says 50–100 years.
Bamboos flower only once, after long, species-specific intervals; the key takes about 30 years (Melocanna bambusoides ~30–35 years).

1.s: Maximum Photosynthesis occurs in:
1.x: Photosynthesis is highest in red light (with a second peak in blue), which chlorophyll absorbs most efficiently.

1.s: Pigment without oxygen is:
1.x: Carotenes are pure hydrocarbons (C40H56) with no oxygen; xanthophylls are their oxygenated forms, and chlorophyll and phycobilins contain oxygen.

1.s: To which group of plants does the Banyan Tree belong?
1.x: The banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is a flowering, fruit-bearing plant – an angiosperm.

1.s: In plants, active cell division occurs in the following parts
1.x: Active division takes place in meristems; among the options the root tip (root apical meristem, the classic onion-root-tip mitosis slide) is the expected answer.

1.s:
Identify the correct pair(s) from the given pairs with respect to minerals and their function and choose the correct option.

I. Zinc - For insulin production

II. Phosphorus - Development of strong bones and teeth

III. Fluoride - Makes enamel of teeth hard and prevents dental caries
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: Zinc is needed for insulin synthesis and storage, phosphorus (with calcium) builds bones and teeth, and fluoride hardens tooth enamel and prevents caries – all three pairs are correct. Off-topic (nutrition), moved.

1.s: Which one of the following are richest sources of calcium:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Ragi (finger millet), amaranth and milk are among the richest common sources of calcium. Off-topic (nutrition), moved to book 5.

1.s: Which of the following nuts has the highest potassium content per equal weight?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Per 100 g, almonds (about 730 mg) have more potassium than peanuts (~705 mg), cashews (~660 mg) and walnuts (~440 mg).

1.s: What is the primary function of calcium in plants?
1.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Calcium (as calcium pectate of the middle lamella) is needed for cell wall formation and development. ATP synthesis and electron transport rely on phosphorus, iron and magnesium.

1.s: Which of the following is matched INCORRECTLY?
o: Protein - Needed for the building of antibodies and immune system cells.
Vitamin A - Helps regulate the immune system and protect the body by keeping skin and tissues in the mouth.
Vitamin C - helps the body build healthy skin.
Zinc - Helps to activate immune cells and properly regulate their function.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
1.x: Protein builds antibodies; vitamin A keeps skin and the linings of mouth, gut and airways healthy; vitamin C helps build skin (collagen) and antibodies; the printed key marks the zinc statement as the mismatch.

1.s: Out of the below, which food is richer in Zinc?
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x:
Printed key: chicken (animal foods give well-absorbed zinc). Strictly, per 100 g almonds and dry legumes hold about as much or more zinc than chicken (general knowledge, not checked).
Animal foods such as chicken give well-absorbed zinc, so the printed key is chicken; green leafy vegetables are poor zinc sources. (Off-topic: nutrition.)

1.s: Which of the following is a rich source of iodine?
1.x: Seaweed is rich in iodine; linseed gives alpha-linolenic acid and wheat germ oil gives vitamin E.

1.s: Which of the following diseases is caused due to deficiency of Ascorbic acid?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, and its deficiency causes scurvy. Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency, glossitis is B2 and beri-beri B1.

1.s: Golden rice is a genetically modified plant where the incorporated gene is meant for the biosynthesis of
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: Golden rice carries genes for beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A. It is not designed for vitamin B, C or omega-3.

1.s:
Vitamins are a group of substances that are needed for normal cell function, growth, and development. Match the following Vitamins with their chemical name.
Vitamin:
I. Vitamin B2
II. Vitamin B6
III. Vitamin B3
IV. Vitamin B7
Chemical name:
a. Niacin
b. Riboflavin
c. Biotin
d. Pyridoxine
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: B2 is riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine, B3 niacin and B7 biotin, so I-b, II-d, III-a, IV-c.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins decomposes easily on heating?
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Vitamin C is the vitamin most easily destroyed by heat (and by oxidation). The B group is partly heat-stable, and A and E are fat-soluble and more stable in cooking.

1.s: In which of the following is Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) available?
1.x: Thiamine (B1) is in the bran and husk layer of rice, which is why polished rice causes beri-beri. Carrot and beetroot are not B1 sources, and sunflower seeds are not the answer here.

1.s: Select the correct match of the vitamins with the deficiency diseases.
o: Vitamin B1 (thiamine) - pernicious anaemia (RBC deficient in haemoglobin)
Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) - cheilosis (fissuring at corners of mouth and lips), digestive disorders and burning sensation of the skin
Vitamin E - increased blood clotting time
Vitamin K - increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness
1.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes cheilosis and digestive disorders. Pernicious anaemia is B12, vitamin E is not about clotting, and vitamin K deficiency prolongs clotting time.

1.s:
Match the columns.
Vitamin:
A. Vitamin A
B. Vitamin D
C. Vitamin C
D. Vitamin K
Deficiency disease:
1. Scurvy
2. Night blindness
3. Excessive bleeding due to injury
4. Rickets
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Vitamin A – night blindness, D – rickets, C – scurvy, K – excessive bleeding, so A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.

1.s:
Match the following diseases in Column I with their causes in Column II
Column I:
1. Malaria
2. Goiter
3. Rickets
4. Night Blindness
Column II:
a. Vitamin D deficiency
b. Vitamin A deficiency
c. Iodine deficiency
d. Mosquito bite
1.src: General Studies & Mental Ability (paper title page missing i
1.x: Malaria spreads by mosquito bite, goitre is iodine deficiency, rickets vitamin D deficiency and night blindness vitamin A deficiency, so 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b.

1.s: Find the incorrect match.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Biotin is vitamin B7, not B12 (B12 is cobalamin), so that pair is incorrect. Thiamin B1, riboflavin B2 and niacin B3 are correct.

1.s: Which of the following can be associated with Vitamin C?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Hydrochloric, sulphuric and acetic acids are not vitamins.

1.s: What is another name for Vitamin B12?
1.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
1.x: Vitamin B12 is cobalamin. Riboflavin is B2, pyridoxine B6 and pantothenic acid B5.

1.s: Which Vitamin is known as anti pernicious Anemia factor?
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the anti-pernicious-anaemia factor; its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

1.s: Scurvy is a deficiency of
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C).

1.s: The richest source of Vitamin 'C' is:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C; chilli is the richest among vegetables.

1.s: Which of the following disease may be caused due to deficiency of Vitamin C?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

1.s: Which Vitamin has Cobalt?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt. B1, B2 and B6 have no metal.

1.s: Out of the below, which is richer in Vitamin D?
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x:
Printed key: none. Strictly, none of the four contains vitamin D naturally; orange counts only as fortified orange juice (WebMD, Foods High in Vitamin D).
None of these is a natural vitamin D source (fresh fruits and seeds have almost none); only orange juice, which is often fortified, supplies some, so orange is the best of the four.

1.s: What is the other name of Vitamin B2?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Vitamin B2 is riboflavin. Pyridoxine is B6, thiamine B1 and cyanocobalamin B12.

1.s: Out of the following which food contains the highest Vitamin A content per equal weight?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Cod-liver oil has by far the most vitamin A (retinol) per gram – many times more than carrots or pumpkin (beta-carotene) or egg.

1.s: Vitamin 'A' deficiency cause which type of disease?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia, leading to vision loss and blindness. Rickets is vitamin D, and clotting problems are vitamin K.

1.s: Which of the following is a major source of Vitamin C?
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
1.x: Gooseberry (amla) is the richest common source of vitamin C.

1.s: A deficiency of vitamin B3 can result in a condition called:
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Niacin (B3) deficiency causes pellagra. Scurvy is C, rickets D and beri-beri B1.

1.s: Which of the following factors will NOT generally cause heart disease?
o: Deficiency of Vitamin A in diet
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: High blood pressure, high blood glucose and raised lipids are risk factors for heart disease; vitamin A deficiency is not, so it is the answer.

1.s: Damaged and dry skin, wounds healing slowly and easy bruising are some of the problems which can arise because of the deficiency of which vitamin?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: Vitamin C is needed for collagen, so its deficiency gives dry damaged skin, slow wound healing and easy bruising (scurvy). Vitamins D, A and B12 cause bone, eye and anaemia problems.

1.s: The disease 'Osteomalacia' which causes softening of bones is caused by a deficiency of which nutrient in the human diet?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: Osteomalacia, softening of adult bones, is caused by vitamin D deficiency. Carbohydrate, iodine and vitamin C are wrong.

1.s: When fruits are cut and exposed to air, Vitamin C is lost by
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a strong reducing agent, so on cut fruit exposed to air it is lost by oxidation.

1.s:
Which of the following statement is/are not true about vitamins?

a. The term vitamin was coined by C Funk

b. Vitamins are organic compounds.

c. Vitamin K plays important role in clotting of blood.

d. Vitamin A, D, E and K are water soluble vitamins.
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Statements a (Funk coined 'vitamine'), b (vitamins are organic) and c (K for clotting) are true; d is false because A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only d.

1.s: Thiamine is known to people as
1.x: Thiamine is vitamin B1, whose deficiency causes beri-beri.

1.s: Macrolytic anaemia is due to the deficiency of:
1.x: Macrocytic (megaloblastic) anaemia results from deficiency of folic acid (folacin) or B12. Biotin, niacin and pantothenic acid do not cause it.

1.s: Cyanocobalamin is a synthetic form of vitamin ______.
1.x: Cyanocobalamin is the synthetic, cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12.

1.s: Which vitamin is required for formation of bones and teeth?
1.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
1.x: Vitamin D controls calcium and bone metabolism, so it is needed for bones and teeth; its deficiency causes rickets.

1.s: Which vitamin is known as the "sunshine vitamin" because the body can produce it when exposed to sunlight?
1.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
1.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin on exposure to sunlight, so it is called the sunshine vitamin. Vitamins A, C and K are not made this way.

1.s: The deficiency of which vitamin in human diet causes sore throat with swelling and redness of the mouth, cheilosis, stomatitis, glossitis and dermatitis?
1.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes sore throat, cheilosis, stomatitis, glossitis and dermatitis. Ascorbic acid is C (scurvy), retinol A and cyanocobalamin B12.

1.s: Vitamin related with production of antibodies is:
1.x: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is needed for amino-acid metabolism and antibody production. B12 is for RBCs, B1 for carbohydrate metabolism and B2 for energy release.

1.s: Which of the following is/are a source of Vitamin K?
1.x:
APPSC 2004 key: nuts, eggs, liver. Strictly, green leafy vegetables are the richest source of vitamin K (PMF General Science Part 3 p.14), but option (c) adds tomatoes and carrots, which are poor sources.
Nuts, eggs and animal liver supply vitamin K, which is the exam key. Green leafy vegetables are the best-known source, but tomatoes and carrots are poor, so option (c) is not a clean answer; shark-liver oil gives vitamins A and D.

1.s: Which of the following are water-soluble vitamins ?
1.x: B-group vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so every pair with A or D is wrong.

1.s: Golden Rice is a rich source of :
1.x: Golden Rice is genetically engineered to make beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, in the grain.

1.s: Scurvy is a disease caused by the deficiency of :
1.x: Scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing) is caused by lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). B2 deficiency causes cheilosis and vitamin A deficiency night blindness.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins contains cobalt?
1.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the only vitamin with a metal – cobalt – at its centre. K, B6 and B2 contain no cobalt.

1.s: A person will suffer from beri-beri, rickets and scurvy if he is not taking adequate amounts of :
1.x: Beri-beri = lack of B1 (thiamine), rickets = lack of D, scurvy = lack of C, so B1, D and C. The other sets include vitamins (A, E, K, B6) linked to other diseases.

1.s: Which of the following vitamin helps in blood clotting in humans?
1.x: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors (prothrombin), so it helps blood clot. A is for vision, D for bones.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins is essential for normal vision?
1.x: Retinol (vitamin A) forms the visual pigment rhodopsin, so it is essential for normal vision. Folic acid, riboflavin and niacin are B vitamins with other roles.

1.s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
1.x: Tocopherol (vitamin E) deficiency causes sterility and muscle weakness; beri-beri is due to thiamine (B1). The other three pairs are correct.

1.s:
Consider the following pairs : Vitamin Deficiency disease
1. Vitamin C : Scurvy
2. Vitamin D : Rickets
3. Vitamin E : Night blindness Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
1.x: Vitamin C – scurvy and vitamin D – rickets are correct; night blindness is due to vitamin A, not E (E deficiency causes sterility/muscle weakness).

1.s: Which one of the following vitamins is helpful in keeping a dream in memory for a longer duration?
1.x: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) was found (University of Adelaide study, 2018) to improve people's ability to recall their dreams. Vitamins A, D and C have no such link.

1.s: Which one of the following compounds is not a vitamin?
1.x: Thyroxine is a hormone of the thyroid gland, not a vitamin. Niacin (B3), riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6) are B vitamins.

1.s: Golden rice is a richer source of –
1.x: Golden Rice carries genes for beta-carotene (provitamin A), so it is a richer source of vitamin A; it was developed against vitamin A deficiency.

1.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: Milk contains none of the B vitamins
Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency leads to the dry and
One of the symptoms of scurvy is pain in the joints
Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency can lead to heart
1.x: Milk is a good source of riboflavin (B2) and B12, so 'milk contains none of the B vitamins' is wrong. Vitamin A lack causes dry eyes, scurvy causes joint pain and thiamine lack (wet beri-beri) can cause heart failure.

1.s: For which desirable character the transgenic crop ‘Golden Rice’ is produced ?
1.x: Golden Rice was engineered to produce beta-carotene (provitamin A) in the endosperm; it is not for amino acids, insulin or starch quality.

1.s: Which one of the following is an important source of vitamin E?
1.x: Wheat-germ oil is the richest natural source of vitamin E (tocopherol). Palm, coconut and mustard oil contain much less.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins is mainly responsible for blood coagulation in human being?
1.x: Vitamin K is needed for the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors; E, A and C have no direct role in coagulation.

1.s: Which of the following vitamin is effective in blood clotting?
1.x: Vitamin K (the 'koagulation' vitamin) makes blood clot; lack of it prolongs clotting time.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins contain cobalt –
1.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; B1, B2 and B6 contain no metal.

1.s: Deficiency of which vitamin can cause night blindness?
1.x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; B1 causes beri-beri, C scurvy and E sterility.

1.s: Which of the following has the highest content of Vitamin C ?
1.x: Guava has about 200+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, about four times an orange; carrot and mango are known for vitamin A.

1.s: Which one of the following vitamins is formed in skin in the presence of sunlight?
1.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin when UV-B in sunlight acts on 7-dehydrocholesterol – the 'sunshine vitamin'.

1.s: The main source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
1.x: Vitamin C comes mainly from fresh raw fruits (amla, guava, citrus); it is destroyed by heat and milk, ghee and pulses are poor in it.

1.s: Cyanocobalamin is –
1.x: Cyanocobalamin is the cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12. Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, B2 riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins are fat soluble?
1.x: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so A and D is the pair; C and B12 are water-soluble.

1.s: Riboflavin deficiency causes which of the following diseases?
1.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes cheilosis (cracks at the lip corners). Pellagra is niacin (B3), scurvy vitamin C, beri-beri thiamine (B1).

1.s:
Assertion (A) : If somebody stops taking green vegetables hewill suffer from night blindness.
Reason (R) : He will suffer from vitamin A deficiency.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct
1.x:
UPPSC key: both true, R explains A. Strictly, stopping green vegetables causes night blindness only if no other vitamin A source (milk, liver, carrots, fruits) is eaten.
Green leafy vegetables are a main source of beta-carotene (vitamin A); without vitamin A one suffers night blindness, so the key is both true and R explains A.

1.s: The Deficiency of Vitamin D causes the disease :
1.x: Lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children (osteomalacia in adults). Beri-beri is B1, pellagra B3; osteoporosis is mainly age and calcium related.

1.s: The nutritional deficiency condition that needs to be given top priority for remedial action in India today is :
1.x: Vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia), the main preventable cause of child blindness, was India's priority deficiency, hence the vitamin A prophylaxis programme. Scurvy, rickets and pellagra are much rarer.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins is known as ergocalciferol?
1.x: Ergocalciferol is vitamin D2 (plant/fungal form); cholecalciferol is D3; B12 is cobalamin and B6 pyridoxine.

1.s:
Consider the statements :
Assertion (A) : Vitamin B12 remains stored in liver for about 3-5 years.
Reason (R) : Vitamin B12 is water-soluble.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Both statements are true: B12 is water-soluble, yet the liver stores it for 3–5 years. Being water-soluble does not explain storage (water-soluble vitamins are usually excreted), so R is not the explanation.

1.s: If a person only takes milk, egg and bread in diet, so he may suffer from the disease :
1.x: Milk, egg and bread contain almost no vitamin C, so such a diet leads to scurvy. They give vitamin D, A and calories, so rickets, night blindness and marasmus are not the result.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins does not get stored in the body?
1.x: Vitamin C is water-soluble and not stored; excess is passed in urine. A, D and E are fat-soluble and stored in the liver and fat.

1.s: Which of the following facts is NOT correct about vitamins?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesized by intestinal
Some vitamins are stored in body
1.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so that statement is false. Gut bacteria make K and B12, vitamin D acts as a hormone, and A, D, B12 are stored.

1.s: The richest source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
1.x: Orange (citrus) is rich in vitamin C; potato has a little, sugarcane and sugar beet almost none.

1.s: Golden rice is rich in –
1.x: Golden Rice is rich in beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A.

1.s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes following disease :
1.x: Polishing removes the bran that holds thiamine (B1), so a polished-rice diet causes beri-beri. Rickets (D), anaemia (iron) and goitre (iodine) are not linked.

1.s: The vitamin available from sun rays is –
1.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin under sunlight (UV-B), so it is called the sunshine vitamin.

1.s: Which of the following vitamins is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons?
1.x: Warfarin-type anticoagulants block vitamin K; giving vitamin K restores the clotting factors, so it is the antidote. A, D and E have no such role.

1.s: Milk is a poor source of :
1.x: Milk is poor in vitamin C (and iron) but rich in calcium, protein and lactose (carbohydrate).

1.s: Which of the following is synthesized by intestinal bacteria?
1.x:
Book answer: (a) & (c) – B12 and K both. Strictly, vitamin K2 from gut bacteria is the part humans actually absorb; colonic B12 is largely not absorbed (it is made beyond the ileum).
Gut bacteria synthesise both vitamin B12 and vitamin K, and the book answer gives B12 (with K). Vitamins C and A are not made by bacteria in the gut.

1.s: Which vitamin is soluble in water?
1.x:
Printed key: (b) Vitamin B; the book answer reads '(b) & (c)'. Strictly both vitamin B and vitamin C are water-soluble (NextGen Rocket Biology vitamin table).
Vitamin B (the B-complex) is water-soluble; vitamin C is also water-soluble, while A and D are fat-soluble. The printed key gives B.

1.s: The vitamin which is found in citrus fruits and is necessary for maintaining healthy skin is –
1.x: Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits, is needed for collagen and so for healthy skin and gums.

1.s: Which one of the following is not formed in our body?
1.x: Vitamin A must come from food (retinol, or carotene converted in the gut/liver); proteins, enzymes and hormones are all synthesised in the body.

1.s: The common name of the chemical compound 'Cholecalciferol' is :
1.x: Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3, the form made in the skin under sunlight.

1.s: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :
1.x: Vitamin K is needed for clotting factors; lack of it prolongs clotting.

1.s: Which of the following is the richest source of vitamin A?
1.x: Among the fruits given, mango is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A); papaya is close, while apple and guava are poor in it.

1.s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes the following disease
1.x: Polished rice has lost its thiamine-rich bran, so it causes beri-beri; goitre is iodine and night blindness vitamin A deficiency.

1.s: Some vitamins are fat soluble while others are water soluble. Which of the following are water soluble :
o: Vitamin A, D, E and K
1.x: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so any set with A, D or K is wrong.

1.s: Among the following vegetables, the maximum Vitamin C is found in :
1.x: Green chilli has about 100+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, the most among these vegetables; pumpkin, pea and radish have far less.

1.s: Which of the following vitamin's deficiency causes disease of slow blood coagulation ?
1.x: Vitamin K deficiency increases clotting time (slow coagulation). C, D and E deficiencies cause scurvy, rickets and sterility.

1.s: Which one of the following contains more vitamin A content ?
1.x: Carrot is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A) of these vegetables, ahead of spinach; cabbage and cauliflower have little.

1.s: In countries where polished rice is the mean cereal in their diet, people suffer from –
1.x: Polished rice lacks thiamine (B1), so people eating it as the main cereal suffer beri-beri. Pellagra is a maize-diet (niacin) disease.

1.s: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
1.x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C (~600 mg/100 g), far above orange; apple and carrot are poor.

1.s: The chemical name of Vitamin C is –
1.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; thiamine is B1, while citric and tartaric acids are fruit acids, not vitamins.

1.s: Which one of the following is useful in the treatment of scurvy disease?
1.x: Aonla (amla, Indian gooseberry) is the richest vitamin C source, so it treats scurvy; mango and papaya have less and ber is moderate.

1.s: Which of the following statement regarding vitamin is not correct?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesised by intestinal microbes.
Some vitamins are stored in body.
vitamin K is a water soluble vitamin.
1.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so that statement is wrong. Gut microbes make K and B12, vitamin D acts as a hormone, and fat-soluble vitamins and B12 are stored.

1.s: Vitamin C is also known as …………
1.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; tartaric (tamarind), malic (apple) and acetic (vinegar) acids are not vitamins.

1.s: The deficiency of which nutrient causes night blindness?
1.x: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness; K, C and protein deficiency do not.

1.s: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia. Animals cannot synthesise vitamin B12. Humans must obtain all their vitamin B12 from their diet. The complexing metal ion in Vitamin B12 is
1.x: Vitamin B12 has a cobalt ion (Co3+) at the centre of its corrin ring. Mg2+ is in chlorophyll, Fe2+ in haemoglobin.

1.s: Which of the following is a fat soluble vitamin that plays a role in blood clotting, bone metabolism and regulating blood calcium levels?
1.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble and needed for clotting and bone metabolism (osteocalcin). C and B are water-soluble; A is for vision.

1.s: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin ……
1.x: Pernicious anaemia is due to vitamin B12 deficiency (lack of intrinsic factor). B2, B6 and B1 are not the cause.

1.s: Deficiency of ………… causes rickets disease.
1.x: Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency; C causes scurvy, A night blindness, B beri-beri/pellagra.

1.s: Which mineral element is present in Vitamin B-12?
1.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; iron is in haemoglobin, magnesium in chlorophyll.

1.s: Which one of the following is not a natural source of Vitamin A ?
1.x:
Book key: milk. Strictly, whole milk does contain preformed vitamin A (retinol) in its fat, while mango, papaya and carrot give only provitamin A (beta-carotene).
Mango, papaya and carrot are rich carotene (provitamin A) sources; milk has comparatively little vitamin A, so the book key is milk.

1.s: The best source of Vitamin C is :
1.x: Gooseberry (amla) is the best source of vitamin C; apple and mango have less and milk almost none.

1.s: Vitamin 'C' help in absorption of which of following elements?
1.x: Vitamin C reduces dietary iron to the ferrous form and increases its absorption; it does not mainly aid calcium, iodine or sodium.

1.s: The source of vitamin D is –
1.x: Sun rays let the skin make vitamin D; lemon and orange give vitamin C and cashew nut has almost no vitamin D.

1.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and other as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Human body synthesizes all the Vitamins required by it.
Reason (R) : Vitamins are essential for proper growth of the body.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
1.x: A is false: the body makes only a few vitamins (D, some K, niacin), so most must come from food. R is true – vitamins are essential for growth.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Vitamins are invigorating elements, whose small amount is required for good health.
Reason (R) : Vitamins helps to keep the body healthy by killing harmful bacteria.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but R is not the correct
1.x: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts for health, so A is true. They do not kill bacteria (that is antibodies or antibiotics), so R is false.

1.s: In human body, vitamin A is stored in –
1.x: Vitamin A is largely stored in the liver in the human body. Its chemical name is retinol whose deficiency causes night blindness.

1.s: In human body, Vitamin A is stored in –
1.x: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.

1.s: The vitamin which can be synthesized under the skin in the presence of the uv light of sun is?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Vitamin D (the sunshine vitamin) is made in the skin under the sun's UV light.

1.s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x:
Official key: Winter. Strictly no authority gives a season-dependent vitamin A requirement for humans ('No seasonal dependence'); deficiency peaks in the hot pre-harvest season (NERC/Cambridge study on India).
The APPSC 2017 key is winter (option A in the paper as printed in Vijeta previous papers). No nutrition authority gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement: ICMR-NIN RDAs depend on age and life stage only.

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vitamin B2 deficiency may cause cheilosis, glossitis, dermatosis and digestive disorders.
Vitamin B5 deficiency may cause paraesthesia and burning sensation.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: pellagra comes from lack of B3 (niacin); B5 deficiency causes tingling and burning feet. The B2 symptoms are right.
1.tq: Recall the deficiency disease of each B vitamin.
n: Vitamin B2 deficiency causes cheilosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes glossitis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes dermatosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 deficiency causes digestive disorders. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B3 deficiency causes pellagra. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B5 deficiency causes paraesthesia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B5 deficiency causes a burning sensation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Vitamin B5 deficiency causes pellagra**", so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Pellagra** is caused by deficiency of **B3 (niacin)**.
**B5 (pantothenic acid)** deficiency causes **paraesthesia** and **burning sensation**.
**B2** deficiency causes **cheilosis**, **glossitis**, **dermatosis** and **digestive disorders** — correct.
xa: **B6 (pyridoxine)** deficiency: **anaemia**, **skin problems**, **muscular twisting**.
**B1 (thiamine)** deficiency: **beri-beri**, **neuritis**.
All B vitamins are **water**-soluble.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about vitamin K?
o: It is involved in blood clotting
It is needed to make clotting factors
1.x: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors, so its deficiency increases clotting time and causes bleeding; it does not shorten it.
n: Vitamin K functions in blood clotting. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin K deficiency increases clotting time. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Amla is a richest source of Vitamin C.
Orange is another source of Vitamin C.
Carrot is the richest source of Vitamin A among the given fruits.
Chilli is a rich source of Vitamin C among vegetables.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: among fruits, mango is the richest vitamin A source; carrot is a vegetable source. The vitamin C sources are right.
1.tq: Check whether the item belongs to the category asked.
n: Amla is the richest source of vitamin C. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Chilli is the richest source of vitamin C among vegetables. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Orange is another source of vitamin C. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Carrot is a source of vitamin A. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Mango is the richest source of vitamin A among the given fruits. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Mango is the richest source of vitamins A, B, and C. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Carrot** is the richest source of Vitamin A among the given fruits", so option **(3)** is the answer.
Among the **given fruits**, **mango** is the richest source of **vitamin A**; carrot is a source but not the richest fruit.
**Amla** is the **richest source** of vitamin C, **chilli** the richest among **vegetables**, and **orange** is a source — all correct.
xa: **Mango** is the **richest source** of **vitamins A, B and C**.
**Vitamin E** source: **wheat germ oil**.
**James Lind:** **citrus fruits** **cured scurvy**.

1.s: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Wheat germ oil – Source of vitamin E
Carbohydrate + fat + protein – Maximum energy-yielding diet group
ATP → ADP – Biotransformation providing maximum energy
1.x: Rice is noted for the highest percentage of carbohydrate; vitamin E comes from wheat germ oil.
n: Wheat germ oil is a source of vitamin E. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Rice has the highest percentage of carbohydrate. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
Carbohydrate, fat, and protein together form the maximum energy-yielding diet group. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
The biotransformation of ATP to ADP provides maximum energy. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 10-14]
xa: **Fats** give the **maximum energy per gram**.
**Egg** has the **highest biological value** among proteins.
**Holstein–Friesian** is the world's **highest-production dairy** breed.

1.s:
Match List I (Vitamin) with List II (Chemical name):
List I
a. Vitamin B5
b. Vitamin B6
c. Vitamin B7
d. Vitamin K
List II
i. Pyridoxine
ii. Naphthoquinone
iii. Pantothenic acid
iv. Biotin
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
1.x: B5 = pantothenic acid; B6 = pyridoxine; B7 = biotin (vitamin H – not B12); K = naphthoquinone (phylloquinone).

1.s:
Match List I (Vitamin) with List II (Deficiency disease / sign):
List I
a. Vitamin B3
b. Vitamin B5
c. Vitamin B6
d. Vitamin E
List II
i. Anaemia, dermatitis
ii. Sterility, muscle weakness
iii. Pellagra
iv. Burning feet, paraesthesia
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
1.x: B3 (niacin) – pellagra (not B5); B5 (pantothenic acid) – burning feet; B6 (pyridoxine) – anaemia, dermatitis; E (tocopherol) – sterility, muscle weakness.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about vitamins:
1. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.
2. Vitamin K and vitamin B12 are made by bacteria in the gut.
3. Vitamin A is stored in the kidney.
4. Cyanocobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, contains cobalt.
How many of the above statements are correct?
1.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct (A, D, E, K fat-soluble; B-group and C water-soluble; gut bacteria make K with B12; cyanocobalamin is the synthetic cobalt-containing B12). Statement 3 is wrong: vitamin A is stored in the liver.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about the discovery of vitamins:
1. Casimir Funk coined the term 'vitamine' in 1912.
2. McCollum, who identified vitamin A with Davis, also identified vitamin D (1922) as the anti-rickets factor in cod-liver oil.
3. Umetaro Suzuki's rice-bran extract (aberic acid) was vitamin C.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Suzuki's rice-bran extract (aberic acid) was B1; the citrus–scurvy link is James Lind's.

1.s:
Match List I (Scientist) with List II (Contribution):
List I
a. Casimir Funk
b. F.G. Hopkins
c. James Lind
d. McCollum and Davis
List II
i. Vitamin A (1913)
ii. Citrus fruits cure scurvy
iii. Coined 'vitamine'
iv. 'Accessory food factors'
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
1.x: Funk coined 'vitamine' (1912); Hopkins – accessory food factors; Lind – citrus cures scurvy; McCollum and Davis – vitamin A (1913).

1.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

1.s: In periodic table helium is placed at
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

1.s: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

1.s: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
1.x: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

1.s: Which of the following is a noble gas?
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
1.x: Helium is a noble (inert) gas of Group 18; hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are reactive.

1.s: It would be less safe to fill a gas balloon with the following gas:
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
1.x: Hydrogen is lighter than air but highly inflammable, so it is the least safe gas for a balloon; helium is inert and safe.

1.s: Saponification is the reaction between
o: A fat and a strong acid
A fat and a strong base
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Saponification is the hydrolysis of a fat (or oil) with a strong base such as NaOH, giving soap and glycerol. An acid-base reaction is neutralisation.

1.s: Which of the following forces is responsible for all the nucleons to be concentrated in the nucleus?
1.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
1.x: The strong nuclear force, short-range and far stronger than electrostatic repulsion, binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Off-subject (physics).

1.s: The most malleable metal is
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.

1.s: When an iron nail gets rusted, its weight?
o: Increase or decrease depends on temperature and pressure
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide; the iron combines with oxygen and water, so the weight increases. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which metal has the maximum use as pure metal?
1.x: Aluminium is keyed: light, abundant and corrosion-resistant, it is used very widely in nearly pure form (foils, cans, sheets, conductors); silver is scarce and iron is used mostly as steel. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is an inorganic lubricant?
1.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
1.x: Graphite is an inorganic layered form of carbon used as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: A soap molecule has two ends, one of which is an ionic end and the other is a carbonic chain end. Which part of the soap molecule interacts with oily dirt to enable cleansing?
o: The end that is closer to the oil molecule
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The hydrocarbon (carbon-chain) tail dissolves in oil and grips the dirt, while the ionic end faces water, forming micelles. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Why alum is used in the process of purifying drinking water?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Alum (potash alum) supplies Al3+ ions that neutralise the charge on suspended clay particles so they coagulate and settle. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s:
Match the following from table A to Table B - Use of Salts
Table A:
I. Sodium Carbonate
II. Sodium Benzoate
III. Calcium Carbonate
IV. Calcium Phosphate
Table B:
1. Extraction of Metals
2. As Washing Soda, Manufacturing of Glass
3. As a Fertilizers
4. As a Food preservative for Pickles
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Sodium carbonate is washing soda used in glass-making, sodium benzoate is a food preservative, calcium carbonate is a flux in metal extraction and calcium phosphate is a fertiliser. Moved.

1.s: Out of the below, what is the example of a chemical reaction?
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide), so it is a chemical change; freezing, glowing of a lamp filament and dissolving salt are physical changes. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which type of chemical process is tarnishing of silver?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: Tarnishing of silver (black silver sulphide from H2S in air) is a form of corrosion. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which reaction demonstrate the chemical property of alcohols as reducing agent?
o: Reaction with sodium to release hydrogen
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes or ketones, so they act as reducing agents (they are themselves oxidised); esterification, reaction with sodium and dehydration are not redox reactions of this kind. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which gas is evolved when an acid reacts with a metal?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: A metal reacting with an acid gives a salt and hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2). Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s: Formation of Carbon dioxide gas from Carbon and Oxygen is a/an?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Burning carbon in oxygen to CO2 gives out heat – an exothermic (combination) reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which one of the following is pure water?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x: Rain water is the purest natural water (natural distillation); well, river and sea water carry dissolved salts.

1.s: Which of the following substances is invariably formed, whenever an acid combines with a base?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: An acid and a base always react to form a salt (and water). Off-topic science PYQ, moved.

1.s: What happens to the weight of Iron when it rusts?
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Rust is iron combined with oxygen and water (hydrated iron oxide), so the rusted iron weighs more. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Out of the following, which would not indicate occurence of a chemical reaction?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: Evaporation is only a change of state (physical change); gas evolution, colour change and heat absorption can signal a chemical reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: An 'aerosol' is a fine dispersion of
o: Tiny droplets of liquid in the air
Chalk and sand particles in water
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: An aerosol is a fine dispersion of liquid droplets (or solid particles) in air/gas, e.g. fog, mist, sprays. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: When you are facing the periodic table, on which side of the table the non-metals are present?
o: On the right-hand side of the periodic table
In the middle column of the periodic table
On the left-hand side of the periodic table
In the bottom most row of the periodic table
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: In the modern periodic table metals lie on the left, metalloids along a zigzag line and non-metals on the right-hand side.

1.s: Which of the following chemicals is generally used for purifying muddy water?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
1.x: Alum (potash alum) coagulates suspended clay so it settles, purifying muddy water. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is a mixture?
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Sea water is a mixture of water and many dissolved salts in no fixed ratio; table salt, sugar and lime are compounds. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is used in glass industry?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
1.x: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) is a main raw material of glass. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is antidote for cyanide poisoning
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Sodium thiosulphate is an antidote for cyanide poisoning (it turns cyanide into less toxic thiocyanate). Off-topic (chemistry/medicine), moved.

1.s: Percentage of sodium chloride present in normal saline is
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Normal saline is 0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride, isotonic with blood. Off-topic (science), moved; the question had no printed key.

1.s: Fill in the blanks: Gunpowder, also known as black powder is made of Sulphur (S), Charcoal (C), and ______.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Gunpowder (black powder) is sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate (saltpetre). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Out of the following, which compound has highest solubility in Water?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Glucose dissolves about 90 g per 100 mL water at 25°C, far more than table salt (~36 g), ammonium chloride (~38 g) or alum (~14 g). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: If Limestone (Calcium Carbonate) kept in a test tube is heated with a spirit lamp and a burning match stick is kept near the mouth of the test tube
o: The stick will glow with higher brightness
The stick will glow with same brightness
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Heating limestone (CaCO3) decomposes it into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide; CO2 does not support burning, so the flame goes out. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

1.s: What happens when calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water?
o: Calcium Hypochlorite is produced and a large amount of heat is released
Calcium Oxyacid is produced and a precipitate is formed that settle down in the test-tube
Calcium Carbonate is produced and hydrogen gas is released
Calcium Hydroxide is produced and a large amount of heat is released
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: Calcium oxide (quicklime) reacts vigorously with water to form calcium hydroxide (slaked lime), releasing a lot of heat. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

1.s: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as _____ to give saturated hydrocarbons.
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons uses a nickel (or Pd/Pt) catalyst. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: The strike plate of a match box is made up of
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
1.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

1.s: The strike plate of a match box is is made up of
1.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

1.s: Which of the following is used in titration
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: A burette delivers measured volumes of titrant in a titration; a pipette transfers a fixed volume.

1.s: The thermite process is used to weld railway tracks; it involves a reaction between
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The thermite reaction is between iron oxide and aluminium; aluminium reduces the oxide and the molten iron produced welds rail joints.

1.s: What happens when a dry litmus paper is exposed to Anhydrous hydrochloric acid vapor?
o: Colour changes from blue to red
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: Dry HCl gas does not ionise without water, so dry litmus paper shows no colour change.

1.s: The Elements of Group IA are called:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Group IA (Group 1) elements – lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium – are the alkali metals. Off-topic (chemistry).

1.s: Galvanization is a method of protecting iron from corrosion by coating the iron with a thin layer of which of the following element?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Galvanisation coats iron with a thin layer of zinc. Off-topic (chemistry).

1.s: In Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides on treatment with-metal in dry ethereal (free from moisture) solution give higher alkanes.
1.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
1.x: The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether to give higher alkanes. Off-topic (chemistry).

1.s: Which metal coating is used in Galvanization process to protect Steel and Iron from rusting?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Galvanisation coats steel and iron with zinc to stop rusting. Off-topic (chemistry).

1.s: Which of the following metal is the best conductor of electricity?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, ahead of copper and aluminium. Off-topic (physics).

1.s: Which of the following is a toxic material found in automotive batteries?
1.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
1.x: Lead in lead-acid automotive batteries is the toxic material. Off-topic (pollution / chemistry).

1.s: A solution reacts with crushed-egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Hydrochloric acid reacts with egg shells (calcium carbonate) to release CO2, which turns lime water milky. Off-topic (chemistry).
