1.s: Which of the following metals can be easily cut with a knife?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Potassium, a soft alkali metal, can be cut with a knife; lead, aluminium and selenium cannot be cut easily. Off-topic (chemistry).

1.s: The head of a matchstick is generally made of
1.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
1.x:
Most books and keys: phosphorus. Strictly, a safety-match head is mainly potassium chlorate with antimony trisulphide; the red phosphorus is on the striking strip (only old 'strike-anywhere' heads carried phosphorus sesquisulphide) (general knowledge, not checked).
Exam keys answer phosphorus for the match head; see the dispute for what a safety-match head is actually made of.

1.s: In vulcanization of natural rubber, the following is used?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Vulcanisation heats rubber with sulphur to make it strong and elastic (Goodyear, 1839).

1.s: Which of the following substances can be used as an acid-base indicator?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: Turmeric turns reddish-brown in bases and back to yellow in acids, so it works as a natural acid-base indicator; tamarind, sugar and salt do not change colour.

1.s: Which of the following can be prepared using Methyl Alcohol?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
1.x: Perspex is PMMA, whose monomer methyl methacrylate is made by esterifying methacrylic acid with methanol (methyl alcohol); neoprene comes from chloroprene and Bakelite from phenol and formaldehyde.

1.s: How many moles of Oxygen are required for combustion of one mole of Propane?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, so one mole of propane needs 5 moles of oxygen.

1.s: A spectral line is emitted when an electron
o: jumps from lower orbit to higher orbit
jumps from higher orbit to lower orbit
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: A spectral (emission) line is emitted when an electron jumps from a higher orbit (energy level) to a lower one, giving out a photon. Jumping up absorbs energy.

1.s: Which element is common to all acids?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: All acids contain hydrogen, which they release as H+ ions in water.

1.s: What is the meaning of pH?
o: To measure the pressure of liquid
To measure the density of a solution
To measure the pressure of a blood
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: pH = 'potential of hydrogen' (power of hydrogen), a measure of hydrogen-ion concentration.

1.s: Which of the following is not necessary for combustion to occur?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and the ignition temperature (the fire triangle); water is not needed.

1.s: An organic compound must contain?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: An organic compound must contain carbon.

1.s: Ammonia is a compound of
o: Nitrogen and sodium hydroxide APPSC PYQS "
1.x: Ammonia (NH3) = one nitrogen + three hydrogen atoms.

1.s: Which of the following elements does not contain neutrons?
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
1.x: Protium (ordinary hydrogen, 1H1) has no neutron; oxygen and nitrogen nuclei contain neutrons.

1.s: Approximately how many different chemical elements exist on the Earth?
1.x: 118 elements are known and about 94 occur naturally on Earth, so 'about 100' is nearest; 200–300 elements do not exist.

1.s: Which of the following is the most common element in the Universe?
1.x: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Universe (about 3/4 of matter); oxygen leads in the Earth's crust.

1.s: An iron nail dipped into Copper sulphate solution turns into the following colour?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate; the nail gets a reddish-brown copper coating (solution turns pale green).

1.s: Into which colour will the yellow silver bromide turn when exposed to sunlight?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
1.x: Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to grey silver metal (photolytic reaction).

1.s: The catalyst used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils is
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Finely divided nickel is the catalyst for hydrogenating vegetable oils into vanaspati.

1.s: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron fillings?
o: Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced
Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced
Iron salt and water are produced
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Iron reacts with dilute HCl to give iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas.

1.s: Which of the following has 1 as its atomic number?
1.x: Hydrogen has one proton, so its atomic number is 1; ammonia is a compound.

1.s: The bright colour of fire crackers containing Magnesium is due to?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: The dazzling white light of magnesium in crackers comes from burning, i.e. oxidation of magnesium to MgO. Reduction and 'explosion of metal' are wrong; 'redox' is too general.

1.s: Which of the following happens during the electro refining of copper?
o: Pure copper from anode deposits at the cathode
Pure copper from anode deposits in the electrolytic solution
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the anode
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the cathode
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: In electrolytic refining the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the solution deposits at the cathode. Copper does not pass directly from anode to cathode, and nothing deposits at the anode.

1.s: The colour given by excess Lithium in Lithium Chloride solid is:
1.x: Excess lithium makes LiCl crystals pink. The colour comes from F-centres, electrons trapped at anion vacancies (NCERT Class XII, Solid State). Excess potassium in KCl gives violet, and excess sodium in NaCl gives yellow.

1.s:
Identify the correct pairs of organic chemical reactions and their mechanisms.

1. Gatterman-Koch Reaction - The formation of cyclopropanes from alkenes using methylene carbene.

2. Friedel-Crafts Acylation Reaction - The conversion of carboxylic acids into esters using acids and alcohols.

3. Etard Reaction - The direct oxidation of an aromatic or heterocyclic bound methyl group with an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.

4. Stephen Reaction - The conversion of nitriles to aldehydes in the presence of hydrochloric acid, using tin chloride.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
1.x: Etard reaction oxidises an aromatic methyl group to an aldehyde with chromyl chloride, and Stephen reaction reduces nitriles to aldehydes with SnCl2/HCl, so 3 and 4 are right. Gattermann-Koch is formylation of benzene (CO + HCl), not cyclopropanation, and Friedel-Crafts acylation adds an acyl group to an aromatic ring, not esterification.

1.s: Which of the elements is used as fungicide?
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
1.x: Sulphur (wettable or dusting sulphur, lime-sulphur) is a widely used fungicide; calcium, phosphorus and carbon are not used as fungicides.

1.s: The reaction of sodium Hydroxide with Hydrochloric acid leading to formation of salt and water is a?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is a neutralisation, a double displacement reaction (ions exchange partners).

1.s: In the Haber's process, X moles of nitrogen react with Y moles of hydrogen to form Z moles of ammonia. What are the values of X, Y and Z?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Haber process: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, so X = 1, Y = 3, Z = 2.

1.s: Which of the below is a physical change?
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change: no new substance forms and evaporation recovers the salt. Burning wax or wood and curdling milk make new substances, so they are chemical changes.

1.s: Name the non-metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature.
1.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
1.x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature. Mercury is liquid but a metal; silicon and lithium are solids.

1.s: Which of the following is a non-metal that remains liquid at room temperature?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
1.x: Bromine is the non-metal that is liquid at room temperature. Helium and chlorine are gases.

1.s: Which of the following can be used as Tear Gas?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Tear gas CN is alpha- (omega-) chloroacetophenone, i.e. 2-chloro-1-phenylethanone. Plain acetophenone is not a lachrymator.

1.s: Which of the following noble gases is NOT present in the air?
1.x:
Most books: all noble gases except radon occur in air. Strictly, radon is present in trace amounts near the ground (decay of radium in soil).
Argon, neon and helium are constituents of air. Radon is radioactive and short-lived, so it is taken as the noble gas not present in air. (Off-topic: chemistry.)

1.s: Name the homologous series with an -OH functional group.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Alcohols form the homologous series with the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group. Hydroxide is the OH- ion of bases, not a functional group.

1.s: When an alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 170°C, it undergoes dehydration. What is the major product formed?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Heating an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 at about 170°C removes water (dehydration) and gives an alkene, e.g. ethanol → ethene.

1.s: Dry ice is used for packing Covid-19 vaccines for transportation. What is dry ice?
1.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
1.x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide (sublimes at -78.5°C), used to keep vaccines cold.

1.s: What is the process of extracting metals from their ores called?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Smelting is extracting a metal from its ore by reduction at high temperature in the fused state; refining purifies the metal and mining removes the ore.

1.s: Identify the functional group responsible for the characteristic smell of fruits.
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Esters (RCOOR') give the characteristic fruity smell of fruits and are used in perfumes and flavouring; aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are not the answer.

1.s:
C2H5OH + alkaline KMnO4 + Heat → X
X + C2H5OH (acid) → Y
What are the products X and Y, respectively?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Alkaline KMnO4 oxidises ethanol to ethanoic (acetic) acid (X); the acid reacts with ethanol in acid medium to form an ester, ethyl acetate (Y).

1.s: Which of the following reactions does not occur in a blast furnace during the extraction of iron?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: In the blast furnace, coke burns to CO, limestone decomposes to CaO + CO2 and CO reduces Fe2O3 to iron; decomposition of FeSO4 does not occur there.

1.s: Which of the following is incorrect about acids?
o: Aqueous solutions of acids are electrolytes
Acids can change the colour of certain acid-base indicators
Acids do not react with active metals
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Acids do react with active metals (e.g. zinc, iron) to give hydrogen gas, so that statement is incorrect. Aqueous acids conduct electricity, taste sour and change indicator colours.

1.s: What is the colour of litmus solution when it is neither acidic or basic?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Litmus solution is purple in a neutral solution; it turns red in acid and blue in base.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about chemicals and their popular names?

A. The chemical name of 'Alum' is Potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate.

B. The chemical name of 'Aspirin' is Acetyl salicylic acid.

C. The chemical name of 'Chalk' is Hypochlorus acid.
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Alum (potash alum) is potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate, KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, and aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, so A and B are correct; chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO3), not hypochlorous acid.

1.s: Tobacco plant contains the following alkaloid?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Nicotine is the alkaloid of the tobacco plant; morphine comes from the opium poppy and reserpine from Rauwolfia, and resin is not an alkaloid. (Off-topic: general science.)

1.s: What happens to the colour of litmus paper when you put a drop of acid on it?
o: Blue Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to blue
Green Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to green
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

1.s: What is the role of Barium Nitrate (Ba(NO3)2) in fireworks and fountains?
o: It acts as a fuel for combustion.
It produces a blue color in the flames.
It is an oxidizer that produces a green color in the flames.
It produces a red color in the flames.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
1.x: Barium nitrate is an oxidiser in fireworks that gives a green flame; strontium gives red and copper blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

1.s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?

a. Melamine polymer is used in the manufacture of unbreakable crockery

b. Enzymes are biocatalysts

c. DNA fingerprinting is used for identification of criminals

d. Tincture of iodine is an antiseptic
1.x: All four are correct: melamine makes unbreakable crockery, enzymes are biocatalysts, DNA fingerprinting identifies criminals and tincture of iodine is an antiseptic.

1.s:
Identify the compound described below:
- It is present in crude oil and gasoline.
- It can cause Leukemia, DNA Strand Breaks, Chromosomal damage, Cancer, and harmful effects on bone marrow.
- It is known to be carcinogenic to humans.
1.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
1.x: Benzene, found in crude oil and petrol, is a known human carcinogen causing leukaemia and bone-marrow and chromosome damage.

1.s: Which property of ammonia explains why it turns red litmus into blue?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Ammonia turns red litmus blue because it is a weak base (NH3 + H2O gives NH4+ and OH-); being a reducing agent, soluble or covalent does not explain the colour change. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: Atoms are composed of
1.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
1.x: An atom is a small nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: The smallest ketone has ____ carbon atom/s.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The smallest ketone is acetone (propanone, CH3COCH3) with 3 carbon atoms, since the C=O must be bonded to two carbons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: Which of the following could be the molecular formula of an alcohol?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: C2H6O is ethanol (C2H5OH), a saturated alcohol CnH2n+2O; C2H4O is acetaldehyde, C3H6O acetone or propanal, and CH2O formaldehyde. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: What substance is added to water to dissolve shellac and create a water-based varnish?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Shellac dissolves in water when borax (an alkali) is added, giving a water-based shellac varnish; spirit (alcohol) gives the ordinary spirit varnish, not a water-based one.

1.s: Which group of elements generally form coloured compounds?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Transition (d-block) metals form coloured compounds because of d-d electron transitions in partly filled d orbitals; alkali-metal and non-metal compounds are mostly colourless.

1.s: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing cast iron cookware from rusting?
1.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
1.x: Seasoning (coating with fat or oil and heating) forms a protective layer that keeps cast iron from rusting; soap and abrasives strip that layer.

1.s: Which of the following is an emulsion?
1.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
1.x: Butter is an emulsion (water droplets dispersed in fat); vinegar, sugar solution and honey are solutions.

1.s: Sulphur is used in vulcanization. This process is mainly associated with
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Vulcanisation is heating natural rubber with sulphur, which cross-links it and makes it harder, stronger and more elastic and wear-resistant (tyres, footwear). Steel, glass and cement making do not use it.

1.s: The ignition temperatures of four substances P, Q, R and S are 95°C, 98°C, 105°C and 108°C, respectively. Which substance/s will catch fire when they are exposed to a temperature of 100°C?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: A substance catches fire only when its temperature reaches its ignition temperature. At 100°C, P (95°C) and Q (98°C) are above their ignition temperatures and burn; R (105°C) and S (108°C) stay below theirs, so only P and Q catch fire.

1.s: Goiter is characterized by:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

1.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

1.s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
1.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
1.x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

1.s: Which of the following is a diuretic
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

1.s: Which is the most abundant element by mass in human body?
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
1.x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s: Commonly used absorbable suture material is
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

1.s:
When it comes to the digestive system, which statements are true?

I. The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and insulin.

II. The small intestine is where most nutrient absorption occurs.

III. The gallbladder stores bile produced by the liver.
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
1.x: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes and insulin, most absorption is in the small intestine, and the gall bladder stores bile – all three true. Off-topic, moved.

1.s: What is the resting rate heart for a normal person?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: A normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (American Heart Association); about 72 is the textbook average.

1.s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Deposition of calcium and other minerals that turns cartilage into bone is ossification. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: The production of tears when dust particles hit the human eye; is an example of which of the following?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Tears flushing dust from the eye are part of the body's first-line (innate) defence – immunity; they contain lysozyme. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: What is a characteristic feature of a first-degree burn?
o: Minor epithelial damage, presence of redness
Partial thickness burn and scalds, may be painful
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: A first-degree (superficial) burn damages only the epidermis, with redness and pain; partial-thickness is second degree and full-thickness/necrosis third degree. Off-topic (first aid), moved.

1.s: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer. Off-topic (biology/health), moved.

1.s: In case of heat stroke, the body temperature?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
1.x: In heat stroke the body's cooling fails and core temperature rises quickly (above 40°C). Off-topic (health), moved.

1.s: The weight of a brain of a normal human adult is about
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3-1.4 kg, i.e. about 3 pounds.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the excretory system in humans?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: Nissl's granules are in the cell body of a neuron (nervous system), not the excretory system; the glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron. Off-topic (human biology), moved to book 5.

1.s: An abnormal cavity containing pus is called as
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: An abscess is a localised cavity filled with pus; a hematoma is collected blood, a cyst a fluid sac, a tumour a mass of cells. Off-topic (health), moved to book 5.

1.s: Tooth enamel is made up of which of the following?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Tooth enamel, the hardest substance in the body, is made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite). Off-topic (biology), moved to book 5.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct with respect to definition of anatomy and physiology?

I. Physiology focuses on the physical arrangement of parts in the body.

II. Anatomy studies the inner functioning of cells, tissues and organs.
o: Only statement I is not correct
Only statement II is not correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Both statements I and II are correct
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
1.x: Both statements swap the definitions: anatomy studies the structure (physical arrangement) of body parts, physiology studies how cells, tissues and organs function – so both are not correct.

1.s: Which of the following is a procedure used to save an abscessed tooth in which the pulp chamber is cleaned out, disinfected, and filled with a permanent filling?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: Root canal therapy cleans, disinfects and fills the pulp chamber of an abscessed tooth; gum grafts and gingivoplasty treat gums. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human female reproductive system?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the MALE reproductive system; fimbriae (of the fallopian tube), cervix and endometrium (uterine lining) are female parts.

1.s: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the male reproductive system; ovary, uterus and fallopian tube are female organs. (Biology; moved.)

1.s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I - Table-II

A. Lipase -
1. Breaks lactose

B. Amylase -
2. Breaks fat

C. Trypsin -
3. Breaks starch

D. Lactase -
4. Breaks Protein
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

1.s: In humans, Milk Teeth generally fall off at what age?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
1.x:
Most books and keys: between 6 and 8 years. Strictly: shedding starts at about 6 and is complete by about 12 (incisors 6-8, canines and molars 9-12) (AAP healthychildren.org; Wikipedia 'Deciduous teeth').
Milk (deciduous) teeth begin to fall at about 6 years, and the incisors are shed by about 6-8 years, so most keys give 6-8. Shedding of canines and molars continues until about 12, which is why 10-12 is only the end of the process.

1.s: The classical example for closed wound is
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: A contusion (bruise) is the classic closed wound, with the skin unbroken; lacerated, penetrating and incised wounds are open.

1.s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x:
Key: ecbolic (a drug class, usually injected), since suppositories and enemas are by definition rectal preparations. Strictly, one ecbolic (misoprostol) can also be given rectally (Wikipedia, Uterotonic).
Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

1.s: In a healthy adult, what is the approximate percentage of white blood cells in total blood volume?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: White blood cells (with platelets) form well under 1% of blood volume (the thin buffy coat), so 'one percent' is the nearest figure.

1.s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the pharynx to the stomach; the duodenum and jejunum are parts of the small intestine and the pylorus is the stomach's outlet.

1.s: Which cranial nerve in humans is the largest and has both, sensory and motor functions?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
1.x: The trigeminal (5th) nerve is the largest cranial nerve and has both sensory and motor fibres.

1.s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
1.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
1.x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

1.s: Which of the following is not a solid form of medicine
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Syrup is a liquid dosage form; tablets, capsules and boluses are solid.

1.s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

1.s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the alveoli, across their thin walls into the capillaries. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: The longest fibre on the cell body of a neuron is called:
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: The axon is the single long fibre that carries impulses away from the neuron's cell body; dendrites are short and branched.

1.s: What is the immediate first aid that can be administered to a victim of burns?
o: Wetting the burnt part in cold water
Removing stuck cloth on the burnt part
1.x: Immediate first aid for a burn is to cool the part in cool or cold running water. Stuck cloth must not be pulled off, butter or ointment should not be applied, and water should not be poured with force.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human respiratory system?
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
1.x: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves (nervous system); trachea, bronchi and larynx are parts of the respiratory tract.

1.s: Number of Incisors, Canines, Premolars and Molars in humans is respectively
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
1.x: Human adult dentition (32 teeth) = 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, 12 molars (dental formula 2123 per half-jaw).

1.s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
1.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
1.x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

1.s: Which of the following are parts of the excretory system?
1.x: Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron in the kidney; colon, rectum, appendix and ileum belong to the digestive system.

1.s: Which of following is NOT a part of the human excretory system?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Alveoli are air sacs of the lungs (respiratory system); nephrons, Bowman's capsule and ureters belong to the excretory system.

1.s: Which of the following is a voluntary muscle that you can control consciously?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
1.x: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary; smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary.

1.s: The capsules that contain medicines taken by us are normally made of
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: Medicine capsule shells are normally made of gelatin (from collagen), which dissolves in the stomach.

1.s: Which of the following is used to control Mange
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Sulphur ointment (sulphur, often with lime) is the classic remedy for mange, a mite infestation of animal skin.

1.s: What is range of the pH value of the human blood?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, pH 7.35-7.45.

1.s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

1.s: Hyper Natrimia is excess presence in blood of?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x: Hypernatraemia means too much sodium in the blood (natrium = sodium).

1.s: Which of the following are the main constituents of Dettol, a commonly used antiseptic in homes?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Dettol's main constituents are chloroxylenol and alpha-terpineol (with pine oil); it has no iodine.

1.s: The gap between two neurons is called a
1.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
1.x: The junction between two neurons is a synapse; dendrites and axons are parts of a neuron, and an impulse is the signal it carries.

1.s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

1.s: For the examination of skin scrapings which of the following is required
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Skin scrapings are cleared with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH mount) so that fungal elements and mites can be seen. Heparin is an anticoagulant, and HCl and dichromate are not used for this.

1.s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

1.s: What is the primary function of the human digestive system?
o: To break down food and absorb nutrients
To provide Oxygen to the body
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
1.x: The digestive system breaks food down into simple absorbable molecules and absorbs the nutrients; temperature control, blood circulation and oxygen supply belong to other systems.

1.s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
1.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
1.x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

1.s: Which blood vessels have the smallest diameter?
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
1.x: Capillaries are the narrowest blood vessels (about 5–10 micrometres), one cell thick. (Off-topic: biology.)

1.s: Which of the elements found in human body has functional requirement?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x:
Official key: Arsenic. Strictly: arsenic's essentiality in humans is unproven (it is a toxic element); none of the options is an established essential element.
Among the options only arsenic is treated as a (possibly essential) ultra-trace element with a functional role; titanium, caesium and aluminium have no known requirement.

1.s: Which part of the eye gives it a distinctive colour?
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: The iris is the pigmented muscular ring around the pupil and gives the eye its colour. The cornea is transparent, the pupil is an opening and the retina lies at the back.

1.s: The human saliva has an average pH of____.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men
1.x: Human saliva is slightly acidic to near-neutral, pH about 6.2-7.6 with an average of about 6.7 (salivary amylase works best near this); 5.5 is the enamel-dissolving critical pH, and 7.8 and 9.1 are too alkaline.

1.s: Which enzyme helps in the digestion of fats in the gut of humans?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
1.x: Lipase digests fats (pancreas, intestine); amylase digests starch, lactase lactose, and helicase unwinds DNA.

1.s: Which of the following enzymes found in saliva is responsible for digestion?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
1.x: Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin), which digests starch; pepsin acts in the stomach, trypsin from the pancreas.

1.s: Of the following bacteria, ____ causes pneumonia.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
1.x: Haemophilus influenzae causes pneumonia (as does Streptococcus pneumoniae); S. thermophilus and Lactobacillus are curd/yoghurt bacteria and E. coli is a gut bacterium.

1.s: Which enzyme is found in tears?
1.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Tears contain lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme that breaks down bacterial cell walls. Ptyalin is in saliva, pepsin in the stomach, and sebum is skin oil. (Off-topic: human physiology.)

1.s: Which body fluid plays an important role in transporting digested fats in humans?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Digested fats are absorbed into the lacteals (lymph vessels) of the villi and carried by lymph, not directly by blood.

1.s: What is the main function of the kidneys in the human body?
o: To filter waste products and excess of water from the blood
Help the body to absorb nutrients from the food
To pump the blood throughout the body
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The kidneys filter waste products and excess water from the blood and form urine; digestion, absorption and pumping are other organs' jobs.

1.s: Which of the following is the longest part of the alimentary canal?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: The small intestine (about 6-7 m) is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

1.s: Fat in the food eaten by us is completely digested in?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Fats are completely digested in the small intestine by bile (emulsification) and pancreatic and intestinal lipase.

1.s: The digestive fluid bile is produced by which organ of the human body?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Bile is produced by the liver and only stored in the gall bladder.

1.s: The duodenum is a part of the
1.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
1.x: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine.

1.s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
1.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
1.x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

1.s: If all the alveoli in a human lung are separated and spread, they will occupy the size of a typical?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: The roughly 300-500 million alveoli have a surface area of about 70 m² – about a tennis court.

1.s: Identify the gland, which release HCl in human digestive tract.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Gastric glands of the stomach wall release HCl.

1.s: Leucocytes are also known as ____ as they are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Leucocytes are white blood cells – colourless because they lack haemoglobin.

1.s: The ____ in the iris that make pigment are called melanocytes.
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Melanocytes are the cells that make melanin pigment in the iris.

1.s: Red blood cells are formed in
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Red blood cells are formed in the red bone marrow.

1.s: Which drugs are used to lower the body temperature?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Antipyretics (e.g. paracetamol) lower raised body temperature; analgesics relieve pain.

1.s: Which of the following carries Carbon dioxide rich blood from heart to lungs in humans?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated (CO2-rich) blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood.

1.s: The largest artery in the human body
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The aorta, leaving the left ventricle, is the largest artery of the body.

1.s: A blood vessel which pumps the blood from the heart to the entire body
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the body (the aorta from the left ventricle); veins return it and capillaries exchange materials.

1.s:
Match the given organs with the arteries which supply blood to them.
Organ:

I. Kidney

II. Liver

III. Heart
Arteries which supply blood:

a. Renal arteries

b. Hepatic arteries

c. Coronary arteries
1.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
1.x: Renal arteries supply the kidney, hepatic arteries the liver and coronary arteries the heart: I-a, II-b, III-c.

1.s: Alimentary canal runs from mouth to?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, rectum, anus).

1.s: Which of the following systems of the human body is responsible when a person sneezes?
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Sneezing is a reflex of the respiratory system: irritants in the nasal lining trigger a forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth. It is controlled by the medulla, but the system involved is respiratory, not immune (printed key: immune system).

1.s: Anorexia and bulimia are types of ____ disorders.
1.x: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa are eating disorders (self-starvation; binge eating with purging).

1.s: A cardiac portion, a fundic region and a pyloric portion are parts of which of the following organs/body parts?
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: The stomach has a cardiac part (near the oesophagus), a fundic region and a pyloric part (opening into the duodenum).

1.s:
In the context of human physiology, match the blood components with their respective names.
Blood components:
1. Erythrocytes
2. Leukocytes
3. Thrombocytes
Names:
A. White blood cells
B. Platelets
C. Red blood cells
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
1.x: Erythrocytes are red blood cells, leukocytes white blood cells and thrombocytes platelets: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B.

1.s: Anorexia nervosa is a ....disorder.
1.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
1.x: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder (self-starvation from fear of weight gain).

1.s: Which of the following is NOT a region of the human stomach?
1.x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).

1.s: All of the following are tests for brain, spinal cord, and nerve disorders, EXCEPT ______
1.x: Bronchoscopy examines the airways and lungs, not the nervous system. Myelography (spinal cord imaging), electroencephalography (EEG – brain's electrical activity) and echoencephalography (ultrasound of the brain) are nervous-system tests.

1.s: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions – heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing, salivation, swallowing and vomiting. The cerebrum handles voluntary action and thought, the cerebellum balance, and the diencephalon (hypothalamus) temperature, hunger and thirst.

1.s: Which part of the brain controls the process of Breathing?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Breathing is controlled by the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata (with the pons). The cerebellum controls balance, the hypothalamus temperature/hunger, the cerebrum voluntary actions.

1.s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
1.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
1.x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)

1.s: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled as ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’. ‘A’ contains plain water, ‘B’ contains solution of an alkali, ‘C’ contains solution of an acid, and ‘D’ contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
1.x: Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.

1.s: Which of the following metals is the most reactive metal?
1.x: In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.

1.s: Zinc is used to protect iron form corrosion because zinc is
o: a good conductor of heat and electricity.
1.x: Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).

1.s: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions (H+)?
1.x: Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.

1.s: Which of the following acids is present in ant bites?
1.x: Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.

1.s: Chemical used for preserving the serum is
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Merthiolate (thiomersal), a mercury compound, is the classic preservative for serum and vaccines. Heparin and oxalates are anticoagulants that stop blood clotting, and formaldehyde is a tissue fixative, not a serum preservative.

1.s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve performance by athletes
A chemical used for the development of food-packaging materials
A special type of alloy steel
1.x: Bisphenol A is an industrial chemical used to make polycarbonate plastics and epoxy food-can linings, i.e. food-packaging materials. It is not a medical test, a doping test or an alloy steel.

1.s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve
A chemical used for the development of food-
A special type of alloy steel
1.x: BPA is used in polycarbonate plastics and food-can linings, so it is a chemical used for food-packaging materials. The other options (medical test, doping test, alloy steel) do not describe it.

1.s: Gold is dissolved in –
o: Mixture of Sulfuric and Nitric Acid
Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)
1.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)); it is added as option 5.
Gold dissolves only in aqua regia, a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acids. No single acid dissolves it, and a sulphuric–nitric mixture does not either, so the printed key (c) is wrong.

1.s: Mustard gas is used –
o: As a source of mustard oil
1.x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) is a blistering chemical-warfare agent. It has nothing to do with mustard oil, fuels or deodorants.

1.s: During the first world war, which of the following gas was utilised as the chemical weapon?
1.x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) was used as a chemical weapon in World War I, along with chlorine and phosgene. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide were not the typical battlefield agents.

1.s: What is the chemical name of the deadly poison ‘cyanide’?
1.x: Prussic acid is hydrocyanic acid (HCN), whose salts are the cyanides. Sulphuric, hydrochloric and nitric acids are mineral acids, not cyanide.

1.s: Stinging hair of nettle leaves inject the following acid causing burning pain?
1.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
1.x: Nettle leaf hairs inject formic (methanoic) acid, causing the burning pain. Acetic acid is vinegar, phosphoric acid is in colas and sulphuric acid is a mineral acid.

1.s: Which of the following materials in normally used in a breath analyzer test to ascertain whether a person is drunk or not?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: In the breath analyser, orange acidified potassium dichromate turns green as it oxidises the alcohol in the breath. Permanganate, silica gel and baking soda are not used.

1.s: What is the dominant acid in a 'bee sting'?
1.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
1.x: School books and Rocket list formic (methanoic) acid as the acid of a bee sting. Lactic, malic and citric acids come from muscles, apples and lemons.

1.s: Hard coffee stains on clothes can be properly removed by?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is an oxidising agent that breaks down the coloured compounds of tea and coffee stains on white cloth. Water and lemon juice only lighten fresh stains, and petrol removes grease, not coffee.

1.s: Cola type soft drinks contain:
1.x: Cola drinks are acidified with phosphoric acid, which gives their tangy taste. Formic, lactic and acetic acids are not cola ingredients.

1.s:
Consider the following statements
1.
Assertion (A): Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid.
2.
Reason (R): Formic acid is an organic acid.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Formic acid is stronger than acetic acid because acetic acid's CH3 group pushes electrons and weakens it. Formic acid is also an organic acid, but that does not explain why it is stronger, so both are true and R is not the explanation.

1.s: When ants bite, they inject:
1.x: Ants inject formic acid (from Latin formica, ant), which causes the burning sensation. Acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are not involved.

1.s: Chlorination is a process used for water purification. The disinfecting action of chlorine is mainly due to:
o: The formation of hydrochloric acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hypochlorous acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of nascent oxygen when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hydrogen when chlorine is added to water
1.x: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and HCl; HOCl is the strong disinfectant that kills microbes. HCl does not disinfect, and 'nascent oxygen' is an older textbook explanation.

1.s: Which is the most reactive metal ?
1.x: Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Fe), so it is the most reactive of the four metals.

1.s: Soft drinks such as colas contain significant quantities of :
1.x: Colas contain significant caffeine, a stimulant alkaloid. Nicotine is in tobacco, tannin in tea and renin is a kidney enzyme.

1.s: Which acid is mainly find in lemons?
1.x: Lemon contains citric acid. Acetic acid is in vinegar, ascorbic acid is vitamin C and nitric acid is a mineral acid.

1.s: When ants bite, they inject :
1.x: Ants inject formic acid, a simple carboxylic acid. Glacial acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are wrong.

1.s: What is the dominant chemical present in vinegar?
1.x: Vinegar is dilute acetic acid, whose IUPAC name is ethanoic acid. Formic acid is the ant-sting acid and malic acid is in apples.

1.s: Food cans are coated with tin but not with zinc because
o: zinc has a higher melting point than tin.
zinc is more reactive than tin.
tin is more reactive than zinc.
1.x: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it would react with food acids and form harmful salts; tin is less reactive and safe. Cost and melting point are not the reason.

1.s: Citric acid is present in free form in
1.x: Lemon contains citric acid in free form. Tamarind mainly has tartaric acid, apple malic acid and milk lactic acid.

1.s: Sodawater obtained by passing carbon dioxide in water is
1.x: CO2 dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, so soda water is acidic. It is not basic, and it is neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.

1.s: Which one of the following acids is used in the manufacturing of baking powder ?
1.x: Baking powder is baking soda plus a mild edible acid, tartaric acid. Oxalic acid is toxic, and lactic and benzoic acids are not its acid component.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Caffeine, a constituent of tea and coffee is a diuretic.
2. Citric acid is used in soft drinks.
3. Ascorbic acid is essential for the formation of bones and teeth.
4. Citric acid is a good substitution for ascorbic acid in our nutrition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Caffeine is a diuretic, citric acid is used in soft drinks and ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is needed for collagen in bones and teeth. Citric acid cannot replace ascorbic acid, so 1, 2 and 3 only.

1.s: Which one of the following does not contain COOH group?
1.x: Ascorbic acid is acidic because of an enol hydroxyl in a lactone ring and has no carboxyl group. Citric, lactic and tartaric acids are all carboxylic (–COOH) acids.

1.s: If a red litmus paper turns to blue when few drops of a liquid are poured on the paper, then the liquid is a/an?
o: Could be an acid or base
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red, and a neutral salt changes neither.

1.s:
Arrange the following solutions in the ascending order of pH value?

A. Lemon juice

B. Human blood

C. Milk of Magnesia

D. Sodium Hydroxide Solution
1.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
1.x: Lemon juice (~2) < human blood (~7.4) < milk of magnesia (~10) < NaOH solution (~14).

1.s: If Hydrochloric Acid is added to few pieces of Zinc in a beaker and a burning match stick is brought near the mouth of the beaker, then?
o: The gas inside the beaker catches fire
The match stick burns at original intensity
The match stick burns at reduced intensity
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: Zinc and dilute HCl give hydrogen gas, which catches fire with a pop when a burning match is brought near. The match is not put out, because hydrogen is combustible.

1.s: During winter in cold regions, bottles of vinegar are found to freeze. This happens because
o: Pure ethanoic acid has a high melting point
Pure ethanoic acid has a low melting point
Pure ethanoic acid is a strong acid
Pure ethanoic acid is a weak acid
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Pure (glacial) ethanoic acid melts at about 290 K (16.6 °C), well above winter temperatures in cold regions, so it freezes; that is why it is called glacial acetic acid (NCERT). A low melting point would keep it liquid, so the printed key 'low melting point' is wrong.

1.s: A man posing as goldsmith went to a house and informed the lady of the house that he will polish her gold ornaments for a nominal amount. He dipped the ornaments given by her in a solution called royal water and they sparkled like new. After he left, the lady weighed the ornaments and found that they reduced in weight. What could be the solution?
1.x: 'Royal water' is aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), the only common reagent that dissolves gold, so the ornaments lost weight. Oil of vitriol is H2SO4 and aqua fortis is HNO3; neither dissolves gold alone.

1.s: Bleaching action of chlorine is due to which reaction?
1.x: Chlorine bleaches by oxidation: with water it forms hypochlorous acid, which gives nascent oxygen that oxidises the coloured matter.

1.s: ‘Oil of Vitriol’ is the common name of which of the following?
1.x: Oil of vitriol is concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4), the 'king of chemicals'. Blue vitriol is copper sulphate.

1.s: Which one of the following is an organic acid?
1.x: Acetic acid (vinegar) is an organic (carboxylic) acid. HCl, HNO3 and H2SO4 are mineral acids.

1.s:
Which among the following is an incorrect pair? (Natural Source – Acid)

I. Vinegar – Acetic acid

II. Curd – Lactic acid

III. Tamarind – Citric acid
Codes
1.x: Tamarind's acid is tartaric acid, not citric acid, so only pair III is incorrect. Vinegar is acetic acid and curd is lactic acid.

1.s: Which one of the following was the first mineral acid discovered?
1.x:
Most keys (Testbook, NDA 2020): sulphuric acid. Some solution books: nitric acid. The history is not settled; the alchemists knew both early.
Sulphuric acid ('oil of vitriol') is usually given as the first mineral acid, known to the medieval alchemists. Some keys give nitric acid instead.

1.s: Which metal is generally used for coating of brass utensils to prevent copper contamination?
1.x: Brass and copper vessels are tinned ('kalai') so that food acids do not dissolve copper. Zinc and lead would themselves be toxic, and aluminium is not used for this.

1.s: Which acid is used in photography–
1.x: Oxalic acid (as ferrous oxalate developer and in toning) is the acid used in photography. Formic acid is in ant stings, citric acid in lemons and acetic acid in vinegar.

1.s: Which gas is used in the purification of drinking water?
1.x: Chlorine is used to disinfect drinking water; it forms hypochlorous acid, which kills germs.

1.s: Which one of the following organic acids is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana?
1.x: Tartaric acid is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana. Citric acid is in citrus fruits, and lactic acid in curd.

1.s:
Which of the following pairs is/are NOT correctly matched ? (Acid) (Acid found in)
1. Lactic acid – Curd
2. Tartaric acid – Grapes
3. Acetic acid – Potato
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
1.x: Lactic acid–curd and tartaric acid–grapes are correct. Acetic acid is in vinegar, not potato, so only pair 3 is wrong.

1.s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I
List-II (Natural Source) (Acid)
A. Vinegar i. Methanoic acid
B. Tamarind ii. Lactic acid
C. Sour milk (curd) iii. Acetic acid
D. Nettle sting iv. Tartaric acid
Codes :
1.x: Vinegar–acetic (iii), tamarind–tartaric (iv), sour milk–lactic (ii), nettle sting–methanoic/formic (i).

1.s: The alkaloid caffeine is present in :
1.x: Caffeine is the alkaloid of both tea and coffee (also colas). Lemon water has citric acid, not caffeine.

1.s: Which one among the following metals is more reactive than hydrogen?
1.x: Tin lies above hydrogen in the reactivity series (Pb, Sn above H), so it displaces hydrogen from dilute acids. Mercury, copper and silver lie below hydrogen.

1.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of electron releasing tendency of metals?
1.x: Zinc is above copper and copper above silver in the reactivity series, so electron-releasing tendency is Zn > Cu > Ag.

1.s: Which of the following acid found in Apple?
1.x: Apples contain malic acid; nitric and sulphuric acids are strong mineral acids not found in fruits, and formic acid is found in ant stings.

1.s: ……… is the primary acid present in ripe bananas.
1.x: Ripe bananas contain malic acid as their main organic acid; formic acid occurs in ants and the others are mineral acids.

1.s: Acid turns blue litmus red and base turns red litmus blue. A student tested a liquid with a red litmus paper which remained red with no change. This shows that the liquid
o: is neither an acid nor a base.
must be pure water or acid.
1.x: Red litmus turns blue only with a base. No change means the liquid is not a base, but it could be an acid or neutral, so only option 1 must be true.

1.s: When we cut an onion, the synthase enzyme converts the amino acid sulfoxide of the onion into which acid?
1.x: Cutting an onion releases alliinase (synthase), which converts amino acid sulfoxides into sulfenic acids; these form the tear-inducing compound.

1.s: The pH of milk is 6. When it turns sour, the pH
1.x: Souring forms lactic acid by bacterial fermentation, so the acidity rises and the pH falls below 6.

1.s: Which one of the following elements will not react with dilute HCl to produce H2?
1.x: Mercury lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Al, Mg and Fe lie above hydrogen and release H2.

1.s: Which one among the following is the correct order of reactivity of the elements?
1.x: In the reactivity series the order is Na > Mg > Zn > Cu, with sodium most reactive and copper least.

1.s:
Match the following From Table A to Table B - Uses of Acids as Food
Table A:
I. Butyric Acid
II. Maleic Acid
III. Stearic Acid
IV. Oxalic Acid
Table B:
1. Fats
2. Wood Sorrel
3. Apples
4. Rancid Butter
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Butyric acid is in rancid butter, malic acid ('Maleic' in the stem) in apples, stearic acid in fats and oxalic acid in wood sorrel. Moved.

1.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
1.x: Orange - citric, tomato - oxalic, tamarind - tartaric: I-c, II-a, III-b.

1.s:
Match the following items with the acids found in them.
Natural source:

I. Orange

II. Tamarind

III. Tomato
Acid:

a. Tartaric Acid

b. Oxalic Acid

c. Citric Acid
1.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
1.x: Orange - citric (c), tamarind - tartaric (a), tomato - oxalic (b): I-c, II-a, III-b (options 2 and 4 are printed identically).

1.s:
Which of the following acids are present in lemons?
(i) Citric acid
(ii) Tartaric acid
(iii) Malic acid
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Lemons contain mainly citric acid with some malic acid; tartaric acid is the acid of tamarind and grapes.

1.s:
Match
List-I (Acid) with
List-II (Source):

a. Citric acid
b. Oxalic acid
c. Lactic acid
d. Acetic acid

1. Tomato
2. Lemon

1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Citric - lemon, oxalic - tomato, lactic - curd, acetic - vinegar: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3.

1.s: Which of the following is a traditional remedy to alleviate the pain from sting of Nettle plant?
o: Rubbing the area with leaf of dock plant
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: The traditional remedy for a nettle sting (formic/methanoic acid) is rubbing the area with a dock leaf, which is basic (NCERT Class 7).

1.s: Tamarind contains:
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Tamarind contains tartaric acid.

1.s: Ripe avocado mainly contains ____ acid
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Avocado fat is mostly the monounsaturated fatty acid oleic acid (as in olive oil).

1.s: Which of the following is the main acid present in Spinach?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
1.x: Spinach is rich in oxalic acid.

1.s:
Match List I (Acid) with List II (Found in / use):
List I
a. Formic acid
b. Tartaric acid
c. Phosphoric acid
d. Oxalic acid
List II
i. Tomato, spinach; removes ink stains
ii. Cola soft drinks
iii. Tamarind, grapes; baking powder
iv. Ant bite, bee sting
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
1.x: Formic acid – ant bite, bee sting, nettle hairs (limited antibacterial preservative); tartaric acid – tamarind, grapes, baking powder; phosphoric acid – colas; oxalic acid – tomato, spinach, ink stains.

1.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid.
Reason (R): Both formic acid and acetic acid are organic acids.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: formic acid is stronger because the CH3 group of acetic acid pushes electrons and weakens it; 'being organic' does not explain the strength.

1.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Food cans are tin-plated rather than zinc-coated.
Reason (R): Zinc is more reactive than tin and would react with food acids to form toxic salts.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A (notes: food cans are tin-plated, not zinc-coated, because zinc is more reactive).

1.s: What is the scientific name of Ashwagandha?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

1.s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.

1.s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
1.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
1.x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

1.s: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules into seeds.

1.s: The magnitude of root pressure would be minimum during
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Root pressure is lowest in summer, when heavy transpiration pulls water up and the positive root pressure largely disappears. It is highest in the rainy season, when absorption is high and transpiration low, so Rainy season was wrong.

1.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Plant):
a. Fennel
b. Ginger
c. Garlic
d. Touch me not
B (Botanical Name):
I. Mimosa pudica
II. Foeniculum Vulgare
III. Zingiber officinale
IV. Allium Sativum
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Fennel – Foeniculum vulgare, ginger – Zingiber officinale, garlic – Allium sativum, touch-me-not – Mimosa pudica. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Medicinal Plant):
a. Sarpgandha
b. Isabgol
c. Arjuna
d. Sandal
B (Uses):
I. diuretic, refrigerant
II. nervous disorder
III. chronic constipation
IV. heart remedy
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Sarpagandha – nervous disorders (hypertension), isabgol – chronic constipation, arjuna – heart remedy, sandal – diuretic, refrigerant. Off-topic, moved.

1.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Stomata – tiny pores on leaves, guard cells – open and close them, chloroplasts – contain chlorophyll, enzymes – biocatalysts. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to sporopollenin?
i. The exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin so that pollen grains can be preserved as fossils.
ii. It cannot withstand high temperatures.
iii. It is one of the most resistant organic materials.
iv. Enzymes can degrade it.
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: Sporopollenin forms the exine; it is one of the most resistant organic materials, withstands high temperatures and strong acids and alkalis, and no enzyme is known to degrade it – so only i and iii. Moved.

1.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT for the processes involved in photosynthesis?

I. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll

II. Oxidation of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates
1.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
1.x: Photosynthesis begins with absorption of light by chlorophyll (I correct); carbon dioxide is reduced, not oxidised, to carbohydrate (II wrong) → Only I. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Apart from Sun light and Carbon Dioxide, the source for production of Oxygen through photosynthesis in plants is?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Plants split water in photosynthesis (photolysis); the oxygen released comes from water, not from CO2, air, chlorophyll or glucose. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
o: To absorb water from the soil
To take in carbon dioxide and release helium
To transport vitamins through the stem
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Photosynthesis lets green plants make their own food (glucose) from CO2 and water using sunlight; it releases oxygen, not helium. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Name the factor that does not require for photosynthesis
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, water and carbon dioxide (and chlorophyll); oxygen is a product, not a requirement. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Anemophily is pollination by wind; hydrophily is by water, entomophily by insects and ornithophily by birds.

1.s: Which part of Garlic plant is used?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: The edible part of garlic is the bulb made of cloves (modified leaves). Off-topic (botany), moved.

1.s: Plants that complete their life cycle within one season are called
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Plants that complete their life cycle in one season are annuals, also called seasonal plants; biennials take two seasons/years and perennials live many years.

1.s: The following is generally used in bone healing in humans?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Cissus quadrangularis (hadjod, 'bone-setter') is the herb traditionally used for bone healing; garlic, black pepper and onion are not.

1.s: Which plants are called naked-seeded plants?
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
1.x: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines, cycas) bear naked seeds not enclosed in a fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits. (Moved to general science.)

1.s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, so the seeds and progeny are weaker; cross-pollination gives vigour and new varieties. (Moved to general science.)

1.s: The study of grasses is known as:
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Agrostology is the study of grasses; agronomy is crop science and anthology a collection of writings.

1.s: Which of the following seeds have wings that help in seed dispersal?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Drumstick (Moringa) and maple seeds are winged and dispersed by wind; Xanthium and Urena have hooks, castor and balsam burst open.

1.s: The eyes of the potato tuber are
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: The 'eyes' of a potato tuber are axillary buds (in the axils of scale leaves), proving the tuber is a stem.

1.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: The fibre length of cotton is 1-5 cm
Recommended dose of fertilizer (kg/ha) for Pusa
Edible part of apple is mesocarp
1.x: The edible part of an apple is the fleshy thalamus (receptacle), not the mesocarp, so 4 is wrong; cotton fibre of about 1-5 cm and boron as a micronutrient are correct.

1.s: What is the function of "stomata" in plants?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Stomata are leaf pores for gas exchange (CO2 in, O2 and water vapour out); xylem transports water.

1.s: Which of the following inputs is required for photosynthesis to occur?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll, light, CO2 and water; oxygen and glucose are its products.

1.s: Which of the following mechanisms help prevent cavitation in the xylem?
o: Negative pressure inside the vessels and the pores
End walls of the vessels and the pores
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: The end walls of xylem vessels and their pit pores (pit membranes) stop air bubbles spreading, preventing cavitation from blocking the whole water column.

1.s: Which Tissue helps in the transport of water in plants?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from roots upward; phloem carries food.

1.s: Which cells control the opening and closing of stomata?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Two kidney-shaped guard cells around each stoma swell or shrink and so open or close the pore; xylem and phloem conduct water and food.

1.s: Which plant is traditionally known as an antidote for snake bites?
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha) is the traditional snake-bite remedy; neem, teak and sal are not.

1.s: An example of a phosphoenol pyruvate carboxyl kinase (PEP-CK) type of C4 photosynthesis
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: Panicum (e.g. Panicum maximum) is the classic PEP-CK type C4 plant; sugarcane and maize are NADP-ME type, Amaranthus NAD-ME type.

1.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the plant kingdom?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
1.x: Annelids (earthworms, leeches) are animals; algae, pteridophytes and angiosperms belong to the plant kingdom.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant through evaporation at the root surface.

II. Transpiration is the main driver of water movement in the root nodules.

III. Transpiration is caused by the evaporation of water at the leaf-atmosphere interface; it creates negative pressure (tension) at the leaf surface.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
1.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
1.x: Only III is correct: transpiration is evaporation at the leaf-air interface creating tension that pulls water up; it is not loss at the root surface, and it does not drive water in root nodules.

1.s: Which of the following plant tissues contains starch grains and is known as the starch sheath?
1.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
1.x: The endodermis of dicot stems stores starch grains and is called the starch sheath.

1.s: In which of the following species is axile placentation commonly observed?
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
1.x: Hibiscus (family Malvaceae, e.g. China rose, roselle) has axile placentation, ovules on a central axis of a multi-chambered ovary. Legumes such as Delonix show marginal placentation.

1.s: The patterns of arrangement of leaves on the stem are called
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: The arrangement of leaves on the stem is phyllotaxy. Venation is the vein pattern, aestivation the arrangement of floral parts in a bud and placentation of ovules.

1.s: Pollination by birds is called
1.x: Pollination by birds is ornithophily. Anemophily is by wind, entomophily by insects and autogamy is self-pollination.

1.s: Which of the following ions is essential for the opening and closing of stomata in plants?
1.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Potassium ions moving into and out of guard cells open and close the stomata. Carbon, iron and sulphur have no such role.

1.s: What is the function of Xylem in a plant?
o: Transport of food from leaves to rest of the plant
Transport of water from roots to leaves
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Phloem carries food from the leaves to the rest of the plant, and cambium makes new wood layers.

1.s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R).
A: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are grouped under Thallophyta.
R: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara lack roots, stem, leaves, and vascular system.
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
1.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
1.x: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are algae, grouped under Thallophyta because the plant body is an undifferentiated thallus with no roots, stem, leaves or vascular tissue. R states that defining feature, so it correctly explains A.

1.s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots through stems to leaves. Phloem carries food; cambium and cortex do not conduct water.

1.s: In a plant transports food from the leaves to the rest of the plant through a process known as translocation.
1.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
1.x: Phloem moves food (sugars) from the leaves to the rest of the plant; this is translocation. Xylem and tracheids carry water, and meristem is growing tissue.

1.s: According to Sach's, the body of the vascular plant is composed of the following three tissue systems
o: Dermal tissue system, vascular tissue system and fundamental tissue system
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: Julius Sachs grouped plant tissues into three systems: dermal (epidermal), vascular (fundamental conducting) and fundamental (ground) tissue systems. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissue types, not Sachs' tissue systems.

1.s: Which of the following parts of the stem consists of xylem and phloem together?
1.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
1.x: A vascular bundle contains xylem and phloem together. The cortex, endodermis and pith are ground-tissue regions without both conducting tissues.

1.s: Which among the following is actually not a tree?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: The banana is a giant herb: its 'trunk' is a pseudostem of leaf sheaths, not wood. Neem, peepal and banyan are true trees. (Off-topic: botany.)

1.s: Which of the following seeds can benifit a patient of diabetes mellitus?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
1.x: Fenugreek (methi) seeds are rich in soluble fibre and help lower blood sugar, so they benefit diabetics. (Biology item, moved.)

1.s:
Which of the following statements is correct about Angiosperms?

A. Seeds naked (not enclosed in ovary)

B. Xylem vessels usually absent

C. Bears flowers where reproductive spores (gametes) develop
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
