1.x: Angiosperms bear flowers, have seeds enclosed in an ovary (fruit) and usually have xylem vessels. Naked seeds and absent vessels describe gymnosperms, so only C is correct. (Biology item, moved.)

1.s: The seeds of the following plants are often called 'dust seeds'
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: Orchids produce minute, endosperm-less 'dust seeds' dispersed by wind. Lodoicea (double coconut) has the largest seed. (Botany item, moved.)

1.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Plant):
a. Potato
b. Carrot
c. Apple
d. Cabbage
List-II (Edible Part): i. Swollen thalamus ii. Vegetative bud iii. Modified root iv. Modified stem
1.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
1.x: The potato is a modified stem (tuber), the carrot a modified root, the apple a swollen thalamus (false fruit) and the cabbage a vegetative bud.

1.s: What is the colour of Chlorophyll a?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Chlorophyll a is blue-green, while chlorophyll b is yellow-green. (Moved to 5:1.)

1.s: Plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation, are called ......
1.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
1.x: Gymnosperms (gymnos = naked, sperma = seed) have ovules not enclosed in an ovary, exposed before and after fertilisation. Angiosperms enclose ovules in an ovary.

1.s: Spirogyra is an example of:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Spirogyra is a green filamentous alga.

1.s: Which part of the plant is a potato?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
1.x: The potato is a tuber - a modified underground stem with eyes (buds).

1.s: Which of the following plants eats mosquitoes?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
1.x: The pitcher plant is insectivorous – its pitcher traps and digests insects such as mosquitoes. Cinchona gives quinine; lemon grass only repels.

1.s: The drug Rauwolfia, is obtained from ______ of Sarpgandha.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: The drug from Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina), used for blood pressure, comes from its roots. (Off-topic: medicinal plants.)

1.s: The complete male flower of the following plant is transported to the female flower for pollination
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: In Vallisneria the male flowers break off and float up to the water surface, where water currents carry them to the female flowers raised on long stalks, so the whole male flower travels. In Zostera (a seagrass) only long pollen grains are released and carried under water; Nymphaea (water lily) is insect-pollinated.

1.s: The National Tree of India is
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
1.x: India's national tree is the Indian banyan, Ficus benghalensis. Ficus religiosa is the peepal (sacred fig), Ficus elastica the rubber fig and Ficus racemosa the cluster fig (gular).

1.s: Which enzyme present in the stomach breaks down the proteins into small peptides?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Pepsin, from the chief cells of the stomach, breaks proteins into small peptides. Trypsin and peptidases act in the small intestine and lipase digests fats.

1.s: Kwashiorkor disease is a result of
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency in a diet that may have enough calories. Vitamin, carbohydrate or water deficiency do not cause it.

1.s: Which of the following diseases is caused in humans by a severe lack of proteins and calories in the diet?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
1.x: Marasmus results from severe lack of both protein and calories. Scurvy is vitamin C deficiency, goitre iodine deficiency and mumps a viral disease.

1.s: Which of the following are only proteins?
1.x: Keratin (hair, nails) and myosin (muscle) are both proteins. Fructose, maltose and sucrose are sugars, so the other pairs are not only proteins.

1.s: Which of the following refers to a sticky film of protein that forms on top of dairy milk?
1.x: Lactoderm is the name of the sticky protein skin that forms on top of heated milk. The other options are made-up words.

1.s: Which of the following is an essential amino acid for the human body?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Isoleucine is one of the essential amino acids that must come from food. Alanine, aspartic acid and cysteine are made in the body.

1.s: Which of the following is cause of main cause of the disease Kwashiorkor?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency. Water deficiency, pollution and viruses do not cause it.

1.s: Which of the following is a non-essential amino acid?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Tyrosine is non-essential because the body makes it from phenylalanine. Methionine, tryptophan and threonine are essential.

1.s: Principle protein of Maize is:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Zein, a prolamin, is the principal protein of maize, as gluten is of wheat.

1.s: The building blocks from which proteins are synthesized are known as:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Proteins are synthesised from amino acids, their building blocks.

1.s: The egg proteins are known as high biological value proteins because they contain
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Egg proteins have high biological value because they contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportion.

1.s: Which are the primary group of proteins present in Milk?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Caseins are the primary group of milk proteins (about 80% of cow's milk protein); whey proteins make up the rest. Lactoferrin and albumin are minor.

1.s: For muscle building, athletes require a
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: Muscle is built from protein, so athletes need a high-protein diet. Calories, vitamins and glucose give energy or regulation, not muscle tissue.

1.s: Nutrients that help in building the body
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Proteins are the body-building nutrients. Carbohydrates and fats give energy and vitamins regulate.

1.s: Which of the following is known as wheat protein?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: Gluten is the protein of wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

1.s: Which of the following diseases is caused due to deficiency of both proteins and calories in the human diet?
1.src: APPSC Combined Recruitment (Hostel Welfare Officer, Division
1.x: Marasmic kwashiorkor results from deficiency of both proteins and calories (wasting with oedema). Goitre is iodine, achondroplasia genetic and rickets vitamin D.

1.s:
Arrange the following food items in the increasing order of the protein content per 100 gm of food.

a. Egg white
b. Bengalgram dal
c. Fish
d. Skimmed milk powder
e. Groundnuts
Select the appropriate option
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.at: a, c, b, e and d
1.x: Protein per 100 g rises from egg white (~11 g) to fish (~20 g), Bengal gram dal (~21 g), groundnut (~25 g) and skimmed milk powder (~35 g). So a, c, b, e, d.

1.s: Which one of the following are the building blocks of proteins?
1.x: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. Ribosomes make proteins, glucose builds carbohydrates and fatty acids build fats.

1.s: Which of the following is most important for the growth of children upto the age of 14 ?
1.x: Proteins are the body-building nutrient, essential for the growth of children. Milk is a food, not a nutrient, and fats and vitamins do not build tissue.

1.s: Proline is a type of _______.
1.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
1.x: Proline is one of the 20 amino acids that make up proteins (a non-essential one). It is not a base, a bacterium or a virus.

1.s: Edema is a typical clinical feature of which disease?
1.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
1.x: Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) typically shows oedema (swelling). Marasmus is wasting without oedema, and hypertension and fever do not feature oedema as a typical sign.

1.s: Which one of the following is not a protein ?
1.x: Oxytocin is a small peptide hormone of nine amino acids, not a protein. Keratin (hair, nails), fibroin (silk) and collagen (connective tissue) are true fibrous proteins.

1.s: Which one of the following is the richest source of protein?
1.x: Groundnut has about 25 g protein per 100 g, far more than rice (~7 g) or apple (<1 g).

1.s: Hair is composed of protein called –
1.x: Hair is made of the fibrous protein keratin. Casein is milk protein, globulin a blood protein and mucin the protein of mucus.

1.s: Which one of the following food materials contains all essential amino acids?
1.x: Egg protein has the highest biological value and contains all essential amino acids in the right proportion, so it is the reference protein. Milk and soybean are good but are not the exam answer; rice lacks lysine.

1.s: Kwashiorkor, a form of malnutrition, is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
1.x: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with adequate calories (oedema, swollen belly). Selenium, chromium and carbohydrate lack do not cause it.

1.s: Silk fibre, hairs, nails and claw are made of –
1.x:
Most books and keys: keratin. Strictly, silk fibre is fibroin, not keratin; only hair, nails and claws are keratin (PMF General Science Part 7, animal fibres: keratin or fibroin).
Hair, nails and claws are made of keratin, the answer books and keys give. Strictly silk is fibroin (another fibrous protein), so keratin is the best of the four; fibrin is the clot protein, elastin and collagen are connective-tissue proteins.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Human diet should compulsorily contain glycine, serine and tyrosin.
Reason (R) : Essential amino acids can not be synthesized in the human body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Glycine, serine and tyrosine are non-essential – the body makes them – so A is false. R is true: essential amino acids cannot be synthesised and must come from food.

1.s: Alpha-keratin is a protein, present in :
1.x: Alpha-keratin is the fibrous protein of the skin's outer layer, hair and nails. Blood and lymph carry albumin and globulins; eggs carry albumin.

1.s: The disease caused by deficiency of protein in children is–
1.x: Marasmus is protein-energy malnutrition of infants (severe wasting). Pellagra (B3), beri-beri (B1) and rickets (D) are vitamin deficiencies.

1.s: The substance responsible for bread-making quality in wheat is –
1.x: Gluten, the protein of wheat, makes dough elastic and lets bread rise. Globulin is another protein class; glycine and lysine are amino acids.

1.s: Which one of the following proteins is present in human hair and nails?
1.x: Keratin forms hair and nails. Oxytocin and vasopressin are peptide hormones; trypsin is a digestive enzyme.

1.s: Casein is milk :
1.x: Casein is the main protein of milk (~80% of milk protein); milk sugar is lactose.

1.s: Which compound present in D.N.A. does not form amino acid ?
1.x: Adenine, guanine and cytosine are nitrogen bases of DNA; tyrosine is an amino acid, not a DNA component – the odd one out the question intends.

1.s: Most of the enzymes are :
1.x: Almost all enzymes are proteins (a few are RNA ribozymes); they are not lipids, acids or alkalis.

1.s: Which of the following proteins is found in milk ?
1.x: Casein is the main milk protein. Myosin is muscle protein, haemoglobin blood protein and agglutinins are antibodies.

1.s: Which one of the following compounds is not stored in human body –
1.x: Amino acids are not stored – surplus is deaminated and passed as urea. Glycogen (liver, muscle), fat and tocopherol (vitamin E, fat-soluble) are stored.

1.s: Enzymes are basically –
1.x: Enzymes are basically proteins (e.g. pepsin, trypsin) acting as biological catalysts; they are not fats, sugars or vitamins.

1.s: Which of the following disease is caused by severe deficiency of proteins?
1.x: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe protein deficiency; anaemia (iron), osteoporosis (calcium) and goitre (iodine) are not.

1.s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List I
List II
I. Vitamin
A. Pepsin
II. Enzyme
B. Carotene
III. Hormone
C. Keratin
IV. Protein
D. Progesterone
Codes:
o: I - A, II - B, III - C, IV - D
I - B, II - A, III - D, IV - C
I - B, II - A, III - C, IV - D
I - A, II - B, III - D, IV – C
1.x: Vitamin – carotene (provitamin A), enzyme – pepsin, hormone – progesterone, protein – keratin, which is code (b).

1.s: Protein requirement of young and old person are –
o: Higher in the young and lower in the old
Higher in the old and lower in the young
Very high in the young and very low in the old
1.x: Older people need more protein per kg than young adults (about 1.0–1.2 g/kg against 0.8 g/kg) because ageing blunts protein use and causes muscle loss, as the key says.

1.s: Choose wrong statement regarding proteins :
o: We obtain proteins from both animals and plants
Proteins are made of amino acids
About 30 percent of our body weight comes from
Proteins are called building blocks of our body
1.x: About 16–20% (NCERT: ~20%) of body weight is protein, not 30%, so (c) is wrong. Proteins come from plants and animals, are made of amino acids and are the body-building nutrients.

1.s: Tendons through which muscles are connected to bones are tightly compacted bundles of which one of the following long fibrous protein?
1.x: Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.

1.s: An enzyme which helps in the digestion of protein is
1.x:
Most keys: trypsin. Strictly: 'protease' is the class of all protein-digesting enzymes, so it is also true.
Trypsin (pancreas) digests protein; urease breaks urea and sulfatase sulphate esters. 'Protease' is the general class name for all protein-digesting enzymes, not one enzyme.

1.s: Which one of the following processes in the bodies of living organisms is a digestive process?
o: Breakdown of proteins into amino acids
Breakdown of glucose into CO₂ and H₂O
Conversion of amino acids into proteins
1.x: Digestion is breaking large food molecules into small absorbable ones, such as proteins into amino acids. The others are respiration or synthesis.

1.s: Which of the following changes is catalyzed by the enzyme trypsin?
1.x: Trypsin (pancreatic juice) breaks proteins (and peptones) into smaller peptides; peptidases finish them to amino acids. Pepsin makes peptones.

1.s: Which one of the following enzymes convert proteins into amino acids?
1.x: Pepsin is the only protein-digesting enzyme among the options (lactase – lactose, urease – urea, zymase – sugar fermentation); strictly pepsin gives peptides, which other enzymes finish to amino acids.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : All the proteins in our food are digested in small intestine only.
Reason (R) : The protein-digesting enzyme from the pancreas are released into the small intestine.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
1.x: Protein digestion starts in the stomach with pepsin, so A is false; R is true – pancreatic trypsin and chymotrypsin enter the small intestine.

1.s: Which of the following is used in beauty parlours for hair setting?
1.x: Hair setting and perming work on the sulphur (disulphide) bonds of hair keratin, which are broken and re-formed in the new shape with sulphur compounds (thioglycolates). Chlorine and phosphorus are not used.

1.s: The plant dye henna imparts orange-red colour to skin and hairs due to its reaction with which of the following?
1.x: Lawsone, the dye of henna, binds to the proteins (keratin) and amino acids of skin and hair, giving the orange-red stain. It does not react with lipids, carbohydrates or nucleic acids.

1.s:
Which of the following are correct with reference to proteins?
i. They are made up of nucleotides.
ii. They are linear chains of amino acids.
iii. They are heteropolymer.
iv. They are homopolymer.
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: Proteins are linear chains of amino acids and are heteropolymers (20 kinds of amino acids); nucleotides make nucleic acids. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Which of the following digestive enzymes acts in the stomach of humans?
1.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
1.x: Pepsin acts in the stomach (protein digestion in acid medium); amylase acts in mouth and intestine, trypsin and lipase come from the pancreas.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about proteins:
1. Proteins give about 4 kcal per gram.
2. Of the 20 common amino acids, about 9-10 are essential.
3. A nursing mother needs at least 45 g of protein a day.
4. Soybean is the highest-protein grain (about 40 g per 100 g).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a nursing mother needs 65 g of protein a day.

1.s:
Match List I (Protein) with List II (Found in):
List I
a. Casein
b. Gluten
c. Zein
d. Keratin
List II
i. Hair, nails, horn
ii. Maize
iii. Milk
iv. Wheat
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
1.x: Casein (~80% of milk protein) – milk; gluten – wheat; zein – maize; keratin – hair, nails, horn.

1.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A child with kwashiorkor shows oedema and a swollen belly.
Reason (R): Kwashiorkor is caused by a severe lack of both protein and calories.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: A is true. R is false: kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with adequate calories; a severe lack of both protein and calories (extreme wasting, no oedema) is marasmus.

1.s: The "Iodine test" is used for testing the presence of?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Iodine solution turns starch blue-black, so the iodine test detects starch. Sugars, fats and salt give no such colour (fat is tested with paper, sugar with Benedict's reagent).

1.s: Which of the following type of carbohydrate is present in starch?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
1.x: Starch is a polysaccharide, a long chain of glucose units. Mono-, di- and oligosaccharides are single sugars or short chains.

1.s: Which of the following is the major nutrient present in rice?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Rice is mostly starch, so carbohydrate is its major nutrient. Its protein is only about 7%, and vitamins and minerals are minor.

1.s: Arrange the following sugars in the descending order of their relative sweetness?
1.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar, followed by sucrose, glucose and maltose. The other orders put glucose, maltose or sucrose first.

1.s: Out of the below, which sugar constitutes the largest component of Honey?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
1.x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%), with slightly less glucose; sucrose and maltose are minor. So fructose is its largest component.

1.s:
Which of the following matches of the sweetener and its explanation is correct?
Sweetener:

I. Ortho-sulphobenzimide (Saccharin)

II. Aspartame

III. Alitame
Explanation:

a. 100 times as sweet as cane sugar

b. High potency sweetener

c. The first popular artifical sweetening agent
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
1.x: Saccharin was the first popular artificial sweetener, aspartame is (in NCERT's words) about 100 times as sweet as cane sugar, and alitame is a high-potency sweetener. So I-c, II-a, III-b.

1.s: What are the basic chemical units with which lipids are made?
1.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
1.x: Lipids (fats) are made of fatty acids joined to glycerol. Glucose and fructose build carbohydrates, and amino acids build proteins.

1.s: The major part in honey is
1.x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%) with slightly less glucose, so fructose is its major sugar. Sucrose and maltose are only minor components.

1.s: The cause of sweet taste in fruits is :
1.x: Fructose (fruit sugar) gives fruits their sweet taste. Maltose is malt sugar, lactose milk sugar and ribose a sugar of RNA.

1.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and other as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : Invert sugar is more sweet than sucrose.
Reason (R) : Invert sugar is obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
1.x: Invert sugar (glucose + fructose) is sweeter than sucrose because of its free fructose. It is made by hydrolysing sucrose, which is true but is not why it is sweeter.

1.s: In honey, which one among the following sugars predominates ?
1.x: Fructose predominates in honey, slightly ahead of glucose. Sucrose, galactose and maltose are minor or absent.

1.s: Which one of the following artificial sweetners is modified sugar?
1.x: Sucralose is made by replacing hydroxyl groups of sucrose with chlorine, so it is a modified sugar. Aspartame is a dipeptide, saccharin and alitame are not made from sugar.

1.s: Which of the following is a cereal grain product :
1.x: Oatmeal is made from oats, a cereal grain. Sago and arrowroot are starches from palm stems and roots, and soya flour comes from a legume.

1.s: Which of the following nutrients is known as the primary 'energy-giving' food for our body?
1.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
1.x: Carbohydrates are the primary energy-giving food. Proteins build the body, and vitamins and minerals regulate it.

1.s: Which of the following is rich in all the three foods carbohydrates, proteins and fats?
1.x: Soybean has about 40% protein and 20% fat besides carbohydrate, so it is rich in all three. Rice is mainly carbohydrate, and mango and cabbage are poor in protein and fat.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT among the essential foods produced by plants each being of value in its own way to human and animal metabolism?
1.x: Plants make carbohydrates, fats and proteins as essential foods for human and animal metabolism. Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) are genetic material, not a food group.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient required for livestock ?
1.x: Vitamins are micronutrients needed in small amounts, whereas protein, carbohydrates and fats are macronutrients.

1.s: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?
1.x: Rice has the highest carbohydrate share of the cereals given (~78% of the grain); wheat, barley and maize have more protein and fibre.

1.s: Which one of the following groups of diet provides maximum energy to human body?
1.x: Carbohydrate, fat and protein are the energy-giving nutrients (about 4, 9 and 4 kcal/g); vitamins, minerals and water give no energy.

1.s: The major food fuel during exercise of long duration is
1.x:
Printed key / most books: carbohydrate. Strictly, in prolonged low- to moderate-intensity exercise fat supplies about half or more of the energy (CSU Nutrition and Fitness 8.6; Nutrition Research Reviews 2003).
The key is carbohydrate: muscle glycogen and blood glucose fuel sustained, high-intensity endurance work, and running out of glycogen ends it. Fat's share rises in very long, gentle exercise, so fat is the tempting option; protein is a minor fuel.

1.s: Glucose is a source of energy, which one of the following types of molecule is glucose ?
1.x: Glucose is a monosaccharide – a simple carbohydrate – not a protein, fat or nucleic acid.

1.s: Which one among the following statements about a healthy diet is correct?
o: Regular eating of high energy snacks between meals is healthy, since it provides energy and vitamins in plenty.
Fruits and vegetables make a good choice because their energy content is high.
A balanced diet must contain plenty of fat and protein with little carbohydrates and fibre.
An optimal quantity of fat, protein carbohydrate with adequate amount of water and fibre makes a healthy diet.
1.x: A healthy diet has an optimal amount of carbohydrate, protein and fat with enough water and fibre. Frequent high-energy snacks, 'high-energy' fruits and a high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet are all wrong ideas.

1.s: Which of the following is known as energy currency for cellular process?
1.x: ATP stores and releases energy for all cell processes, so it is the energy currency. Glucose is the fuel, ADP the spent form and pyruvic acid a glycolysis product.

1.s: What taste do starchy substances have?
1.x:
APPSC key: sweet. Strictly, pure starch is nearly tasteless; it tastes sweet only as salivary amylase turns it into maltose (NCERT Class 7, Nutrition in Animals).
Starch is broken by salivary amylase into maltose, so starchy food tastes sweet on chewing – the key. Bitter, mint and sour are not carbohydrate tastes.

1.s: How do carbohydrates taste?
1.x: Carbohydrates (sugars such as fructose, sucrose, glucose) taste sweet; starch tastes sweet on chewing as amylase forms maltose.

1.s: Which of the following gives maximum energy in metabolic processes?
1.x: Fats give about 9 kcal/g, more than twice carbohydrates or proteins (~4 kcal/g); minerals give no energy.

1.s: In which category of food is the most amount of calories per unit –
1.x: Fats have the most calories per gram (~9 kcal), against ~4 kcal for carbohydrates and proteins; vitamins give none.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : Unsaturated fats are more reactive compared with the saturated fats.
Reason (R) : Unsaturated fats have only single bonds in their structure.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
1.x: Unsaturated fats are more reactive because they have carbon–carbon double bonds, so A is true and R (only single bonds) is false; single bonds only describe saturated fats.

1.s: Which of following is an artificial sweetening agent?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
1.x: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener; sucrose is natural sugar, glycine an amino acid and steviol glycosides a natural sweetener from stevia.

1.s: Which one of the following statements regarding starch and cellulose is not correct?
o: Both of them are of plant origin.
Both of them give colour with iodine
Both of them are made up of glucose molecules.
1.x: Starch gives a blue-black colour with iodine, but cellulose does not. Both are plant-origin glucose polymers.

1.s: Which of these is not a colloid?
1.x: Honey is a supersaturated sugar solution (true solution), not a colloid. Milk is an emulsion, blood and ice-cream are colloidal systems.

1.s: What is the formula of glucose ?
1.x: Glucose is C6H12O6; C6H10O5 is the starch/cellulose unit and C12H22O11 is sucrose.

1.s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

1.s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

1.s: In which of the following season human beings require food with more fat content
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: In winter the body needs more energy to keep warm, so fat-rich (energy-dense) food is needed most then. Off-topic (nutrition).

1.s: Carbohydrates are organic compounds with the basic structure:
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

1.s:
Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules which include carbohydrates. Match the following Group of Carbohydrates with their examples.
Group of Carbohydrates:
I. Monosaccharides
II. Oligosaccharides
III. Polysaccharides
Examples:
a. Cellulose
b. Ribose
c. Maltose
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: Ribose – monosaccharide, maltose – oligosaccharide (disaccharide), cellulose – polysaccharide. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s:
A company marketing food products advertise that its items do not contain trans-fats. What does this campaign signify to the customers?

A. The food products are not made out of hydrogenated oils.

B. The food products are not made out of animal fats/oils.

C. The oils used are not likely to damage the cardiovascular health of the consumers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: 'No trans-fats' means no partially hydrogenated oils (A) and so less harm to heart health (C); animal fats may still be used (small natural trans fats aside), so B does not follow.

1.s: Which of the following contains high caffeine content per equal weight?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: By equal dry weight, tea leaves contain more caffeine (about 3-4%) than coffee beans (about 1-2%), though a brewed cup of coffee has more; chocolate has far less.

1.s: The sweetest sugar is
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: Fructose (fruit sugar, levulose) is the sweetest natural sugar, about 1.7 times as sweet as sucrose.

1.s: Honey is sweeter than cane sugar or corn syrup. Which one of the following carbon sugars is responsible for this?
1.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
1.x:
Levulose (option 2) is the same sugar as fructose, so both options are chemically right; keyed 'Fructose' as the standard name.
Honey is sweeter than cane sugar mainly because of fructose, the sweetest sugar. Levulose is only another name for fructose; dextrose (glucose) and sucrose are less sweet.

1.s: Which of the following forms of sugar is the main constituent of sugar cane juice?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Sugarcane juice is mainly sucrose (cane sugar), a disaccharide of glucose and fructose. Glucose, fructose and dextrose are only minor components.

1.s: After eating which of the following items, a person is likely feel more thirsty?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Salted chips add sodium, raising the salt concentration of body fluids and triggering thirst; the other foods have little salt.

1.s: Test used to detect starch adulteration in milk
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Starch in milk turns blue with iodine solution – the iodine test.

1.s: Why are roughages important in our food?
o: They help in expel of undigested food
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Roughage (dietary fibre) is indigestible plant carbohydrate: it gives no energy or nutrients but adds bulk and helps the body get rid of undigested food (prevents constipation). Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats, body building from proteins, and vitamins from food itself – not from roughage.

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbohydrates are the main energy-giving food.
2. Fat gives about 9.3 kcal per gram, the most per gram.
3. Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar.
4. Invert sugar is less sweet than sucrose.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statements 1-3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: invert sugar (glucose + fructose from hydrolysis of sucrose) is sweeter than sucrose because of its free fructose.

1.s: 'Volume of a given mass of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature'. This statement is associated with:
1.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
1.x: Boyle's Law: at constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's Law relates volume and temperature.

1.s: Ignoring friction of air, if one brick and one feather are released to ground from top of a building, which one reaches ground first?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g whatever their mass, so the brick and the feather reach the ground together (Galileo; shown on the Moon by Apollo 15).

1.s: Which liquid would boil last?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
1.x: Mercury boils at about 357°C, far above water (100°C), benzene (80°C) and ethyl alcohol (78°C), so it boils last.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of friction?
o: Applying brakes to stop a moving car
Revolution of the planets around the sun
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Planets revolve round the Sun because of gravity in near-vacuum space, so there is no friction; brakes, striking a match and walking all depend on friction.

1.s: A Ball thrown outside from an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth will –
o: Revolve around the Earth in the same orbit with the
1.x: A ball released from an orbiting satellite already has the satellite's orbital speed, so it keeps falling round the Earth in the same orbit, like the satellite itself.

1.s: If a piece of wood and a piece of iron are placed in a fridge and taken out after 15 minutes, which one would feel more cold on touching?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster and feels colder, though both are at the same temperature. Wood is a poor conductor.

1.s: What is a change of position?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x:
Most keys: Motion. Strictly: the change in position (a vector) is displacement (NCERT Class 9 ch. 8).
In school physics, motion is the change of position of a body with time, which is the key the paper gives. Strictly, the size and direction of the change in position is displacement, and distance is the path length.

1.s: "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving at a constant velocity will continue moving at a constant velocity, unless it is acted on by an unbalanced force". This law is called as ____.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The second law gives F = ma, the third deals with action and reaction, and there is no fourth law.

1.s: Which of these is the change of gaseous state directly to solid state without going through liquid state?
1.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
1.x: The change of a gas directly into a solid is deposition (desublimation); sublimation is the reverse, solid to gas. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: If two papers are kept very close to each other and wind is blown in between them, they would
1.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Air blown between the sheets moves fast and its pressure drops (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher outside pressure pushes the papers together. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Which of the following principles is used in the process of cooling air in air-conditioners?
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Air-conditioners cool a room by circulating air: cooled air sinks and warm air rises to the unit – a convection current. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A person wonders how is it possible for insects to walk on water, human beings can't do it. In order to answer this question, we will have to refer to the concept of:
1.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
1.x: Surface tension – the cohesive 'skin' of the water surface – supports light insects such as water striders. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of substance by 1°C is called
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C is its specific heat. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Why a glass bottle full of water breaks, if kept in a fridge?
o: The pressure in the fridge would be very high
When water solidifies, it expands in volume
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice exerts pressure that cracks the glass bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The Volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain of freezing
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
1.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: If a person goes down into a deep mine, his weight?
o: Depends on location of the mine
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: g falls with depth below the surface, so a person's weight decreases slightly in a deep mine. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: When an air bubble at the bottom of a lake rises to the top, it will
o: Flattens into a dish like shape
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: Water pressure falls as the bubble rises, so the trapped air expands and the bubble grows (Boyle's law). Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain on freezing
1.x: Water expands on freezing; the ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Super cooling stands for cooling of a liquid
1.x: Supercooling is cooling a liquid below its freezing point without it solidifying. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: After taking out from the fridge, compared to an apple, water melon would retain the coolness for more time because?
o: It is bigger in size and hene more volume
It contains more water which has higher specific heat
It is more green in colour which does reflects atmospheric heat
It has thicker skin which would not allow penetration of heat
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
1.x: Watermelon contains more water, which has a high specific heat, so it takes longer to warm up. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: What happens when salt is added to boiling water?
o: The water will boil more and temperature of the water would fall
The Water will stop boiling and the temperature of the water would fall
The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
The water will boil more and the temperature of the water would rise
1.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
1.x: Salt raises the boiling point, so the water stops boiling for a moment and its temperature rises to the new, higher boiling point before it boils again. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: Ice skating demonstrates that when ice is under pressure, its melting point
o: Melting point has no relation with pressure
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
1.x: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice (regelation); the skate's pressure melts a thin water layer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: What is the result when we add salt in water?
o: The boiling point decreases and freezing point increases.
The boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.
Both the boiling point and the freezing point increase.
Both the boiling point and freezing point decrease.
1.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
1.x: A dissolved salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: Mothballs work on the principle of
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
1.x: Naphthalene mothballs pass straight from solid to vapour – sublimation. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: During winter in cold countries, the following is mixed to melt the ice on the roads?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Salt (rock salt) spread on roads lowers the freezing point of water and melts ice. Off-topic (everyday chemistry), moved.

1.s: The triple point of pure water is at
1.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
1.x: The triple point of pure water – where ice, liquid water and vapour coexist in equilibrium – is 0.01 °C (273.16 K) at about 611.657 Pa. (Off-topic physics; moved.)

1.s: When ice is melting its temperature would?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: While ice melts, the heat supplied goes into latent heat of fusion, so its temperature stays constant at 0°C. Off-topic (physics), moved.

1.s: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Displacement is the shortest straight-line path between the initial and final positions; distance is the actual path length. Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

1.s: How much heat is required to increase the temperature of 1 gram kerosene by 1 degree centigrade?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: The specific heat of kerosene is about 2.1 J/g°C, i.e. about 0.5 cal per gram per °C (water = 1 cal). A physics question, moved.

1.s: What is the approximate value of 1 calorie in Joules?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: 1 calorie = 4.186 J, i.e. about 4.2 J (Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat). A physics question, moved.

1.s: Which liquid is represented by the Volume-Temperature Curve? (The curve shows volume falling from 0°C to a minimum at 4°C and rising again up to 10°C.)
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: Water contracts from 0°C to 4°C (maximum density) and expands above it – the anomalous expansion of water.

1.s: Which of the following is responsible for slowing down a moving object?
1.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
1.x: Friction is the force that opposes motion and slows a moving object.

1.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of gravity?
o: Revolution of planets around the sun
A rock rolling down a hill
Formation of tides in the ocean
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
1.x: Writing with a pencil works by friction, not gravity; planetary revolution, a rock rolling downhill and tides are effects of gravity.

1.s: A boat filled with heavy stones is in a lake. If the stones are thrown into the lake, the level of water with respect to the boat would?
1.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
1.x: A floating boat displaces water equal to the stones' weight; sunk, the stones displace only their volume, so the lake level falls (and the lighter boat rides higher).

1.s: If an object is thrown upwards, what will be its velocity, when it reaches its maximum height (neglect the air resistance)?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: At the maximum height the vertical velocity of a body thrown upwards becomes zero (it then falls back).

1.s: Which of the following materials is not commonly used as sound-proof material?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: Rockwool, wood and (double/laminated) glass are used for sound insulation; plain iron sheets reflect and transmit sound and are not a sound-proofing material.

1.s: Stainless steel pans are sometimes provided with copper bottom because?
o: Copper is not a harmful metal
Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
Oil stains on Copper are easier to clean
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
1.x: Copper conducts heat much better than steel, so a copper bottom spreads heat quickly and evenly.

1.s: How many classes of levers are there with reference to simple machines?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
1.x: Levers are of three classes (fulcrum, load or effort in the middle). Physics of simple machines, not ICT.

1.s: What is the density of water?
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Pure water has a density of about 1 g/cm3 (1,000 kg/m3), highest at 4 °C.

1.s:
Assertion (A) : A man standing on a completely frictionless surface can propel himself by whistling.
Reason (R) : If no external force acts on a system, its momentum cannot change.
Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
1.x:
Printed key: (b) both true, R not the explanation. Many solvers argue (a), since conservation of momentum (R) explains the recoil, and some call A practically false (general knowledge, not checked).
Both statements are true, and the printed key takes R as not the correct explanation of A. Blowing air out while whistling pushes the man the opposite way (third law), while R is the general conservation of momentum.

1.s: What should be the size of the burner of the gas stove to save the consumption of LPG?
o: Size of the burner does not matter
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: A small burner saves LPG because its flame stays under the vessel's base. A large flame spills heat around the sides. (Off-topic: energy saving in daily life.)

1.s: If a balloon filled with air is immersed in hot water, its volume would
1.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
1.x: Air expands when heated (Charles's law), so a balloon in hot water swells and its volume increases. (Off-topic: physics.)

1.s: If egg shell is carefully dissolved in acid and then immersed in salt water, then the shell?
1.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
1.x: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate shell, leaving the semi-permeable membrane; in strong salt water (hypertonic) water leaves the egg by osmosis, so it shrinks. Off-topic science, moved.

1.s: Temperature and time used to sterilise glassware in hot air oven
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

1.s: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
1.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
1.x: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

1.s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
1.x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

1.s:
Match the types of following of asexual reproduction in Column A with correct example in Column
B.
Column A:
A. Binary fission B. Budding
C. Regeneration
D. Spore formation
Column B: i. Amoeba ii. Yeast iii. Rhizopus iv. Planaria
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Binary fission – Amoeba, budding – yeast, regeneration – Planaria, spore formation – Rhizopus. Off-topic, moved.

1.s:
Match the given component of living tissues with the percentage of the total cellular mass.
Component:
I. Lipids
II. Proteins
III. Carbohydrates
IV. Nucleic acids
Percentage of the total cellular mass:
a. 5-7%
b. 10-15%
c. 3%
d. 2%
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x: In a cell, proteins are 10–15%, nucleic acids 5–7%, carbohydrates 3% and lipids 2% of the mass (water 70–90%). Moved.

1.s: Aerobic respiration process requires
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose using oxygen (giving CO2, water, energy). Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: Which is the correct statement about a genetic code?
o: UAC, UAG, and UGA are stop codons.
Initiation codon AUG codes for arginine.
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: The genetic code is a triplet (codon of three bases) and nearly universal; stop codons are UAA, UAG, UGA (not UAC); AUG codes for methionine. Off-topic (biology), moved.

1.s: ATP molecule releases about how much energy?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP releases about 30.5 kJ/mol (7.3 kcal/mol) under standard conditions.

1.s: Normally how many number of Autosomes will be present in human beings?
1.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
1.x: Human cells have 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs (44) of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

1.s: The structural carbohydrates of vegetables and fruits are
1.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
1.x: Cellulose is the structural carbohydrate of plant cell walls in fruits and vegetables.

1.s: Genes controlling the body characteristics are found in
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
1.x: Genes for body characters are carried by both sperms and eggs, which each pass one set of chromosomes.

1.s: In Chlorophyll, the central metal ion is?
1.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
1.x: Magnesium is the central metal ion of chlorophyll. Off-topic (biology).

1.s: Which of the following chromosomes is/are the sex chromosomes?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
1.x: Humans have two sex chromosomes, X and Y (XX female, XY male); Z belongs to the ZW system of birds.

1.s: What is the full form of ATP?
1.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
1.x: ATP is Adenosine Triphosphate: adenosine (adenine + ribose) with three phosphate groups, the cell's energy currency. 'Adenine' alone lacks the ribose, and 'protease' is an enzyme class.

1.s: What is known as the 'energy molecule' in the living World?
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. TNT is an explosive, ADP is its spent form and DNA is the genetic material.

1.s: Which of the following is the controlling centre of a cell?
1.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
1.x: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and directs its activities, so it is the control centre of the cell. Chloroplasts make food, mitochondria release energy and the nucleolus only makes ribosomes.

1.s: Which organelle is called power house of the cell?
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell: they release energy as ATP by cellular respiration.

1.s: Which of the following part of a cell is called power house of energy?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; the nucleus controls the cell and vacuoles store substances.

1.s: If mitochondria is removed from a living cell?
o: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
Cell fluid would not be transported
1.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
1.x: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, so removing them stops the cell's energy metabolism. Reproduction and transport would only fail as a later result.

1.s: At what time respiration takes place in plants?
o: There is no need for respiration in plants
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: Plants respire all the time, day and night; only photosynthesis needs light. So respiration is a continuous process.

1.s: The occurrence of differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species is called
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Differences in characters among individuals of the same species are called variation. Inheritance is passing on traits, evolution the long-term change and adaptation a fit to the habitat.

1.s: Fermentation of Yeast is an example of?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
1.x: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and CO2 without oxygen, so fermentation is anaerobic respiration.

1.s: The limit of growth is fixed by which of the following factor?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
1.x: The limit of growth is fixed by internal (genetic, hormonal) factors of the organism; nutrition and exercise only help reach it.

1.s: Sweating is an
o: Difficult to state, which type of process it is
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: Sweat cools the body because its evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, so sweating is an endothermic process.

1.s: Respiration is an
1.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
1.x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

1.s: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is a/an?
1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
1.x: Composting is microbial oxidation of organic matter and releases heat (compost heaps warm up), so it is exothermic.

1.s: What term describes the phenomenon in which a single species evolves into several different forms to exploit different ecological niches?
1.x:
Printed key: Adaptation (adaptive radiation). Strictly the phenomenon is adaptive radiation, a form of divergent evolution, so 'Divergence' is also defensible (general knowledge, not checked).
A single species evolving into many forms that exploit different niches is adaptive radiation (Darwin's finches), which the key reads as 'adaptation'. Strictly, adaptive radiation is a case of divergent evolution; convergence is the opposite process.

1.s: Out of the following, which is a product of the first stage of oxidation of Glucose?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: The first stage of glucose oxidation is glycolysis, which splits glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate) in the cytoplasm; CO2, and ethanol (in fermentation) come later, and ATP is a by-product, not the product of glucose breakdown.

1.s: Identify the organisms that reproduce asexually by budding.
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
1.x: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by budding; Amoeba and Paramecium divide by binary fission.

1.s: In humans, which cells can perform anaerobic respiration during oxygen shortage?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Skeletal muscle cells respire anaerobically in oxygen shortage, producing lactic acid.

1.s: Which of the following is present in plant cells but not cells of animals?
1.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
1.x: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack; both have vacuoles, plasma membrane and Golgi.

1.s:
Assertion (A): The amount of DNA present in somatic cell depends on the phase of the cell cycle.
Reason (R): Telophase and G1 phase nuclei contain only half (as 2c) the amount of DNA found in the prophase; G2 phase and metaphase cells represent 4c.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is not correct explanation for (A).
(A) is correct and (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct and (R) is correct
1.x: DNA content changes over the cell cycle: G1 and telophase nuclei are 2C, G2/prophase/metaphase 4C after S-phase replication - so R correctly explains A.

1.s: During the period of intense body exercise, which of the following increases in the blood of person?
1.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
1.x: During intense exercise muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up in the blood; oxygen and glucose fall.

1.s: Which of the following is a homopolymer?
1.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
1.x: Cellulose is a homopolymer of beta-glucose only; proteins and collagen are built from many different amino acids, and agarose has alternating galactose units (agarobiose). (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: The most abundant organic compound in world is?
1.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
1.x: Cellulose, the main component of plant cell walls, is the most abundant organic compound on Earth. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: The ATP production through respiration is called
1.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
1.x: ATP made in respiration via the electron transport chain is oxidative phosphorylation; photophosphorylation is ATP formation in photosynthesis. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

1.s: In a mammal, what is the ratio of the number of chromosomes in a somatic cell to that in a gamete?
1.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
1.x: Somatic cells are diploid (2n, 46 in humans) and gametes haploid (n, 23), so the ratio is 2:1.

1.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
1.x: Mitochondria - powerhouse, ATP (3); ribosomes - protein synthesis (1); cell membrane - regulates passage (4); nucleus - control centre with genetic material (2).

1.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Amoeba is reproduced by fission.
2.
Reason (R): All unicellular organisms are reproduced by asexual methods.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
1.x: Amoeba reproduces by binary fission (A true), but not all unicellular organisms are only asexual - Chlamydomonas, Paramecium (conjugation) and yeast show sexual reproduction (R false).

1.s:
Arrange the following events of "biogeny theory" in a sequence.

a. Formation of coacervates

b. Aerobic organisms came to existence

c. Heterotropic organisms began to form

d. Mycoplasmas are first formed cells
1.x: In the biogeny sequence, coacervates formed first, then the first cells (mycoplasma-like), then heterotrophs, and aerobic organisms came last: a, d, c, b. (Off-topic: origin of life.)

1.s: Recently the State of Tamil Nadu banned the sale of cotton candy due to the presence of which cancercausing agent in it?
1.x: Rhodamine B, a textile dye, was found colouring cotton candy; it is carcinogenic, so Tamil Nadu banned the sale (Feb 2024). Aristolochic acid comes from some herbal medicines, benzidine is a dye intermediate and 1,3-butadiene a rubber monomer.

1.s: Which of the following is used as an adulterant of a mustard seed?
1.x: Argemone (Mexican prickly poppy) seeds look like mustard seeds and are mixed with them; their oil causes epidemic dropsy. Papaya, cumin and coriander seeds are not the usual adulterants of mustard.

1.s: Which of the following pairs (Fat - Oil) is not correctly matched?
1.x: Mustard oil is an edible vegetable oil, not a lubricant, so that pair is wrong. Mineral oil comes from petroleum, vegetable fats contain phytosterols and animal fats contain cholesterol.

1.s: The chemical that is used to ripen mangoes is
1.x: Calcium carbide reacts with moisture to give acetylene, which acts like the ripening hormone ethylene, so it is (illegally) used to ripen mangoes. Calcium sulphide, carbonate and chloride release no such gas.

1.s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins which are not generally destroyed by normal cooking process. Aflatoxins are produced by
1.x: Aflatoxins are made by moulds (Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus) that grow on badly stored grain and oilseeds. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses do not produce them.

1.s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins, which are not destroyed by the normal cooking process? Aflatoxins are produced by:
1.x: Aflatoxins are poisonous, cancer-causing chemicals made by moulds such as Aspergillus flavus on stored grain; cooking does not destroy them. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses are wrong.

1.s: Which of the following chemicals is used for ripening?
1.x: Calcium carbide gives acetylene, which ripens fruit like ethylene, so it is the chemical used for (artificial) ripening. Sodium and potassium chloride have no ripening action.

1.s: Which of the following is the most common food preservative against mould, bacteria, fungus and yeast?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
1.x: Sorbic acid and its salt potassium sorbate are the commonest preservatives against moulds, yeasts and fungi. Tartaric acid is a food acid, acetylsalicylic acid is aspirin and formic acid only a limited preservative.

1.s: Sodium benzoate is used as a:
1.x: Sodium benzoate (E211) is a food preservative that stops bacteria, yeast and moulds in acidic foods and drinks. It is not a flavour, colour or antacid.

1.s: What causes ‘Blackheart’ in potato ?
1.x: Blackheart of potato is a storage disorder caused by oxygen deficiency in the tuber's centre. It is not caused by a copper, boron or potassium deficiency.

1.s: The substance employed for the food processing is
1.x: Benzoic acid (as sodium benzoate) is a standard food-processing preservative. Sodium carbonate, acetylene and sodium nitrate are not the usual answer.

1.s: Date of manufacture of food items fried in oil should be checked before buying because oils become rancid due to
1.x: Fats and oils turn rancid when they are oxidised by air, which is why the manufacture date of fried food matters. Reduction and hydrogenation do not cause rancidity.

1.s: Fruits stored in a cold chamber exhibit longer storage life because
o: concentration of carbon dioxide in the environment is increased.
there is an increase in humidity.
1.x: Low temperature slows the respiration rate of fruits, so they ripen and decay more slowly and keep longer. Darkness, CO2 or humidity are not the main reason.

1.s: What is IQF in food preservations?
1.x: IQF stands for Individually Quick Frozen, a technique where each piece of food is frozen separately and rapidly to keep texture and quality.

1.s: Which of the following phytohormone is mainly responsible for fruit ripening ?
1.x: Ethylene is the gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening. Cytokinin promotes cell division and abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor.

1.s: The gas used for artificial ripening of green fruit is
1.x: Ethylene is the gas (plant hormone) used for artificial ripening of green fruit. Acetylene from calcium carbide only imitates it, and ethane and CO2 do not ripen fruit.

1.s: Plants contain a variety of sterols like stigmasterol, ergosterol, sitosterol etc which very closely resemble cholesterol. These plant sterols are referred as
1.x: Plant sterols (stigmasterol, sitosterol, ergosterol) are called phytosterols; ergocalciferol is vitamin D2 and lumisterol a by-product of its synthesis.

1.s: Artificial chemicals are bio-chemically known as
1.x: Man-made chemicals that interfere with the hormone system (BPA, phthalates, some pesticides) are called endocrine disruptors. 'Facilitators', 'reactors' and 'inhibitors' are not the accepted term.

1.s: Which gas is used to ripen fruits?
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Ethylene is the gaseous fruit-ripening hormone.

1.s:
Which of the following are symptoms of food allergy?

a. Nervousness

b. Fall in blood pressure

c. Atherosclerosis

d. Flushing of the skin

e. Difficulty in swallowing and speaking
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Food allergy can cause a fall in blood pressure (anaphylaxis), flushing or hives, and swelling of the throat with difficulty in swallowing and speaking. Atherosclerosis is a chronic artery disease, and nervousness is not a typical allergic sign.

1.s: Which one of the following is the best example of desiccant?
1.x: Silica gel absorbs moisture and is the standard desiccant (in packets with shoes, medicines, electronics). Polystyrene is a plastic, and NaCl and Na2CO3 are not used as desiccants.

1.s: Which hormone is found in the gaseous form ?
1.x: Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas (fruit ripening); abscisic acid, gibberellins and auxins are not gaseous.

1.s: "Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following? Environmental Degradation PMF IAS E&E – 44
1.x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

1.s: 'Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following?
1.x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

1.s: Sun drying is a method of:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

1.s: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
1.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
1.x: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

1.s: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
1.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

1.s: Most of the artificial food colouring agents are derived from
1.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
1.x: Most synthetic food colours (tartrazine, sunset yellow) are coal-tar (petroleum-derived) dyes. Flowers, fruits and lichens give natural colours.

1.s: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
o: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
1.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
1.x: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

1.s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
1.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
1.x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

1.s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
1.x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

1.s: Rancidity is a/an
1.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
1.x: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

1.s: Which of the following chemical compound added to bread was banned in India
1.src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
1.x: FSSAI removed potassium bromate from the list of permitted additives in 2016 after CSE found it in bread (possible carcinogen). Gluconate, sulphate and oxalate were not the banned bread additive.

1.s: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
o: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
1.x: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

1.s: Development of off odour in fats & oils when they are stored for a longer duration is known as
1.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
1.x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

1.s: Primary methods to prevent food spoilage do NOT include:
1.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
1.x: Food spoilage is prevented by refrigeration, drying, salting, canning and preservatives; exposure to air, moisture and microbes causes spoilage, so it is not a method.

1.s: Which of the following food–adulterant pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chilli powder — Brick powder or Sudan dyes
Milk — Water, detergent, urea or starch
1.x: Turmeric is adulterated with metanil yellow or lead chromate; argemone oil is the adulterant of mustard oil.
xa: Argemone oil in mustard oil causes **epidemic dropsy**.
**Lead chromate** in spices is a source of **lead** — **neurotoxic**, worst in children.
Adulteration effects: acute poisoning, allergies, nutritional deficiency.

1.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: BPA — Polycarbonate plastics and thermal receipts
1.x: Lead is associated with old paints, pipes, some cosmetics and lead-chromate-adulterated spices, not MRI contrast agents. BPA, triclosan and phthalates are correctly matched with their listed sources.
1.tq: Find the incorrectly matched source among closely related chemical-product pairs.
xs: **Lead – MRI contrast agent** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**Lead** is found in **old paints, pipes, some cosmetics, spices adulterated with lead chromate**.
Others are right: **triclosan** — antibacterial soaps, toothpaste; **BPA** — polycarbonate plastics, thermal receipts; **phthalates** — PVC, toys, cosmetics.
xa: Lead is **neurotoxic**, worst in **children**.
BPA also lines **food cans** (epoxy linings).
**MRI** uses a **magnetic field + radio waves** with **no ionising radiation**.

1.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sodium benzoate is used in soft drinks, acidic foods and fruit juice.
Propionic acid or sodium propionate is used in stored grains, cheese and milk.
Boric acid is a commonly preferred modern food preservative.
Sodium metabisulphite is used in jams, sauces and pickles.
1.x: Option C is incorrect: boric acid is an old preservative, no longer preferred because it is toxic. Sodium benzoate, propionates and metabisulphite are current preservatives.
1.tq: Discriminate old from modern food preservatives.
n: Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in soft drinks. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in acidic foods. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in fruit juice. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in jams. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in sauces. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Sodium metabisulphite is used as a preservative in pickles. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in stored grains. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in cheese. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Propionic acid and sodium propionate are used as preservatives in milk. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Boric acid was used as a food preservative in older practice. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **boric acid** is a preferred modern preservative, so option **(3)** is the answer.
The notes list **boric acid** only as an **older practice**.
**Sodium benzoate** (soft drinks, fruit juice), **propionates** (stored grains, cheese, milk) and **sodium metabisulphite** (jams, sauces, pickles) are correctly matched.
xa: Sodium benzoate is **C₇H₅NaO₂**, code **E211**.
**Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate** act against **yeasts and moulds** — cheese, cooked foods, pickles.
**SO₂** preserves **dried fruits** and is used in **winemaking**.

1.s: Which food preservative is INCORRECTLY matched with its use?
o: Sodium benzoate – Soft drinks and fruit juice
Sodium propionate – Stored grains, cheese and milk
Sulphur dioxide – Stored grains and milk
1.x: Sulphur dioxide preserves dried fruits and is used in winemaking; propionates preserve grains and cheese.

Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in acidic foods. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]

xa: **Sodium metabisulphite (Na₂S₂O₅)** is used in **jams, sauces and pickles**.
**Vinegar (acetic acid)** preserves **pickles and sauces**.
**Formic acid** has **limited use** as an **antibacterial preservative**.

1.s:
Assertion (A): Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer.
Reason (R): Monosodium glutamate provides umami flavour.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: MSG gives the savoury umami taste, which is why it enhances flavour.
1.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
Monosodium glutamate provides umami flavour. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Monosodium glutamate (MSG)** — **Ajinomoto** — is a **flavour enhancer** because it gives **umami** flavour.
xa: MSG also has a **mild preservative action**.
**Food additives** are chemicals added **intentionally** to improve food (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
⚠ **Adulteration** is **intentionally adding inferior/harmful substances** — not the same as additives.

1.s: The food-safety reforms of July 2026 proposed ending dual certification under which two systems?
1.x: The July 2026 reforms included ending dual BIS/AGMARK certification, alongside Food Safety on Wheels, blockchain tracing and One Nation, One Regulator.
xa: **FSSAI** marks fortified food with the **"+F" logo**.
**Rhodamine B** sale was banned in **Tamil Nadu** — a state ban on a carcinogenic dye.
The **food-safety reform roadmap (Jul 2026)** is a current-relevance item.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about food additives:
1. Food additives are added intentionally to improve food.
2. Adulteration means adding inferior or harmful substances to food.
3. Fructose is an artificial sweetener.
4. FSSAI marks fortified food with the '+F' logo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statement 3 is wrong: fructose is a natural sugar, not an artificial sweetener (aspartame is). The others are correct.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about food irradiation:
1. It uses ionising (gamma) radiation to kill organisms without much loss of nutrients.
2. The Department of Atomic Energy has installed 25 irradiators in PPP mode.
3. The Cold Chain scheme under the PM Kisan Sampada Yojana is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
4. Irradiation lets potatoes and onions keep for 8 months without cold storage.
How many of the above statements are correct?
1.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PMKSY's Cold Chain scheme is run by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (16 irradiation units approved, 9 operational, Aug 2025).

1.s:
Match List I (Chemical) with List II (Found in):
List I
a. Rhodamine B
b. Aristolochic acid
c. Bisphenol A
d. Phthalates
List II
i. Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings

1.x: Rhodamine B – textile dye illegally used in cotton candy; aristolochic acid – Aristolochia in some herbal medicines; BPA – polycarbonate plastics, can linings, thermal receipts; phthalates – PVC plasticisers.

1.s:
Consider the following statements about adulterants:
1. Argemone oil in mustard oil causes epidemic dropsy.
2. Turmeric is adulterated with metanil yellow and lead chromate.
3. The sale of Rhodamine B-coloured cotton candy was banned in Kerala in February 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
1.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the ban (Feb 2024) was in Tamil Nadu.

1.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Fruits keep longer in cold storage.
Reason (R): Low temperature lowers the rate of respiration of fruits.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
1.x: Both are true and R explains A: cold storage works because low temperature lowers the rate of respiration.

1.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
1.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
1.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

1.s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answer from the given options.
Column I (Phylum):

A. Ctenophora

B. Porifera

C. Coelenterata (Cnidaria)
