Standard Tally ERP 9 shortcut lists give Alt+2 = duplicate voucher, Alt+A = add voucher, Alt+I = insert voucher, and Alt+D = delete a voucher or master, so 'Alt+D – Delete a Company' is the odd (incorrect) pair. (A company can be deleted with Alt+D only from the Company Alteration screen.)

12.s: What are Transitions in Powerpoint Presentation?
12.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
12.x: Slide transitions are the visual effects used when one slide gives way to (introduces) the next; animations act on objects within a slide. Off-topic, moved to software.

12.s: To move to the bottom of a document, press
12.x: Ctrl + End moves to the bottom (end) of the document; the End key alone only moves to the end of the current line. Off-topic, moved to software.

12.s: The icon with a minus sign (-) in Windows is used to
o: Move the window to the required place
12.x: The minus (–) button on a window's title bar minimises the window.

12.s: A function inside another function in excel is called
12.x: A function used inside another function in Excel is a nested function, e.g. =ROUND(SUM(A1:A5),0). Round and Sum are single functions.

12.s: MS - Excel is a good application for What IF analysis. Which of the following tool help for this?
12.x: Goal Seek is MS-Excel's What-If Analysis tool that finds the input needed to reach a target result (the other What-If tools are Scenario Manager and Data Table). Off-topic ICT question.

12.s: In MS-Access, Lookup wizard is used to:
12.x: In MS-Access the Lookup Wizard makes a field that picks its value from another table (or a value list).

12.s: When you start typing the same value as of some cells on same column, Excel automatically shows that text. This feature is known as :
12.x: AutoComplete in Excel suggests the rest of an entry when you start typing text already present in that column. AutoFill extends series, AutoCorrect fixes typos.

12.s: All the slides of MS PowerPoint presentation can be viewed in a single screen by using __.
12.x: Slide Sorter view shows all slides as thumbnails on one screen; Slide Show runs them one at a time and Master view edits the template. (Computers; moved to row 12.)

12.s: 'Technology Preservation' is also referred to as:
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: A computer museum preserves old computing technology, so 'technology preservation' refers to it (APPSC 2019).

12.s: The full form or meaning of I.C.T
12.x: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology, the devices and applications used to access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information.

12.s: Identify the positive impact of internet in life.
o: Users suffer from internet addiction disorder.
Best source of knowledge through a click.
Leads to less physical activity and poor eye sight.
12.x: Easy access to knowledge at a click is the positive impact; cyber-crime, internet addiction and poor eyesight are negative effects.

12.s: The field of science which studies automation and communication between human and machine is called-
12.x: Cybernetics, named by Norbert Wiener, is the study of automation, control and communication between human and machine; hydroponics, cryogenics and dietetics are unrelated.

12.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Smart card is a plastic card with an embedded microchip.

II. Digital technology is primarily used with new physical communication medium such as satellite and fibre optics transmission.

III. A digital library is a collection of documents in an organised electronic form available on the internet only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: A smart card is a plastic card with an embedded microchip, and digital technology is used with satellite and fibre-optic transmission. A digital library need not be on the internet only, so III is wrong (UPSC 2002: I and II).

12.s: Which of the following is not the term of 'Information Technology'?
12.x: Cyberspace, upload and modem are standard IT terms; 'light storage' is not an IT term.

12.s: The term Information Technology can be defined as
12.x:
Printed key / question banks: Connectivity + Hardware. Many textbooks instead define IT as computers + communication (connectivity) (testbook explanation; general knowledge).
The printed key defines IT as connectivity + hardware, i.e. networked hardware for acquiring, processing and sharing information.

12.s: "Computer is an instrument to replace human brain". This definition of computer is:
12.x: The definition is incorrect: a computer is a fast machine that obeys programs written by humans; it has no thinking or judgement of its own and cannot replace the brain.

12.s: Which one of the following is NOT a computer term ?
12.x:
Printed key kept, but strictly all four options are computer terms, so the question has no clean answer.
The printed MPPSC 2019 key is 'BINARY CODE'. (Printed key kept; the official key could not be found.)

12.s: Which of the following is an example of technology preservation?
12.x: A computer museum preserves old technology, so it is an example of technology preservation.

12.s: Which of the following is a concern linked with the spread of ICT?
12.x: Concerns of ICT include privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology.

12.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Artificial Intelligence makes machines intelligent so that they mimic human actions.
2. ICT aims at smooth human-human, human-machine and machine-machine (M2M) communication.
3. The term 'cybernetics' was coined by Charles Babbage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'cybernetics' – the study of automation and communication between human and machine – was coined by Norbert Wiener.

12.s: Datum is
12.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
12.x: Datum is the singular of 'data': a single piece of information or fact.

12.s: Digitization is
12.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
12.at: The process in which media is made into computer readable form
12.x: Digitisation converts text, images, sound or video from analogue form into digital (computer-readable) form.

12.s: Communicated Information can be termed as
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: Information that is communicated is called a message.

12.s: Information is piecemeal, ____ particular; while knowledge is ____ and coherent.
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: Information is piecemeal, fragmented and particular, while knowledge is structured and coherent.

12.s: Information is
12.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
12.x: Information is processed (organised) data that has meaning.

12.s: In using inferential statistics, which one of the following will be considered as relevant information?
o: Information about the tool of research
12.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
12.x: In inferential statistics, the sampling procedure decides how far results from the sample can be generalised to the population.

12.s: Among the following groups, which group is most reliable for primary source of information? (Information Sources)
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: Primary sources of information are original records such as patents, standards, theses and journal articles.

12.s: Encapsulation is a term associated with:
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: Encapsulation is a digital-preservation strategy: an object is packaged with its metadata and the information needed to render it later. (ICT item; moved.)

12.s: Abstract which not only describes the content of the work but also evaluates the work and its presentation is called
12.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
12.x: A critical abstract summarises a work and also evaluates it and its presentation. An informative or indicative abstract only describes the content.

12.s: SQL stands for
12.x: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, used to manage relational databases. Off-topic here; moved to software.

12.s: Which Command is used to modify the structure of the database?
12.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
12.x: ALTER (a DDL command) changes the structure of a table; UPDATE changes the data, REVOKE removes privileges.

12.s: Database is
o: A collection of information that can only be retrieved
An organized collection of data that can be manipulated or retrieved
A collection of only numeric data that can be manipulated and retrieved
A backup storage where data can be saved
12.x: A database is an organised collection of data that can be stored, manipulated and retrieved; it is not read-only, not limited to numbers and not merely a backup store. (ICT item, moved.)

12.s: What is Cardinality?
o: Number of entities in a entity set.
Number of times an entity set participates in a relationship set.
Number of attributes of an entity.
Number of Unique keys of an entity set.
12.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
12.x: In ER modelling, cardinality is the number of times an entity of an entity set participates in a relationship set (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many). The number of entities in a set or of attributes is something else.

12.s: An RDBMS consists of
12.x: An RDBMS stores data as a collection of related tables (relations) made of records and fields. (Moved to 5:12.)

13.s: The software, which allows you to view the webpage, is called
13.x: A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) is the software used to view web pages. A website is the content, and an interpreter or OS is other software.

13.s: Which of the following is not a means of communication?
13.x: Snapdeal is an e-commerce company, not a means of communication. Darknet, the Internet and Bluetooth all carry communication.

13.s: Commercial messages on the net are identified as
13.x: 'Webmercial' (web + commercial) is the term for a commercial or advertising message on the internet.

13.s: The web server maintains information in the ____ which have all the text marked with ____ tags.
13.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
13.x: A web server keeps information in web pages, and their text is marked up with HTML (HyperText Markup Language) tags.

13.s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:

A. Web 3.0 technology enables people to control their own data.

B. In Web 3.0 world, there can be blockchain based social networks.

C. Web 3.0 is operated by users collectively rather than a corporation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: All three are correct: Web 3.0 lets users control their own data, allows blockchain-based social networks, and is run collectively by users (DAOs) rather than by corporations (UPSC 2022 answer d).

13.s: Microsoft's new search engine launched in 2009 is called as
13.x: Microsoft launched the Bing search engine in 2009 (replacing Live Search). Buzz was a Google social tool.

13.s: The language of the world wide web is:
13.x: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language of the WWW; the other options are misspellings.

13.s: The following is one of the world's most popular server-side scripting language of building dynamic and data-driven Web applications
13.x: PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely used server-side scripting language for dynamic, data-driven websites. The other expansions are invented.

13.s: What is the use of <em> tag in HTML?
o: Indicate the importance of the text.
Increase the font size of the text.
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: The <em> tag marks emphasised text, i.e. it stresses the importance of the text (shown in italics). It does not create lists or change font size.

13.s: Which one of the following is not a search engine?
13.x: Chrome is a web browser (by Google), not a search engine. Google, Yahoo and Bing are search engines.

13.s: Which of the following is not a web browser?
13.x: Yahoo is a search engine and web portal, not a web browser. Internet Explorer, Firefox and Chrome are browsers.

13.s: In the field of Internet, W3C stands for :
13.x: W3C = World Wide Web Consortium, the international web standards body founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994.

13.s: Which of the following is a search engine?
13.x: Baidu is China's leading search engine. Packets are units of data and cookies are browser data.

13.s: Which of the following is not a search engine?
13.x: Orkut was Google's social networking site, not a search engine. Google and AltaVista are search engines, and ScienceDirect is a searchable research database.

13.s: DuckDuckGo is a
13.x: DuckDuckGo is a privacy-focused search engine that does not collect user information.

13.s: Which web browser was developed by Google?
13.x: Google developed the Chrome browser (2008). Internet Explorer is Microsoft's, Firefox is Mozilla's and Safari is Apple's.

13.s: The first page displayed by Web Browser after opening a Website is called :
13.x: The home page is the first page a browser shows when a website is opened.

13.s: Which of the following is not a Web browser?
13.x: Google Apps is a productivity suite, not a web browser. Opera, Vivaldi and Firefox are browsers.

13.s: Web Crawler is also known as :
13.x: A web crawler is also called a web spider (spiderbot): a bot that scans the Web for indexing.

13.s: Bing is a web search engine owned and operated by :
13.x: Bing is owned and operated by Microsoft.

13.s: JSP stands for :
13.x: JSP = Java Server Pages, a technology for dynamic web pages released by Sun Microsystems in 1999.

13.s: Which one of the following computer languages is used for displaying web pages and other information that can be displayed in a web browser?
13.x: HTML is the language used to build and display web pages in a browser. HTTP is the transfer protocol, not a display language.

13.s: Which one of the following is the small piece of data sent from a website and stored in a user’s web browser while a user is browsing a website?
13.x: A cookie is a small piece of data sent by a website and stored in the user's browser. A worm is malware, and a thumbnail is a small image.

13.s: In order to view pages on a website, the user needs to enter the site address called
13.x: A web page is opened by entering its URL (Uniform Resource Locator). A MAC address identifies hardware, and an e-mail address identifies a mailbox.

13.s: In information technology, what does HTML refers?
13.x: HTML = HyperText Markup Language.

13.s: Kurrently is a/an :
13.x: Kurrently is a real-time search engine for social-media content (Twitter, Facebook).

13.s: Yahoo, Google, and MSN are –
13.x: Yahoo, Google and MSN are internet sites (search engines/portals).

13.s: What is a homepage?
13.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
13.x: A homepage is the main or introductory page of a website, from which its other pages are linked.

13.s: Solr is related to
13.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
13.x: Apache Solr is an open-source enterprise search platform (built on Lucene) used for full-text indexing and searching, e.g. in library discovery systems.

13.s: The search engine "Bing" is created and operated by
13.x: Bing is the search engine of Microsoft.

13.s: An online search in which all aspects of the records in natural language may be used as sought terms is known as ____.
13.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
13.x: Free-text searching lets every word in the records, in natural language, be used as a search term (unlike controlled-vocabulary searching).

13.s: To reload a webpage, press the ____ button.
13.x: A web page is reloaded with the browser's Reload (Refresh) button, shortcut F5 or Ctrl+R. Ctrl alone does nothing. (Off-topic: ICT.)

13.s: In a URL, which part comes immediately after the protocol (such as https://)?
13.x: A URL has the protocol, then the domain name, then the path to the file.
xa: **URL** = **Uniform Resource Locator**.
**DNS** turns the domain name into a numerical **IP address**.
**NIXI** runs India's **.in registry**.

13.s: Which of the following indexes webpages so that they can be found?
13.x: A search engine indexes pages; a web server stores and serves them and a browser displays them.
xa: ⚠ Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" = **browser**; "which one stores them" = **server**.
**URL** parts: **protocol** + **domain name** + **path to the file**.
The **surface web** (~**4-5%**) is the part indexed by search engines.

13.s: What is the main role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)?
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
13.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
13.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
xs: **W3C** **develops and maintains web standards** so pages work the same across browsers — so option **(1)** is correct.
MAC addresses are **burnt into the network card**; the global domain name system is coordinated by **ICANN**.
xa: W3C was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994**.
Berners-Lee invented the **WWW** in **1989** at **CERN**.
Core front-end technologies: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript**.

13.s: What is the full form of HTML?
13.x: Webpages are marked up with HTML, HyperText Markup Language.

13.s: What is the full form of URL?
13.x: URL = Uniform Resource Locator.

13.s: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
13.x: Baidu is a Chinese search engine; Firefox, Opera and Vivaldi are web browsers.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the Web:
1. The deep web, about 90-95% of the Web, is not indexed by search engines.
2. The dark web is a small hidden part of the deep web that needs tools such as Tor or I2P.
3. Web 3.0 consists of static, read-only HTML pages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: static read-only HTML pages describe Web 1.0 (1990s); Web 3.0 is the decentralised (blockchain), semantic/AI web – read-write-own.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. OCEN (Open Credit Enablement Network) aims to democratise lending so that small borrowers get good credit terms.
2. Java Server Pages (JSP) was released in 1999 by Microsoft.
3. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in 1994 by Tim Berners-Lee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: JSP was released in 1999 by Sun Microsystems, not Microsoft.

13.s: All of the computers and printers on the network are called
13.x: Every device on a network, such as a computer or printer, is a node of the network.

13.s: The hardware unit required to connect a home computer to an internet is
13.x: A modem is the hardware that connects a home computer to the internet over the telephone or cable line. Wi-Fi only distributes an existing connection, and a switch or repeater works inside a LAN.

13.s: What is the function of a modem?
o: Voice to data conversion and data to voice conversion
Convert from analog signals to digital and from digital to analog signals
13.x: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital signals to analog and analog signals back to digital. It does not encrypt, convert voice or check for viruses.

13.s: SMTP is the protocol of which OSI reference model Layer?
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: SMTP (e-mail sending) is an Application-layer protocol (layer 7), like HTTP, FTP and DNS.

13.s:
Arrange the following network devices used, starting from physical layer to application layer of OSI reference model:

A. Router
B. Switch, Bridge
C. Gateway
D. NIC Card
E. Firewall
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: Going up the OSI layers: NIC (physical/data link) → switch and bridge (data link) → router (network) → firewall (network/transport and above) → gateway (up to application). So D, B, A, E, C.

13.s: A device used to convert Digital Data Signals into Analog Signals that can travel over standard telephone lines is called ___.
13.x: A modem converts digital data into analog signals that can travel on telephone lines, and back again. Repeaters, routers and switches do not modulate signals.

13.s: A device used for connecting a computer to Internet through a telephone line is :
13.x: A MODEM connects a computer to the internet through a telephone line. Switches, hubs and bridges join devices inside a network.

13.s: Which of the following performs, modulation and demodulation?
13.x: Modulation and demodulation are done by a modem. Coaxial cable, fibre and satellite are transmission media.

13.s: Which of the following is not a connecting device?
o: None of these (all are connecting devices)
13.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None of these (all are connecting devices)); it is added as option 5.
Router, hub and switch are all connecting (networking) devices, so none of the printed options is 'not a connecting device' and the printed key (Router) is wrong. The original MPPSC 2014 question asked 'Which of the following is a connecting device?', answer 'All of these'.

13.s: In a network environment, which is not server?
13.x:
Official key (MPPSC 2021): Network Server. Strictly, a network server is a server too; it is just the generic term, while the other three are specific types.
File, print and application servers are named server types; 'network server' is the general name for any powerful central computer on a network, so the key treats it as 'not a server (type)'.

13.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Modem helps in stabilizing the voltage
Modem converts the analog signal into digital signal
13.x: A modem converts analog signals into digital signals (and digital to analog). It is hardware, not software or an operating system, and it does not stabilise voltage.

13.s:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below :
(1) Proxy server provides TCP/IP address.
(2) Proxy server processes clients requests by forwarding the requests to other servers.
Code :
13.x: A proxy server is a go-between that forwards client requests to other servers (statement 2 correct). It does not hand out TCP/IP addresses; DHCP does that (statement 1 wrong).

13.s: Which system or arrangement connects microcomputer with telephone ?
13.x: A MODEM connects a microcomputer to the telephone line. A VDU is a display, and UNIX is an operating system.

13.s: IP addresses are used on which layer of OSI reference model?
13.x: IP addresses are used at the Network layer (layer 3; the Internet layer of TCP/IP), where routers work. MAC addresses belong to the Data Link layer.

13.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. The most important technological application of liquid crystals is in digital display.
2. Modem is a device that is connected to a computer and to a phone line.
3. The National Institute of Oceanography is located at Coimbatore.
4. Virginis-70 is a system for recording video programmes. Of these statements :
13.x: 1 is correct (digital display, LCD) and 2 is correct (a modem connects a computer to a phone line). 3 is wrong because NIO is at Goa, and 4 is wrong because 70 Virginis is a star, not a video system. So only 1 and 2.

13.s: The layer between Physical and network layer is known as?
13.x: In the OSI stack the Data Link layer (layer 2) sits between the Physical (1) and Network (3) layers.

13.s: Such a device which convert data into impulses and transmitted it through terminal to computer or computer to terminal over telephone line, it is–
13.x: A modem converts data into signals sent over the telephone line between terminal and computer. Discs and CD-ROMs are storage.

13.s: A modem converts :
13.x: A modem converts both ways: digital to analog (modulation) and analog to digital (demodulation).

13.s: A modem is a hardware device that interfaces –
13.x: A modem interfaces telephone lines with computer equipment.

13.s: For sending and receiving data between computers around the world through telephone lines, we need:
13.x: A modem lets computers send and receive data worldwide over telephone lines. A fax sends images of documents, and a hub only joins devices locally.

13.s: In which year was the OSI model ratified?
13.x: The seven-layer OSI model was ratified in 1984; 1969 is ARPANET, 1989 is WWW and 1994 is W3C.

13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the modem?
o: It converts digital to analog and analog to digital
It works at the Transport layer
It links a microcomputer with the telephone line
13.x: The modem works at the Physical layer, not the Transport layer.

13.s:
Match List-I (Network device) with List-II (Job):
List-I | List-II
a. Repeater | i. Broadcasts to all ports
b. Switch | ii. Regenerates a weak signal to extend the cable
c. Gateway | iii. Forwards frames by MAC address
d. Hub | iv. Joins networks using different protocols
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: Repeater – regenerates a weak signal (Physical layer); switch/bridge – forwards frames by MAC address (Data Link); gateway – joins networks using different protocols (up to Application layer); hub – broadcasts to all ports (Physical).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the OSI model:
1. Encryption, compression and data formats are functions of the Presentation layer.
2. TCP and UDP work at the Network layer.
3. A router works at the Network layer and routes by IP address.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: TCP and UDP belong to the Transport layer (layer 4, end-to-end delivery); the Network layer (3) handles routing and IP addresses.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the OSI model:
1. It has seven layers, with the Application layer at the top.
2. The Session layer lies immediately below the Presentation layer.
3. A modem is a Transport-layer device.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (7 Application, 6 Presentation, 5 Session …). Statement 3 is wrong: a modem only converts signals and is a Physical-layer (layer 1) device.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): A switch can forward frames inside a LAN without reading IP addresses.
Reason (R): A switch works at Layer 2 using MAC addresses, while a router works at Layer 3 using IP addresses.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
13.x: Both are true and R explains A: a switch/bridge forwards frames by MAC address at the Data Link layer; routing by IP is the router's Layer-3 job.

13.s: The web browser 'World Wide Web' was invented by
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (1989, CERN) and wrote the first web browser, itself named 'WorldWideWeb'. Crick (DNA) and Gould (palaeontology) are unrelated.

13.s: World Wide Web was discovered by
13.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(A) Engineering Assistant
13.x: The WWW was invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989. Ted Nelson only coined the word 'hypertext'; Gates and Page founded Microsoft and Google.

13.s: Personal Computers can be connected together to form a
13.x: Personal computers linked together to share data and resources form a network; a server is one machine on a network, not the linked whole.

13.s: Who is the founder of Internet?
13.src: Asst. Director in A.P. Economics & Statistical Services 2011
13.x: Leonard Kleinrock developed packet-switching theory and sent the first ARPANET message (1969), so he is credited as a founder of the Internet (Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, the TCP/IP designers, are not among the options). Bill Gates founded Microsoft.

13.s: Internet allows to
13.src: Asst. Director in A.P. Economics & Statistical Services 2011
13.x: The Internet lets users send e-mail, view web pages and connect to servers, so all of the above.

13.s: Internet in India was started by VSNL in the year
13.x: VSNL launched public internet access in India on 15 August 1995. ERNET (1986) was only an academic network.

13.s: A network of networks is simply called –
13.x: The Internet is called a 'network of networks' because it interconnects millions of networks worldwide through TCP/IP. An intranet is one organisation's private network and an extranet extends it to partners.

13.s: The collection of linked information residing on computers which is available through internet is called
13.x: The World Wide Web is the collection of linked (hypertext) information on computers that is reached through the internet. A web server is only one computer that stores pages.

13.s: Who, among the following is considered as the inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW) ?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW in 1989 at CERN. Vinod Dham is known for the Pentium chip and Edward Kasner for the word 'googol'.

13.s: WWW on the Internet stands for –
13.x: WWW (W3) stands for World Wide Web, the information system of linked documents on the internet.

13.s: World Wide Web (WWW) is a hypermedia system because –
o: It links to other computer resources
It can be used only to bring in video material
13.x: The WWW is a hypermedia system because its documents link to other computer resources (text, images, other pages). Its speed has nothing to do with the name, and it is not limited to video.

13.s: The full form of WWW is –
13.x: WWW = World Wide Web.

13.s: Who is the inventor of World Wide Web (WWW)?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW at CERN in 1989. John Dalton gave the atomic theory.

13.s: In internet, the abbreviation WWW stands for
13.x: In internet usage WWW stands for World Wide Web.

13.s: Who is the inventor of WWW?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW (CERN, 1989). Ray Tomlinson invented network e-mail.

13.s: Once the message is encoded in a desired format it is transferred through a medium called
13.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
13.x: In the communication process (sender → encoder → channel → decoder → receiver), the encoded message travels through the channel.

13.s: Who is called the father of e-Mail?
13.x: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network e-mail on ARPANET in 1971 and chose the @ sign, so he is called the father of e-mail.

13.s: Where did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web in 1989?
13.x: The WWW was invented at CERN in 1989; ARPANET was a US DoD project.

13.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. WWW invented
2. ARPANET
3. ERNET
4. VSNL public internet in India
13.x: ARPANET (1969), ERNET (1986), WWW (1989), VSNL public internet (1995).

13.s:
Match List-I (Year) with List-II (Event):
List-I | List-II
a. 1969 | i. Satyam Infoway (Sify), India's first private ISP
b. 1986 | ii. VSNL launches public internet in India
c. 1995 | iii. ERNET, India's academic network
d. 1998 | iv. ARPANET of the US Department of Defense
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: 1969 – ARPANET (US DoD), forerunner of the internet; 1986 – ERNET; 15 August 1995 – VSNL public internet; 1998 – Satyam Infoway (Sify), first private ISP (ICANN also set up in 1998).

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Data sent over the internet as separate packets still arrives complete and in order.
Reason (R): IP directs the packets to their destination, while TCP checks for errors and reassembles them.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
13.x: Both are true and R explains A: data is broken into packets, IP routes them and TCP checks errors and reassembles them, so nothing goes missing; DNS turns names into IP addresses.

13.s: What does the letter "S" stand for in the Web terminology "HTTPS"?
13.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
13.x: HTTPS = Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; the S means Secure, because traffic is encrypted with SSL/TLS.

13.s: Standard protocol used for Internet surfing is
13.x: TCP/IP is the standard protocol suite on which all internet use, including surfing, runs. ARPANET was a network, while FTP and TELNET serve narrower tasks.

13.s: DNS stands for.....
13.x: DNS = Domain Name System. It translates domain names into IP addresses.

13.s: A database that contains the names and address of various hosts on internet is called :
13.x: The Domain Name System is the distributed database of names and addresses of internet hosts.

13.s: The set of protocols, which defines all transmission exchanges across the internet is called
13.x: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that defines all transmission exchanges across the internet. CSMA/CD is an Ethernet access method, and FDDI is a fibre ring LAN standard.

13.s: FTP stands for :
13.x: FTP = File Transfer Protocol, used to exchange files over the internet.

13.s: Which of the following protocol may be used for accessing World Wide Web?
13.x: HTTP is the protocol for accessing the WWW. SMTP sends e-mail, and SLIP is an old serial-line IP protocol.

13.s: A set of rules that governs data communication is called:
13.x: A protocol is a set of rules that governs data communication; RFCs are documents that publish such standards.

13.s: What is the full form of http?
13.x: http = Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

13.s: Which protocol is used for fetching web pages on the World Wide Web?
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: HTTP is the protocol for fetching web pages on the WWW. HTML is the markup language, and FTP transfers files.

13.s: Which of the following is a valid domain name extension?
13.x: .com, .gov and .net are all valid top-level domain extensions, so all of the above.

13.s: Which of the following countries represented by AU as its domain name?
13.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
13.x: .au is the country-code top-level domain of Australia (Austria .at, UAE .ae, Aruba .aw).

13.s: I.R.C. stands for :
13.x: IRC stands for Internet Relay Chat, an application-layer protocol for real-time text chat. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

13.s: HTTP refers to
13.x: HTTP = HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol of the World Wide Web.

13.s: What does PPTP stand for?
13.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
13.x: PPTP = Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, a VPN protocol.

13.s: Through which of the following does HTTPS encrypt the traffic between the browser and the server?
13.x: HTTPS is more secure than HTTP because it encrypts browser-server traffic through TLS.

13.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
13.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
13.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
xs: **HTTP** sets **how messages pass between web browsers and web servers** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Turning domain names into IP addresses is **DNS**.
Downloading e-mail to a device is **POP3**; PAN devices use **Bluetooth**.
xa: **HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**.
HTTP is an **Application** layer (**7**) protocol.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (when and how fast).

13.s: Which element of a protocol specifies the format of data?
13.x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics the meaning of each field, and timing when and how fast data is sent.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about e-mail protocols:
1. SMTP sends e-mail.
2. POP3 keeps mail on the server.
3. IMAP keeps mail synced across devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: SMTP sends and IMAP keeps mail on the server; POP3 usually deletes mail from the server.

13.s: What is the full form of DNS?
13.x: DNS (Domain Name System) turns domain names into IP addresses.

13.s:
Match List-I (Protocol) with List-II (Function):
List-I | List-II
a. SMTP | i. Downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server
b. POP3 | ii. Sends e-mail
c. IMAP | iii. Assigns IP addresses automatically
d. DHCP | iv. Keeps mail on the server, synced across devices
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: SMTP – sends e-mail (Application layer); POP3 – downloads to one device, usually deleting from the server; IMAP – keeps mail on the server, synced; DHCP – assigns IP addresses automatically.

13.s: Which of the following is a computer network that is confined to a single building?
13.x: A LAN covers a limited area such as a home, office or single building. A MAN covers a city and a WAN countries; a PAN covers only personal devices within a few metres.

13.s: Which of the following is used to connect computers with in a small area ?
13.x: A LAN connects computers within a small area (room, building, campus). WAN and MAN cover wider areas, and IoT is not a network-size category.

13.s: Which network topology is the generalization of Bus topology?
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: Tree topology is a generalisation of bus topology: a branching cable with no closed loops (Stallings). Mesh, ring and star are separate layouts.

13.s: Which of the following is a network type?
13.x:
Printed key: MAN. Strictly, CAN (Campus Area Network) is also a network type (PMF S&T Part 5 p.30), so the stem has two right options; MAN is the standard textbook type.
MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) is a network type by area. Mesh and star are topologies, not types.

13.s: What is a "Virtual Private Network"? Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 87
o: It is a private computer network of an organisation where the remote users can transmit encrypted information
It is a computer network across a public internet that provides users access to their organisation's network while
It is a computer network in which users can access a shared pool of computing resources through a service provider.
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is the correct description of virtual private networks.
13.x: A VPN is a network across the public internet that gives users secure (encrypted) access to their organisation's network. (a) is too narrow, and (c) describes cloud computing (UPSC 2011 answer b).

13.s: ______ is not a common network topology.
13.x: The common topologies are bus, star, ring, mesh, tree and hybrid; 'grid' is not a network topology.

13.s: Ethernet is an example of
13.x: Ethernet is the wired technology (IEEE 802.3) used in LANs, e.g. office Ethernet. Wi-Fi is wireless LAN, not a network scope.

13.s: Internet system uses which of the following topology?
13.x:
Most books and keys: Tree. Strictly, the Internet is a hybrid, largely mesh, interconnection of networks (app notes 5:13: 'The Internet is the largest hybrid topology').
Exam keys say the Internet uses a tree topology, a hierarchical mix of bus and star.

13.s: In the context of the internet, what is the full form of MAN?
13.x: MAN = Metropolitan Area Network, which covers a city.

13.s: LAN stands for
13.x: LAN = Local Area Network, a network within a building or campus. Off-topic, moved to networks.

13.s: Which of the following best describes a private, company wide network, closed to public access?
13.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Intranet); it is added as option 6.
A private, company-wide network closed to public access is an intranet. The printed options repeat 'Internet' (option b is evidently a misprint of 'Intranet'); a VPN is a secure tunnel over a public network, cloud computing is remote services, and an extranet opens part of the network to outsiders.

13.s: What does a Virtual Private Network mainly provide?
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
13.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
13.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
xs: A **VPN** provides an **encrypted tunnel over a public network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not replace protocols, is not a one-room wireless link and is not a privately owned cable.
xa: Network types by scope: **PAN** (personal, Bluetooth) → **LAN** (office/home/campus) → **MAN** (a city) → **WAN** (large areas).
**The internet is a global WAN**.
**HTTPS** also encrypts browser-server traffic, via **TLS**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about computer networks:
1. A firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi uses a MAN.
2. A PAN covers a personal area of about 1-10 m, as with Bluetooth.
3. Ethernet, an example of a LAN, follows IEEE 802.3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: LANs in different cities are linked by a WAN (APPSC 2019); a MAN covers a single city.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network topologies:
1. In a star topology, the failure of any one node stops the whole network.
2. In a star topology, the failure of the central hub stops the whole network.
3. A mesh topology is the most resilient and needs n(n-1)/2 links for n nodes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in a star a failed node is only isolated; only a hub failure stops all. (In a bus, a backbone break stops the network.)

13.s: The standard length of the MAC address is
13.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
13.x: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes, 12 hex digits). IPv4 is 32 bits and IPv6 is 128 bits.

13.s: Which of the following is used to identify a computer uniquely on the internet?
13.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
13.x: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on the internet. SMTP, TCP and UDP are protocols, not identifiers.

13.s: Which of the following is not class of IP address?
13.x: IPv4 has classes A to E only (A, B, C for networks, D multicast, E experimental). There is no Class F.

13.s: IPv4 and IPv6 are addresses used to identify computers on the Internet. Which statement is correct?
o: IPv4 and IPv6 require the same number of bits
Number of bits required for IPv4 address is less than number of bits required for IPv6 address
IPv4 requires more bits than IPv6
Both IPv4 and IPv6 are 32-bit addresses
13.x: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits and IPv6 addresses 128 bits, so IPv4 needs fewer bits than IPv6.

13.s: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is ________ bits long.
13.x: A MAC address is 48 bits long. 32 bits is IPv4 and 128 bits is IPv6.

13.s: A computer on internet is identified by
13.x: A computer on the internet is identified by its IP address.

13.s: Which of the following is not a valid IP address?
13.x: '192.23.350' is not a valid IPv4 address: it has only three octets, and 350 exceeds the maximum octet value of 255. The other three are valid dotted-decimal addresses.

13.s: What is the full form of IP?
13.x: IP stands for Internet Protocol, the addressing and routing protocol of the internet. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

13.s: At which layer of the OSI model is the MAC address, programmed into the network card, used?
13.x: The 48-bit MAC address is burnt into the NIC and is used at the Data Link layer (Layer 2); IP addresses work at the Network layer.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network addresses:
1. An IPv4 address is 32 bits long.
2. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long, written as 8 groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
3. A MAC address is 64 bits long.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes, 12 hex digits), burnt into the NIC and used at the Data Link layer.

13.s:
Match List-I (IPv4 class) with List-II (First-octet range / use):
List-I | List-II
a. Class A | i. 224–239, multicast
b. Class C | ii. 1–126, large networks
c. Class D | iii. 240–255, experimental
d. Class E | iv. 192–223, small networks
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: Class A 1–126 (large), B 128–191 (medium), C 192–223 (small), D 224–239 (multicast), E 240–255 (experimental); there is no Class F.

13.s: Which of the following allows Internet access from cellular phones, portable and hand-held computers and other such portable gadgets?
13.x: 'Wireless web' means internet access from cellular phones, hand-held computers and other portable gadgets. Spaceweb, Astroweb and Cosmoweb are not standard terms.

13.s: Which of the following is a type of Internet connection that uses telephone lines?
13.x: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) delivers internet over existing telephone lines. Cable uses coaxial TV lines, and fibre uses light in glass.

13.s: Slowest Internet connection service is –
13.x: Dial-up is the slowest connection (up to 56 Kbps). DSL, cable modem and leased lines are broadband and far faster.

13.s: The latest edition of Bluetooth is
13.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
13.x:
Bluetooth moved on to 5.2-5.4, 6.0 (2024, Channel Sounding), 6.1 (May 2025), 6.2 (Nov 2025) and 6.3 (May 2026) – now Bluetooth Core 7.0 (Nov 2026, High Data Throughput) (bluetooth.com blog 6 May 2026; audioxpress.com 4 Nov 2026).
When the paper was set (2019), Bluetooth 5.1 was the latest version (now Bluetooth Core 7.0, adopted Nov 2026).

13.s:
Consider the following:
1. Bluetooth device
2. Cordless phone
3. Microwave oven
4. Wi-Fi device
Which of the above can operate between 2.4 and 2.5 GHz range of radio frequency band?
13.x: All four work in the 2.4-2.5 GHz ISM band: Bluetooth, cordless phones, microwave ovens (2.45 GHz) and Wi-Fi, so the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.

13.s: What is the difference between Bluetooth and Wi-Fi devices?
o: Bluetooth uses 2.4 GHz radio frequency band, whereas Wi-Fi can use 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz frequency band.
Bluetooth is used for wireless local area networks (WLAN) only, whereas Wi-Fi is used for wireless wide area net-
When information is transmitted between two devices using Bluetooth technology, the devices have to be in the line
The statements (a) and (b) given above are correct in this context
13.x: Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz band, while Wi-Fi uses 2.4 or 5 GHz. (b) is wrong because Bluetooth is PAN, not WLAN; (c) is wrong because neither needs line of sight (UPSC 2011 answer a).

13.s: The first in the world, the Wi-Fi banking branch network was started by
o: State Bank of India and Windsor
13.x: Yes Bank, with Intel, launched the world's first Wi-Fi banking branch network.

13.s: Speed of internet is measured in
13.x: Internet speed is a data rate, measured in bits per second (Mbps, Gbps); GHz is frequency, GB is storage and dpi is print/scan resolution. Off-topic here; moved to networks.

13.s: Bluetooth 6.0 (August 2024) added which feature?
13.x: Bluetooth 6.0 added Channel Sounding.

13.s:
Match List-I (Internet connection) with List-II (Medium):
List-I | List-II
a. Dial-up | i. No terrestrial wire
b. DSL | ii. Coaxial cable-TV lines
c. Cable broadband | iii. Existing telephone lines, 2-24 Mbps
d. Satellite | iv. Telephone line, up to 56 Kbps
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: Dial-up – telephone line + modem, slowest (56 Kbps); DSL – existing telephone lines (2-24 Mbps); cable – coaxial cable-TV lines; satellite – GEO/LEO, no terrestrial wire.

13.s:
Match List-I (Transmission mode) with List-II (Example):
List-I | List-II
a. Simplex | i. Telephone call
b. Half duplex | ii. Radio or TV broadcast
c. Full duplex | iii. Walkie-talkie
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
13.x: Simplex – one way (radio/TV broadcast, keyboard); half duplex – both ways one at a time (walkie-talkie); full duplex – both ways at once (telephone call).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1 and Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11.
2. Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz band, while Wi-Fi uses 2.4 and 5 GHz.
3. Bluetooth needs line of sight between devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (UPSC 2011: the difference is the band). Statement 3 is wrong: neither Bluetooth nor Wi-Fi needs line of sight.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about wireless technologies:
1. Wi-Fi 7 corresponds to IEEE 802.11ax.
2. Li-Fi carries data on LED light.
3. Wi-Fi Direct links devices with each other without a LAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Wi-Fi 7 is IEEE 802.11be (2.4, 5 and 6 GHz).

13.s: Orbicom is the international network of
13.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
13.x: Orbicom is the international network of UNESCO Chairs in Communication, linking communication scholars and practitioners.

13.s: The 5th World Information Technology Forum was held during 17-18 April 2012 at
13.x: WITFOR 2012 (5th World IT Forum, IFIP) was held in New Delhi, 16–18 April 2012.

13.s: In which year was NIXI, the body under MeitY that runs the .in registry and IRINN, established?
13.x: NIXI was established in 2003 and runs internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.

13.s: A website opens for users of one ISP but not for users of another. What is the likely cause?
o: ISP-level DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
Expiry of the website's domain name
13.x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering, so access differs between ISPs; the other causes would affect all users.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about ICANN and NIXI:
1. ICANN manages the global Domain Name System.
2. NIXI runs the .in registry.
3. BhashaNet is an initiative of ICANN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: ICANN manages the global DNS and NIXI runs the .in registry; BhashaNet is by MeitY-NIXI, not ICANN.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about internet regulation in India:
1. Sections 69A and 79 of the IT Act, 2000 let the government order ISPs and intermediaries to block content.
2. The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
3. The power to suspend internet services lies only under the Cable Television Networks Act, 1995.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the power to suspend internet services is held under the Telecommunications Act, 2023.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's internet connections rose from 25.15 crore (2014) to 96.96 crore (2024).
2. BharatNet fibre reaches 2.18 lakh gram panchayats.
3. CM Chandrababu Naidu and Sunil Mittal discussed an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.
4. BhashaNet promotes the .Bharat domain in the Telugu script.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: BhashaNet (MeitY and NIXI, 2022) promotes .Bharat in Devanagari.

13.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): BhashaNet (2022) of MeitY and NIXI promotes Universal Acceptance for Indian languages.
Reason (R): Universal Acceptance means every app and e-mail system accepts all domain names and e-mail IDs, including those in Indian scripts.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
13.x: Both are true and R explains A: BhashaNet's goal is that domain names and e-mail IDs in Indian scripts (such as .Bharat in Devanagari) work everywhere, which is what Universal Acceptance means.

14.s: 'Ticker' is related to
14.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer Screening Test General Stu
14.x: A ticker (news crawl) is the strip of scrolling text, such as headlines or share prices, along the bottom of a television screen.

14.s: e-journals are usually published on
14.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
14.x: E-journals are electronic journals, usually published on the Internet.

14.s: Directing the user to appropriate sources of information available elsewhere is known as
14.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
14.x: A referral service (in library and information science) directs the user to suitable sources of information available elsewhere, rather than supplying the information itself.

14.s: What is "innuendo" in legal terms?
14.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
14.x: Innuendo is defamation by implication. When spoken it is slander (written defamation is libel), so the flashcard links it to slander.

14.s: Heliodisplay refers to
14.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
14.x: A Heliodisplay is a mid-air display that projects images onto a thin layer of mist, with no physical screen.

14.s: An infomercial is
14.src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
14.x: An infomercial is paid programming: a long-format TV advertisement made to look like a regular programme.

14.s: What is a radio program shared over the Internet called
14.x: A radio-style programme shared over the Internet for streaming or download is a podcast. Internet radio is a live stream.

14.s: The scientific study of signs and sign systems is called 349
14.x: Semiotics is the study of signs and sign systems (Saussure, Peirce). Aesthetics is the study of beauty.

14.s: FCP software is used for
14.x: FCP (Final Cut Pro) is Apple's professional non-linear video-editing software, so it is used for video production.

14.s: Audio-visuals, voiceovers, animation and graphics which are combined with text is called —-
14.x: Content that combines text with audio-visuals, voiceovers, animation and graphics is multimedia.

14.s: A radio program which can be shared via internet is also called:
14.x: A radio programme shared via the Internet for streaming or download is a podcast. Internet radio and digital broadcast are live transmissions.

14.s: Technological determinism means that
o: That Web radio stations must pay royalties for songs that are accessed
Specially equipped mobile units transmit live and taped remote reports back to a local station
14.x: Technological determinism (associated with Marshall McLuhan) holds that technology drives social change, i.e. it 'causes' certain behaviours.

14.s: A radio program which can be shared via internet is als
14.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
14.x: A podcast is a radio-style programme shared as digital audio over the Internet. Internet radio and digital broadcast are live transmissions.

14.s: FCP software is used for
14.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
14.x: FCP is Final Cut Pro, Apple's non-linear video-editing software, so it is used for video production.

14.s: Heliodisplay refers to
14.x: A Heliodisplay projects images in mid-air onto a thin curtain of mist, so it is an air-based display.

14.s: An infomercial is
o: A news program highlighting a topic of interest to advertisers
14.x: An infomercial is paid, long-format TV programming that advertises a product while looking like regular content.

14.s: "According to knowledgeable/informed sources" means
o: Source is official and has access to official information
Source is not official with no access to official information
Source is not official but has access to official information
Source is official with not access to official information
14.x: 'Knowledgeable/informed sources' are not official spokespersons but have access to official information.

14.s: The agency for the measurement for TV audiences is
14.x: BARC (Broadcast Audience Research Council, 2015) measures TV audiences in India; it replaced TAM ratings. IRS and NRS are readership surveys.

14.s: The Wall Street Journal is published from
14.x: The Wall Street Journal is a business daily published from New York, USA (Dow Jones, News Corp).

14.s: Multimedia can contain :
o: Graphics, animation, video, music and voice
14.x: Multimedia combines graphics, animation, video, music and voice (with text). Numeric data alone is not multimedia.

14.s: Name the media company that purchased the legendary studio of 21st Century Fox.
14.x: Disney bought most of 21st Century Fox's film and TV assets, including the studio, in a deal completed in March 2019.

14.s: Which Bollywood film became the world's first feature film offered for download from www.kazam.com at $2.99?
14.x: Supari (2003) was the first Bollywood feature offered for paid download ($2.99) to users of the Kazaa file-sharing network ('kazam.com' in the question).

14.s: What is the full form of CNN?
14.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
14.x: CNN = Cable News Network, the US 24-hour news channel founded by Ted Turner in 1980.

14.s: Real object taken out from their natural setting is
14.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
14.x: A real object taken out of its natural setting (e.g. a preserved plant or animal used as a teaching aid) is a specimen. A model is a replica and a sketch is a drawing.

14.s: Method of assessing information needs of user community is known as
14.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
14.x: In library and information science, the methods of assessing a user community's information needs are called user studies. Off-topic, moved to media/information services.

14.s: Which company makes the Final Cut Pro (FCP) video editing software?
14.x: FCP is Apple's professional non-linear video editor; Premiere Pro is Adobe's.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about multimedia:
1. Its components include text, graphics, audio, video and animation.
2. A podcast is a radio programme shared via the internet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
14.x: Multimedia combines text, graphics, audio, video and animation; a podcast is a radio programme shared via the internet.

14.s: Which body measures television ratings in India, replacing TAM?
14.x: The Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC), set up in 2015, measures TV ratings and replaced TAM.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

15.s: 'eVTOL Technology' is related to which field ?

15.s:
With reference to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), consider the following statements :
I. All types of UAVs can do vertical landing.
II. All types of UAVs can do automated hovering.
III. All types of UAVs can use battery only as a source of power supply.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
15.x: None of the statements is correct. Fixed-wing UAVs cannot land vertically or hover, and many UAVs run on fuel engines or hybrids rather than battery alone (UPSC 2025 key d).

15.s:
Match List-I (Drone class, Drone Rules 2021) with List-II (Weight):

b. Micro | ii. Up to 250 g
c. Medium | iii. Above 150 kg
d. Large | iv. 250 g – 2 kg

15.x: Nano up to 250 g; micro 250 g–2 kg; small 2–25 kg; medium 25–150 kg; large above 150 kg.

15.s:
Consider the following statements about drones in India:

2. DigitalSky is India's online permission platform for drones.
3. Drone swarms are many drones coordinated by software.
4. The AP Drone City is coming up at Visakhapatnam.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
15.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the AP Drone City is at Orvakal, Kurnool.

15.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kisan drones are used for spraying and land mapping; 100 were flagged off in February 2022.
2. Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women's Self-Help Groups.
3. Namo Drone Didi covers 1,500 SHGs.

15.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Namo Drone Didi has ₹1,261 crore (2023-24 to 2025-26) for 15,000 SHGs, not 1,500.

15.s: The World Economic Forum’s proposed Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s:
o: first such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
fourth such centre after Bengaluru, Mumbai and Telangana
third such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
15.x: The proposed centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s third, after the centres in Mumbai and Telangana.
15.tq: Count the ordinal position from the explicitly named earlier locations.
xs: The **WEF** centre in AP would be India's **third**, after **Mumbai** and **Telangana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre**.
xa: The term **Fourth Industrial Revolution** was coined by **Klaus Schwab**, founder of **WEF**, in **2016**.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).

15.s: Electricity, mass production and the assembly line were the defining features of which stage of the industrial revolution?
15.x: Industry 2.0 brought electricity and mass production; Industry 1.0 was steam power and 3.0 automation and computers.

15.s: What is a system in which computing is tightly joined with physical processes, a core element of Industry 4.0, called?
15.x: A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is central to Industry 4.0 and NM-ICPS.
xa: Cyber-physical systems are the **core of Industry 4.0**.
India's **NM-ICPS** mission targets them; it runs **25 Technology Innovation Hubs**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.

15.s: What is a collaborative robot designed to work safely beside humans called?
15.x: A cobot is a collaborative robot working alongside humans; remote monitoring of plants and grids is SCADA.

15.s: In 5G, what is the mMTC (massive machine-type communication) slice meant for?
15.x: mMTC supports dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.
xa: **NDCP 2018** covers **5G, IoT and M2M**.
IoT devices exchange data **without human intervention**.
**DHRUV64** (C-DAC) is a **RISC-V** processor for **5G, IoT, automotive**.

15.x: Industry 1.0 – steam, mechanisation; 2.0 – electricity, assembly line; 3.0 – automation, computers; 4.0 – cyber-physical systems, IoT, AI; 5.0 – human-machine collaboration.

16.x: In June 2023 Microsoft signed an MoU with the Directorate General of Training to give AI and cloud skills to 6,000 students and 200 educators of ITIs and NSTIs.

16.x: Machine learning is a branch (subset) of AI; network design, cyber forensics and full-stack development are not branches of AI.

16.x: FPGA = Field Programmable Gate Array, an integrated circuit that can be reconfigured after manufacture, used to accelerate AI.

16.x: Machine learning is of three types: supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement.

16.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) is Google's AI chip.

16.s: Who among the following is known as Father of Artificial Intelligence?
16.x: John McCarthy, who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' for the 1956 Dartmouth workshop, is called the father of AI. Babbage is the father of the computer; Lee de Forest invented the triode; Eckert co-built ENIAC.

16.s: Artificial Intelligence means
16.x: AI is intelligence created in computers (machines) – machines copying human thinking functions; it is not 'artificial talents' or general creative reasoning.

16.s: Who is known as father of Artificial Intelligence?
16.x: John McCarthy coined 'artificial intelligence' (Dartmouth, 1956) and is called its father. Turing proposed the Turing test; Dartmouth is the workshop, not a person.

16.s: Artificial Intelligence is augmenting the human capabilities by:
o: enhancing mechanical power of computing devices
helping the marketing activities throughout the globe
making machine intelligent and mimicking human actions
16.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
16.x: AI augments human capability by making machines intelligent and able to mimic human actions; more languages, mechanical power or marketing do not describe AI.

16.s:

2. Alan Turing proposed his test in the 1950 paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'.
3. The Turing test was first called 'the thinking machine game'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: 1 and 2 are correct (Dartmouth 1956, proposed in 1955 by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon; Turing 1950). 3 is wrong: the Turing test was first called 'the imitation game'.

16.s:
Consider the following statements about types of AI:
1. All AI in use today is Narrow (Weak) AI, which performs one specific task and cannot transfer across domains.
2. Siri and Alexa are examples of General (Strong) AI.
3. Artificial Superintelligence is a hypothetical AI that surpasses humans in every way.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
16.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Siri and Alexa are Narrow AI; General AI (human-level reasoning across domains) has not been achieved.

16.s:
With the present state of development, Artificial Intelligence can effectively do which of the following?
1. Bring down electricity consumption in industrial units
2. Create meaningful short stories and songs
3. Disease diagnosis
4. Text-to-Speech Conversion
5. Wireless transmission of electrical energy
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
16.x: AI can cut industrial electricity use (1), diagnose disease (3) and convert text to speech (4). Truly meaningful stories and songs (2) are still beyond it, and wireless power transmission (5) is physics, not AI.

16.s: India's first Autonomous Navigation facility, TiHAN inaugurated by the Union Minister of State for Science and Technology, Jitendra Singh at which IIT?

16.s: Which of the following software companies is working with the farmers in Andhra Pradesh for yield management by using artificial intelligence (AI)?

16.x: Facial recognition (computer vision), handwriting comparison and speech recognition are AI pattern-recognition applications (I, II, IV); a hacker cracking a password is a human act, not AI.

16.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: AI4AP is for traffic management, crime prediction and investigation (using CCTNS). 4 is wrong: SAHI is the Strategy for AI in Healthcare.

The speed of sound is greater in air than in steel

20.s: Which one is not an example of electromagnetic wave?

20.x: TIR needs light to go from a denser to a rarer medium: diamond (n≈2.42) to glass (~1.5) qualifies; water to glass and air to water/glass go rarer to denser.

20.s: An endoscope is used by a physician to view the internal parts of a body organ. It is based on the principle of –
20.x: An endoscope is a bundle of optical fibres carrying light and the image by total internal reflection.

20.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. Fibre optics is based on the principle of total internal reflection.
2. In an optical fibre communication system, power consumption is extremely low.
3. Optical fibre communications are free from radio frequency interference.
4. In India, Reliance Group of Industries is engaged in the manufacture of the optical fibre. Which of these statements are correct :
20.x: Fibre optics works on TIR, uses very little power and is free from radio-frequency interference, so 1, 2 and 3 are right. Statement 4 is wrong: optical fibre in India is made by Sterlite, not the Reliance Group.

20.s: Sea seems blue due to –
o: Reflection of sky and scattering of light by the drops
20.x: The sea looks blue because it reflects the sky and water scatters the shorter blue wavelengths; water itself is nearly colourless.

20.s: The speed of light will be minimum while passing through–
20.x: Light is slowest in the medium with the highest refractive index; glass (~1.5) beats water (1.33) and air, and vacuum is fastest.

20.s: Optical fibre works on the principle of :
20.x: Optical fibre transmits light by total internal reflection with very little loss.

20.s: 'Endoscope' used by the doctors for examining the inside of patient's stomach, works on the principle of-
20.x: Endoscopes use a fibre-optic bundle in which light travels by total internal reflection.

20.s: The phenomenon used in optical fiber for transmission of light energy is
20.x: Optical fibres guide light pulses by total internal reflection; plain refraction would let light leak out of the fibre.

20.s: Total internal reflection can take place when light travels from :
20.x: TIR happens only from denser to rarer medium above the critical angle; diamond is denser than glass, so diamond to glass qualifies.

20.s: Which one of the following phenomenon is used in optical fibres?
20.x: Optical fibres work on total internal reflection, which keeps light pulses inside the glass strand.

20.s:
Assertion (A): Small glass beads fixed on traffic signals glow brightly when light falls upon them.
Reason (R) : Light is totally reflected when the angle of incidence exceeds a certain critical value and light travelling in a denser medium is reflected from a rarer medium.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct
20.x: Glass beads glow because light entering them is totally internally reflected back towards the source, and R states the TIR condition correctly, so R explains A.

20.s:
Assertion (A) : A stick is dipped in water in a slanting position. If observed sideways, the stick appears short and bent at the surface of the water.
Reason (R) : A light coming from the stick undergoes scattering from water molecules giving the stick a short and bent appearance.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct

20.x: The stick does look bent and shorter (A true), but this is due to refraction of light at the water surface, not scattering by water molecules, so R is false.

20.s: Optical fibres, though bent in any manner, allows light to pass through. What is the inference that one can draw from it?
o: The concept that light travels in straight path is wrong.
Light can flow through the optical fibres.
Light can travel through the fibres because of their ductility.
Light can travel through the fibres due to multiple total internal reflection.
20.x: Light stays inside a bent fibre because it undergoes repeated total internal reflections; ductility has nothing to do with it, and light still travels straight between reflections.

20.s: In total internal reflection, the light travels from
o: rarer to denser medium and it occurs with no loss of intensity.
denser to rarer medium and it occurs with no loss of intensity.
rarer to denser medium and it occurs with loss of intensity.
denser to rarer medium and it occurs with loss of intensity.
20.x: TIR occurs when light goes from a denser to a rarer medium above the critical angle, and the whole of the light is reflected back, with no loss of intensity.

20.s: Light rays move in straight lines. But through an optical fibre, they can move in any type of zig-zag path because
o: the holes through the fibres are extremely fine.
light rays are absorbed at the entry end and relieved at the exit end of the fibre.
scattering of light occurs inside the fibre.
successive total internal reflections occur as a ray moves through the fibre.
20.x: Successive total internal reflections at the core boundary give the zig-zag path through the fibre.

20.s: Brilliance of diamond is due to
20.x: Diamond's very high refractive index gives a small critical angle (~24.4°), so light inside it suffers multiple total internal reflections, which causes its brilliance.

20.s: In which of the following cases can Total Internal Reflection (when angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle) take place? When light travels from
20.x: TIR needs denser to rarer: diamond to air qualifies; air to water or air to glass go rarer to denser.

20.x: A desert mirage is caused by total internal reflection of light in the hot, rarer air layers near the ground.

20.x: Light signals propagate through an optical fibre by total internal reflection.

20.x: Fibre-optic communication sends information as pulses of light (light waves) through the fibre.

20.s: Optic fiber is mainly used for which of the following?
20.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
20.x: Optical fibres carry signals by total internal reflection and are used mainly for communication (telecom, internet, cable TV).

20.s: In fibre optic communication the source of Light used is:
20.x:

Long-distance optical fibre links use semiconductor lasers (laser diodes), which give narrow, coherent, high-speed light. LEDs serve only short, low-speed links, and a CFL is never used.

20.x: Li-Fi stands for Light Fidelity: data carried by visible light from LEDs (term by Harald Haas).

20.s: The first railway station in the country to provide Google's free public Wi-Fi service is :
20.x: Mumbai Central became the first Indian railway station with Google's free public Wi-Fi in January 2016 (RailTel-Google partnership).

20.x: WiMAX mainly uses licensed bands around 2.3, 2.5 and 3.5 GHz, i.e. the 2-3.5 GHz range (UPSC 2010 key b).

20.x: Bluetooth forms secure short-range Personal Area Networks and uses 2.4 GHz radio waves to send data wirelessly, so both statements are correct.

Landline phone to mobile phone communication
20.x: Bluetooth provides short-range wireless communication between devices (phones, laptops, headsets) using radio waves.

20.x: Project Loon used high-altitude balloons in the stratosphere (~20 km) to give internet to remote areas: wireless communication technology.

20.x: WiMAX (Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access) is a wireless broadband communication technology.

o: It is an experiment to capture aerial pictures and measure the greenery per square kilometre.
It is a drone fitted with a camera for surveillance of the campus and capturing suspicious movements.

20.x: UHF (300 MHz-3 GHz) is neither guided along the ground nor reflected by the ionosphere, so it travels by line-of-sight space waves.

1. of small size of antenna.
2. rain droplets absorb the energy of radio waves.
3. rain droplets disperse the energy of radio waves from their original direction.

20.x: Rain drops absorb radio-wave energy and scatter it away from its direction, so the signal weakens and a small dish antenna cannot pick it up; the key treats all three as reasons.

20.s: …… are used for communication in artificial satellites.

20.x: Satellite communication uses microwaves (uplink/downlink); millimetre waves are only a sub-band of microwaves, so microwave is the better answer.

21.s: When the alarm of your smartphone rings in the morning, you wake up and tap it to stop the alarm which causes your geyser to be switched on automatically. The smart mirror in your bathroom shows the day's weather and also indicates the level of water in your overhead tank. After you take some groceries from your refrigerator for making breakfast, it recognises the shortage of stock in it and places an order for the supply of fresh grocery items. When You step out of your house and lock the door, all lights, fans, geysers and AC machines get switched off automatically. On your way to the office, your car warns you about traffic congestion ahead and suggests an alternative route, and if you are late for a meeting, it sends a message to your office accordingly. In the context of emerging communication technologies, which one of the following terms best applies to the above scenario?
21.x: Appliances, mirror, fridge and car talking to each other and acting without human input is the Internet of Things (UPSC 2018).
