3. The World Commission on Dams was set up in 1998 by UNEP and IUCN.
4. The World Commission on Dams released its report 'Dams and Development' in 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
60.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct as given in the notes; statement 3 is wrong – it was set up by the World Bank and IUCN.

61.s: Recently, North Korea claimed successful test of which type of bomb?
61.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
61.x: North Korea claimed a successful hydrogen (thermonuclear) bomb test in January 2016 and again in September 2017.

61.s: The intense heat of Sun is due to
o: all the three types of these reactions
61.x: The Sun's heat comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core, not fission or chemical burning.

61.s: What is the name of atomic bomb that was dropped on Hiroshima in 1945 by Americans?
61.x: 'Little Boy', a U-235 bomb, was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945; 'Fat Man' (plutonium) hit Nagasaki.

61.s: Hydrogen Bomb is based upon the principle of
61.x: The hydrogen bomb is based on uncontrolled nuclear fusion of deuterium and tritium, triggered by a fission bomb.

61.s: Which of the following processes is responsible for release of energy by an atomic bomb?
61.x: An atomic bomb releases energy by an uncontrolled nuclear fission chain reaction; fusion is the hydrogen bomb.

61.s: Which one of the following is not correct?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Darwin.
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called fusion
'Dry ice' is nothing but solid carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
61.x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. Darwin's evolution, dry ice = solid CO2 and Bell's telephone are all correct.

61.s: The difference between a nuclear reactor and an atomic bomb is that
o: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
no chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb
61.x: Both a reactor and an atom bomb run on a fission chain reaction; in the reactor it is controlled by control rods, in the bomb it is uncontrolled.

61.s:
Consider the following statements: In a nuclear reactor, self-sustained chain reaction is possible, because
I. more neutrons are released in each of the fission reactions.
II. the neutrons immediately take part in the fission process. Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 56
III. the fast neutrons are slowed down by Graphite.
IV. every neutron released in the fission reaction initiates further fission. Which of these statements are correct?
61.x: I and III are correct: each fission releases more neutrons, and graphite slows fast neutrons so they cause further fission. II and IV are wrong: neutrons are not all absorbed at once and not every neutron causes a new fission.

61.s: The stars receive their energy from which of the following?
61.x: Stars get their energy from nuclear fusion, mainly hydrogen fusing into helium, not from fission.

61.s: Which one of the following is not correct :
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Dar-
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called
‘Dry ice’ is nothing but solid carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
61.x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. The other three statements are correct.

61.s: Otto Hahn discovered atom bomb by the principle of –
61.x: Otto Hahn (with Fritz Strassmann, 1938-39) discovered nuclear fission, the principle of the atom bomb. 'Uranium fission' is only one case of it, and alpha or gamma radiation is decay, not fission.

61.s: The principle of atomic bomb is based on –
61.x: The atomic bomb works by uncontrolled nuclear fission; fusion is the principle of the hydrogen bomb.

61.s: Hydrogen bomb was developed by :
61.x: Edward Teller is called the father of the hydrogen bomb (first US test, November 1952). Oppenheimer led the fission bomb project.

61.s: What was the fissionable material used in the bombs dropped at Nagasaki (Japan) in the year 1945 ?
61.x: 'Fat Man', dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, used plutonium-239; 'Little Boy' at Hiroshima used U-235.

61.s: Which one of the following is incorrect?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called
Dry ice is nothing but solid Carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
61.x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one.

61.s: Hydrogen bomb is based on the principle of –
61.x: The hydrogen bomb works by uncontrolled fusion of deuterium and tritium into helium. Controlled reactions describe reactors, and fission describes the atom bomb.

61.s: The principle of atom bomb is based on –
61.x: The atom bomb relies on uncontrolled nuclear fission of uranium or plutonium. Fusion is the principle of the hydrogen bomb.

61.s: The working principle of atom bomb is nuclear fission of uranium and the working principle of hydrogen bomb is –
o: explosion of bomb involving hydrogen gas
61.x: The hydrogen bomb works by nuclear fusion of deuterium (and tritium) into helium, not by fission of thorium or chemical explosions.

61.s: Source of Energy from the Sun is :
61.x: The Sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.

61.s: The difference between nuclear reactor and atom bomb is that :
o: There is no chain reaction in nuclear reactor whereas
The chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled
The chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
Atom bomb is based on nuclear fusion whereas in
61.x: Both a reactor and an atom bomb use a chain reaction; the difference is that in the reactor it is controlled.

61.s: The energy of Sun is released due to :
61.x: The Sun's energy is released by nuclear fusion (hydrogen into helium), not fission or oxidation-reduction.

61.s: Which statement is not associated with nuclear fission:
o: Source of energy in nuclear reactor that produces
Enormous energy is released in an atom bomb
61.x: Energy generation in stars comes from fusion, so it is not associated with fission. Fission is neutron-induced and powers reactors and the atom bomb.

61.s: Solar energy is due to
61.x: Solar energy comes from nuclear fusion in the Sun's core, not ionisation, fission or oxidation.

61.s: The first atom bomb was thrown over
61.x: The first atom bomb was dropped on Hiroshima (6 August 1945, Little Boy); Nagasaki followed on 9 August.

61.s: In which cities of Japan were atomic bomb dropped during Second World War?
61.x: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima (Little Boy) and Nagasaki (Fat Man) only.

61.s: Basic scientific principle behind a nuclear reactor is
61.x: A nuclear reactor runs on controlled nuclear fission. Uncontrolled fission is a bomb, and fusion power is still at the research stage.

61.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The chain reaction process is used in nuclear bombs to release a vast amount of energy, but in nuclear reactors, there is no chain reaction.

II. In a nuclear reactor, the reaction is controlled, while in nuclear bombs, the reaction is uncontrolled.

III. In a nuclear reactor, all operating reactors are ‘critical’, while there is no question of ‘critically’ in case of a nuclear bomb.

IV. Nuclear reactors do not use moderators, while nuclear bombs use them.
Which of the above statements about operational principles of a nuclear reactor and a nuclear bomb is/are correct?
61.x: II and III are correct: a reactor's chain reaction is controlled and a running reactor is 'critical' (self-sustaining). I is wrong because reactors do use a chain reaction, and IV is wrong because reactors, not bombs, use moderators.

61.s: The source of energy of the sun is
61.x: The Sun runs on nuclear fusion (hydrogen into helium), not fission or photoelectric processes.

61.s: Hydrogen bomb is based on
61.x: The hydrogen bomb is based on nuclear fusion of deuterium and tritium, triggered by a fission bomb.

61.s: Nuclear fission is caused by the impact of
61.x: Fission starts when a neutron hits a heavy nucleus such as U-235, which splits and releases 2-3 more neutrons. Protons and electrons do not trigger it.

61.s: The difference between a nuclear reactor and atomic bomb is that
o: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor is not controlled.
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled.
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled.
no-chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb while it takes place in nuclear reactor.
61.x: In a reactor the chain reaction is controlled by moderators and control rods; in an atom bomb it is uncontrolled. Both involve chain reactions.

61.s: Hydrogen bomb is based on
61.x: The hydrogen bomb is based on nuclear fusion; the atom bomb is the one based on fission.

61.s: Which one of the following reactions is the main cause of the energy radiation from the sun?
61.x: The Sun radiates energy from fusion reactions (hydrogen into helium) in its core.

61.s: Which one of the following is not correct?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Darwin.
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called fusion.
' Dry ice ' is nothing but solid carbon dioxide.
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell.
61.x: Breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. Fusion is the joining of light nuclei.

61.s: What initiates the fusion reaction in a hydrogen bomb?
61.x: A hydrogen bomb uses fusion triggered by a fission explosion; an atomic bomb is based on uncontrolled fission.
xa: **Hiroshima** (Little Boy) = **U-235**; **Nagasaki** (Fat Man) = **Pu-239**.
Fusion naturally powers the **Sun and stars**.
**Atomic Energy Act 1948** limited atomic energy to **peaceful uses**.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about nuclear fission and fusion:
1. Fusion releases more energy per unit mass than fission – about 3–4 times as much.
2. All present-day nuclear electricity is generated by controlled nuclear fusion.
3. Critical mass is the minimum mass of fissile material that can sustain a chain reaction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: all present-day nuclear electricity comes from fission; fusion power is still at the R&D stage. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.

61.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Otto Hahn
(b) Edward Teller
(c) Little Boy (Hiroshima)
(d) Fat Man (Nagasaki)
List-II
(i) U-235
(ii) Discovery of nuclear fission (1938-39)
(iii) Father of the hydrogen bomb
(iv) Plutonium-239
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
61.x: Correct matching: (a) Otto Hahn – (ii) Discovery of nuclear fission (1938-39); (b) Edward Teller – (iii) Father of the hydrogen bomb; (c) Little Boy (Hiroshima) – (i) U-235; (d) Fat Man (Nagasaki) – (iv) Plutonium-239.

61.s: The mass number of a nucleus is :
o: the sum of the numbers of neutrons and protons
the total mass of neutrons and protons
always more than the atomic weight
always less than its atomic number
61.x: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons (the nucleon count). It is a count, not the total mass, and it is not always more or less than other quantities.

61.s: The atoms, in which the number of protons is same but the number of neutrons is different, are known as –
61.x: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are isotopes. Isobars share the mass number, isotones the neutron number.

61.s: The isoneutronic group, in the following, is :
61.x: Isoneutronic (isotone) nuclides have the same neutron number: 6C14 (14-6), 7N15 (15-7) and 8O16 (16-8) all have 8 neutrons. In option a the neutrons are 6, 7 and 8.

61.s: Isotopes is that nuclei of atomic nucleus in which –
o: Number of neutrons is same but number of protons is
Number of protons is same but number of neutrons is
Number of both protons and neutrons is same
Number of both protons and neutrons is different
61.x: Isotopes have the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons. Same neutrons, different protons describes isotones.

61.s: The number of neutrons in the nucleus of plutonium nuclide (94Pu242) is :
61.x: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 242 - 94 = 148.

61.s: Constituents of atomic nucleus are –
61.x: The nucleus is made of protons and neutrons (the nucleons); electrons move around it in shells.

61.s: Isotopes are those atoms of the same element which have–
o: Atomic mass is same but atomic number is different
Atomic mass is different but atomic number is same
Atomic number and atoms mass both are same
61.x: Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but a different atomic mass (mass number), because their neutron counts differ.

61.s: Isotopes of an element differ in :
61.x: Isotopes share the atomic number (protons and electrons) but differ in mass number, because their neutron counts differ.

61.s:
With reference to Isotopes, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Atoms with identical atomic numbers but different atomic mass numbers are known as isotopes.
2. Protium, Deuterium and Tritium are isotopes of carbon.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: isotopes have the same atomic number and different mass numbers. Statement 2 is wrong: protium, deuterium and tritium are isotopes of hydrogen, not carbon.

61.s: The Nucleus of Helium has –
61.x: A helium nucleus (the alpha particle) has two protons and two neutrons.

61.s: Heavy water is that water –
o: The temperature of which is kept constant at 4°C
In which insoluble salts of Calcium and Potassium
In which isotopes takes place of Hydrogen
In which isotopes takes place of Oxygen
61.x: In heavy water (D2O) deuterium, an isotope of hydrogen, takes the place of ordinary hydrogen. Oxygen is unchanged.

61.s: The heaviest natural element is ?
61.x: Uranium (Z = 92) is the heaviest element found naturally in significant amounts. Gold, mercury and calcium are much lighter.

61.s: Atomic number of an atom gives the number of which of the following?
61.x: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus (equal to the electrons only in a neutral atom).

61.s: Isotopes of an element have ……… .
61.x: Isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons. They have the same atomic number and the same chemical properties.

61.s: Electrons in the highest energy level of an atom are called
61.x: Electrons in the outermost (highest energy) shell are valence electrons. 'Valence' or 'orbital' protons do not exist.

61.s: An element has an atomic weight of W and an atomic number of N. The number of protons in the nucleous of its atom is
61.x: The number of protons equals the atomic number, N. W is the mass number and W - N gives the neutrons.

61.s: Atomic mass of an element is equal to the sum of number of
61.x: The atomic mass (mass number) of an element is the sum of its protons and neutrons; electrons add almost nothing.

61.s: Atoms of different elements have
o: same atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and different number of valence electrons.
same number of electrons and neutrons.
61.x: Atoms of different elements have different atomic numbers and so different electronic configurations and numbers of valence electrons.

61.s: Mass number is always equal to ……..
o: sum of number of protons and number of electrons
sum of number of protons and number of neutrons
61.x: Mass number is always the sum of protons and neutrons.

61.s: Which one among the following is the most appropriate statement with respect to the atomic weight of an element?
o: The atomic weight of an element is the sum total of the number of protons and neutrons present in the atom of an element.
Unlike mass number, the atomic weight of an element can be a fraction.
The atomic weight of an element is a whole number.
The atomic weight of all the atoms in an element is the same.
61.x: Atomic weight is the average mass of an element's isotopes, so it can be a fraction (chlorine 35.5), whereas the mass number is always a whole number.

61.s: The atoms of the elements having same difference between mass number and atomic number are called …………… .
61.x: Mass number minus atomic number gives the neutrons; atoms with the same neutron number are isotones.

61.s: Isobars have …… .
o: same mass numbers but different atomic numbers.
different mass numbers but same atomic numbers.
61.x: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers (3H and 3He).

61.s: Scattering of α-particles by a thin gold foil suggests the presence of
o: positively charged nucleus at the centre of an atom
61.x: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil but a few bounced back, showing a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom (Rutherford).

61.s: The most of the mass of the atom can be found in
61.x: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus carry almost all the atom's mass; electrons are about 1/1837 of a proton.

61.s: An atom has 7 electrons in its M-shell and contains 18 neutrons in its nucleus. What is its mass number?
61.x: 7 electrons in the M-shell means 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons, so 17 protons. Mass number = 17 + 18 = 35.

61.s: The force of attraction between an electron revolving around the nucleus and the nucleus is an … force.
61.x: The negatively charged electron and the positively charged nucleus attract by the electric (electrostatic) force; gravity is negligible at that scale.

61.s: Neutron is a fundamental particle carrying
o: a charge of + 1 and mass of 1 unit.
no charge and a mass of 1 unit.
a charge of - 1 and a mass of 1 unit.
61.x: A neutron has no charge and a mass of about 1 atomic mass unit (slightly more than a proton).

61.s: Charge on proton is equal to the charge on ………… .
61.x: A positron carries +1 charge, the same as a proton. The electron is negative, the neutron neutral and the alpha particle +2.

61.s: Chemical properties of Isotopes
61.x: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, so their chemical properties must be the same; only physical properties such as mass differ.

61.s:
Which of the following statements with regard to isotopes and isobars is/are correct?

I. Isotopes have same mass number.

II. Isobars have same atomic number.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
61.x: Both statements are reversed: isotopes share the atomic number (not the mass number) and isobars share the mass number (not the atomic number). So neither is correct.

61.s: An atom of carbon has 6 protons. Its mass number is 12. How many neutrons are present in an atom of carbon?
61.x: Neutrons = mass number - protons = 12 - 6 = 6.

61.s: The number of electrons and neutrons in an element is 18 and 20 respectively. Its mass number is
61.x: A neutral atom has as many protons as electrons (18), so the mass number = 18 + 20 = 38.

61.s: Which one of the following statements about the properties of neutrons is not correct?
o: Neutron mass is almost equal to proton mass
Neutrons are located inside the atomic nuclei
Neutrons revolve around the atomic nuclei
61.x: Neutrons sit inside the nucleus; they do not revolve around it (electrons do). Their mass is almost equal to a proton's and they have zero charge.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tritium, an isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons, is made by bombarding lithium with neutrons.
2. Heavy water was discovered by H.C. Urey, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1934 for it.
3. The helium nucleus, identical to the alpha particle, has 2 protons and 2 neutrons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Urey's Nobel Prize (1934) was in Chemistry, not Physics. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.

61.s: The most common method Uranium enrichment is?
61.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
61.x: Uranium (as UF6 gas) is enriched mostly in gas centrifuges, which separate U-235 from the slightly heavier U-238. Distillation, ionisation and calcification are not used.

61.s: The fuel used in the nuclear reactors is
61.x: Uranium (U-235) is the fuel of nuclear reactors. Thorium is only fertile and must first be bred into U-233; radium is not a reactor fuel and 'nuclear water' does not exist.

61.s: Material most commonly used in nuclear power plants is
61.x: Uranium-235 is the fissile fuel most commonly used in nuclear power plants. Plutonium is used in fewer reactors, thorium is only fertile and radium is not a fuel.

61.s: Which of the following radio active elements is used to make nuclear fission reaction?
61.x: Uranium (its fissile isotope U-235) is the element split in nuclear fission reactors and bombs. Thorium is fertile and must first become U-233; barium is a fission product, not a fuel.

61.s: Which nuclear fuel is produced when thorium is bombarded with neutrons?
61.x: Th-232 is fertile; when it absorbs a neutron it turns into fissile Uranium-233. Hard water, hydrogen sulphide and heavy water are not nuclear fuels.

61.s: What nuclear fuel does bombarding Thorium with neutrons produce?
61.x: Bombarding Thorium-232 with neutrons converts it into fissile Uranium-233, the basis of India's thorium fuel cycle. The other options are not nuclear fuels.

61.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to the enrichment of Uranium:

I. Uranium enrichment refers to increasing the percentage of U-238 (the fissile isotope) through the process of isotope separation.

II. Weapons-grade Uranium has to be enriched to a maximum of 20 percent of the fissile isotope.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement I is wrong: enrichment raises the share of U-235, the fissile isotope, not U-238 (which is fertile). Statement II is wrong: 20% is the ceiling for research reactors, while weapons-grade uranium is about 90% U-235. So neither is correct.

61.s: Which one of the following elements is essential for the construction of nuclear reactors?
61.x: Zirconium alloys clad the fuel rods because they resist corrosion and absorb very few neutrons. Cobalt, nickel and tungsten are not essential reactor materials.

61.s: Which Uranium isotope is used in nuclear power plants to produce electricity?
61.x: U-235 is the fissile isotope burnt in nuclear power plants; natural uranium has only about 0.7% of it. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-234 and U-239 are not used as fuel.

61.s: Identify the mineral not associated with atomic power –
61.x: Chromium has no role in atomic power. Monazite is the ore of thorium, thorium is a fertile fuel and beryllium (oxide) is a moderator and a prescribed atomic substance.

61.s: Which fuel is used by Nuclear reactors in India ?
61.x: Indian PHWRs burn natural uranium, which is about 99.3% U-238 with 0.7% U-235, so U-238 is the only printed option that fits. U-270 and U-500 do not exist and gasohol is a motor fuel.

61.s: Which of the following element is not included as a nuclear fuel–
61.x: Cadmium is not a fuel: it absorbs neutrons and is used in control rods. Thorium, plutonium and uranium are nuclear fuels (thorium after breeding).

61.s: Enriched Uranium is –
o: Uranium sticks laid in particular shell
Natural uranium in which radioactive U235 isotope is
mixture of natural uranium and thorium
61.x: Enriched uranium is natural uranium in which the share of the U-235 isotope has been raised by isotope separation. It is not a thorium mixture or coated sticks.

61.s: Which is not used as Atomic fuel?
61.x: Lead is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium and plutonium are fissile, and thorium is fertile and can be bred into U-233.

61.s: Which of the following is not a fuel element?
61.x: Helium is an inert gas and not a nuclear fuel element. Uranium and thorium are nuclear fuels; radium is radioactive but the clear odd one out is helium.

61.s: Which one of the following can not be used as a nuclear fuel?
61.x: Calcium is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium-235 and plutonium-239 are fissile, and thorium is bred into U-233.

61.s: Which metal can be used for producing electricity?
61.x: Uranium is the metal used to produce electricity, as nuclear fuel in power plants. Iron, copper and aluminium only carry or build things.

61.s: Which of the following uranium isotope is used in nuclear reactor for generation of electricity?
61.x: U-235 is the fissile uranium isotope used to generate electricity. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-334 does not exist and U-239 is not a fuel.

61.s: Which one of the following is a good nuclear fuel?
61.x: Plutonium-239 is fissile, so it is a good nuclear fuel. U-238 is only fertile (it must first become Pu-239), neptunium is not a fuel and 'thorium-236' is not the fertile Th-232. (The old app notes said the APPSC 2007 key was U-238; that key was not verified and is factually wrong.)

61.s: The main element in the Ore Pitchblende is
61.x: Pitchblende (uraninite, UO2/U3O8) is the chief ore of uranium. Monazite, not pitchblende, is the thorium ore.

61.s: Which one of the following mineral is used as a fuel in nuclear power stations?
61.x: Pitchblende is the main uranium ore, and uranium is the fuel of nuclear power stations. Bauxite (aluminium), quartz and feldspar are not nuclear fuels.

61.s: What percentage of natural uranium is U-235?
61.x: Fissile U-235 is only 0.72% of natural uranium; fertile U-238 is 99.28%.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about uranium:
1. U-238 forms about 99.3% of natural uranium and is a fissile isotope.
2. Light-water power reactors use uranium enriched to 3–5% U-235.
3. Weapons-grade uranium contains about 90% U-235.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is wrong: U-238 is fertile, not fissile – it absorbs a neutron and becomes fissile Pu-239. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. So only two are correct.

61.s: Which one of the following is not radioactive ?
61.x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive. Astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen.

61.s: Radioactive substance emits –
61.x: An unstable nucleus can emit alpha, beta and gamma radiation, so all three.

61.s: Emission of β-particle from an atom
o: increases the number of protons in the atom.
increases the number of neutrons in the atom.
decreases the number of proton in the atom.
does not change the number of neutrons and protons in an atom.
61.x: In beta-minus emission a neutron changes into a proton and an electron, which is emitted, so the number of protons rises by one.

61.s: What is end product of nuclear fission of Uranium?
61.x:
Printed key / books: Lead (end of the uranium decay series). Strictly, nuclear fission of uranium yields barium, krypton and other fission fragments, not lead (PMF S&T Part 4 p.24).
Lead is the stable end product of uranium's radioactive decay series (U-238 to Pb-206), which is the reading the key takes. Fission itself splits uranium into lighter nuclei such as barium and krypton; radium and thorium are intermediate decay products and plutonium is bred from U-238.

61.s: Which of the following is not a radioactive series?
61.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
61.x: There is no 'carbon series'. Thorium, actinium and uranium are natural radioactive decay series, and neptunium is an artificial series.

61.s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of:
o: Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single positive charge
61.x: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons), so its mass is almost that of a helium atom; electrons weigh very little. Two protons alone would be only half that mass.

61.s: Which of the following particles has zero charge?
61.x: The neutrino has zero charge (and almost no mass). The positron is +1, the electron -1 and the alpha particle +2.

61.s: Which of the following is not a sub-atomic particle?
61.x: The basic sub-atomic particles are the neutron, proton and electron. A deuteron is the nucleus of deuterium (a proton plus a neutron), not a basic sub-atomic particle.

61.s: Which of the following carries a negative charge?
61.x: Beta particles are fast electrons and carry a negative charge. Alpha particles are positive, while X-rays and gamma rays are uncharged radiation.

61.s: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 10 days; it means there will be :
o: complete decay of substance in 20 days
complete decay of substance in 40 days
decay of 3/4 part of substance in 20 days
decay of 1/4 part of substance in 5 days
61.x: After one half-life (10 days) half remains, after two (20 days) a quarter remains, so 3/4 has decayed in 20 days. A substance never decays completely.

61.s: The half-life of a radioactive element is 5 years then the fraction of the radioactive substance that remains after 20 years is –
61.x: 20 years is 4 half-lives of 5 years, so (1/2)^4 = 1/16 of the substance remains.

61.s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of –
o: Nucleus of an atom of helium
Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single
61.x: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons, i.e. the nucleus of a helium atom, so its mass equals that of a helium nucleus.

61.s:
With reference to the radioactivity, which of the following statements is/are correct ?
1. Radioactivity is a nuclear property.
2. Hydrogen bomb is prepared on the principle of nuclear fission.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Codes :
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: radioactivity is a nuclear property. Statement 2 is wrong: the hydrogen bomb works on fusion, not fission.

61.s: Which particle is free of charge?
61.x: The neutron carries no charge. The alpha particle (+2) and proton (+1) are positive, the electron negative.

61.s: Radioactivity is measured by –
61.x: Radioactivity is detected and measured with a Geiger (Geiger-Muller) counter. A hydrometer measures density, a seismometer earthquakes and an ammeter current.

61.s: Which among the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?
o: More than one of the above
61.x: Alpha rays are positively charged helium nuclei emitted by radioactive elements. Beta rays and cathode rays are electrons (negative).

61.s: Which of the following is not a radio active element?
61.x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive, whereas astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive hydrogen isotope.

61.s: Beta rays emitted by a radioactive material are
o: the electrons orbiting around the nucleus.
61.x: Beta rays are electrons (or positrons) emitted from the nucleus, so they are charged particles. They are not orbital electrons, not neutral and not electromagnetic radiation (that is gamma).

61.s: Half-life of a radioactive element is 10 days. What does it mean?
o: Element will be completely disintigrate in 20 days.
Element will be completely disintigrate in 40 days.
3/4th part of element will disintigrate in 20 days.
1/4th part of element will distintigarate in 5 days.
61.x: After 10 days half remains and after 20 days a quarter, so 3/4 has disintegrated in 20 days. The element never fully disintegrates.

61.s: In an observation, α-particles, β-particles and γ-rays have same energies. Their penetrating power in a given medium in increasing order will be
61.x: Alpha is stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium and gamma only by lead or concrete, so penetrating power rises in the order alpha, beta, gamma.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly matches radiation with its usual shielding requirement?
o: Beta — a few millimetres of aluminium
Gamma — a thin layer of aluminium only
61.x: Beta radiation can generally be stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium. Alpha is stopped by paper or skin, whereas gamma requires dense shielding such as lead or concrete.
61.tq: Use penetration order to reject swapped shielding materials.
xs: **Beta** is stopped by **a few mm of aluminium** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Alpha** is stopped by **paper/skin**, not lead; **gamma** needs **lead/concrete**, not paper or thin aluminium.
xa: Alpha = **helium-4 nucleus**; beta = **fast electrons/positrons**.
Gamma = **electromagnetic waves**.
Tritium is a **beta emitter**.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioactive series?
o: The neptunium series is a natural radioactive series
The thorium series begins with Th-232 and ends with Pb-208
The actinium series begins with U-235 and ends with Pb-207
The uranium series begins with U-238 and ends with Pb-206
61.x: The neptunium series is artificial, not natural.
xa: Radioactivity discovered by **Henri Becquerel (1896)**.
**Half-life** = time for half the nuclei to decay.
Emissions: **alpha, beta, gamma**.

61.s: What is a positively charged beta particle called?
61.x: Positive beta is a positron; negative beta is an electron and an alpha particle is a +2 helium nucleus.
n: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus with a +2 charge. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
A beta particle is an electron or positron. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
Gamma radiation is electromagnetic radiation. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
xa: Alpha mass: about **4 atomic mass units**.
Beta penetrates a few mm of **aluminium**; gamma needs **lead/concrete**.

61.s: In which year did Henri Becquerel discover radioactivity?
61.x: Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896.

61.s: In which isotope does the natural thorium decay series, starting with Th-232, end?
61.x: The thorium series runs Th-232 to Pb-208; the uranium series ends in Pb-206, and the neptunium series is artificial.

61.s:
With reference to radioactivity, consider the following statements:
1. Gamma radiation can be stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.
2. Half-life is the time taken for half the radioactive nuclei to decay, so a substance never decays completely.
3. Xenon-135 is called a 'nuclear poison' because it is a fission product that absorbs neutrons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is wrong: a few mm of aluminium stops beta particles; gamma, the most penetrating, needs lead or concrete. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 2 and 3 only.

61.s: In May, 2017, the Central Cabinet decided to launch 10 indigenous nuclear reactors of the following type as part of a mega project?
61.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
61.x: In May 2017 the Union Cabinet approved 10 indigenous 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors to be built in fleet mode. PWRs and FBRs were not part of that decision; Magnox is a British design.

61.s: A moderator is used in nuclear reactors in order to
o: slow down the speed of neutrons
61.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
61.x: A moderator slows fast neutrons to thermal speed so that U-235 can capture them and fission. It does not add, absorb or accelerate neutrons; absorbing is the job of control rods.

61.s: ___ is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.
61.x: Heavy water (D2O) is a moderator: it slows neutrons while absorbing very few of them. Hydrogen peroxide, dihydrogen and CFCs are not moderators.

61.s: Which one of the following is used as moderator in a nuclear reactor ?
61.x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Heavy water. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Heavy water slows neutrons without absorbing many, so it is the classic moderator. Ordinary (light) water is a moderator too, in PWRs and BWRs, which is why the book lists '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

61.s: Which one of the following is used as a moderator in the nuclear reactor?
61.x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Graphite. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Graphite slows neutrons and is a standard moderator. Ordinary water is also a moderator in light-water reactors, which is why the book prints '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

61.s: Graphite is used in the nuclear reactor as –
61.x: Graphite slows fast neutrons, so it serves as a moderator; it is not the fuel. Its lubricant use is outside reactors.

61.s: The moderator used in nuclear reactor is :
61.x: Heavy water, D2O (deuterium oxide), is the moderator. U2O, Na2O and Cl2O are not moderators.

61.s:
Match the following:
Column A: i. Fission ii. Control rod iii. Coolant iv. Fuel v. Reactor core
Column B:
a. Where fuel, moderator and control rods are located
b. Splitting of heavy atomic nuclei to release energy
c. Transfer heat from the reactor core
d. Splitting of heavy atomic nuclei to release energy
e. Substance that slows down neutrons
61.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
61.x: Only option b has fission-splitting of nuclei (b), coolant-transfers heat (c) and reactor core-where fuel, moderator and control rods are located (a). The printed list is garbled: 'e' (slows neutrons) describes a moderator, not a control rod, which absorbs neutrons, and 'd' repeats 'splitting'.

61.s: What is the function of moderator in a nuclear reactor?
61.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
61.x: A moderator slows down neutrons so that they can cause further fission. Absorbing heat is the coolant's job; control rods regulate the rate.

61.s: What happens if the control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor?
o: Chain process would go out of bounds
The reactor will be slow to act
The reactor will continue to work as it is
61.x: Control rods absorb surplus neutrons; without them the chain reaction would go out of bounds rather than stop or slow down.

61.s: The substance used as moderator and coolant both, in nuclear reactors is :
61.x:
Printed key / most books: (a) Ordinary water. Strictly, (b) heavy water is also both moderator and coolant, in PHWRs (PMF S&T Part 4 p.43-44).
Ordinary (light) water is both the moderator and the coolant in PWRs and BWRs. Heavy water does both jobs in PHWRs, which is why the book prints '(a) & (b)'. Liquid ammonia and liquid hydrogen are neither.

61.s: Heavy water is a type of –
61.x: Heavy water is chiefly a moderator that slows neutrons; in PHWRs it also acts as coolant. It is not an ore or a fuel.

61.s: Gas cooled reactor uses following materials as moderator and coolant.
61.x: Gas-cooled reactors such as Magnox use graphite as the moderator and carbon dioxide gas as the coolant.

61.s: Heavy water is used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor. The function of the moderator is
o: to control the energy released in the reactor.
to absorb neutrons and stop the chain reaction.
to slow down the neutrons to thermal energy.
61.x: A moderator slows fast neutrons down to thermal energy so that U-235 can fission. Absorbing neutrons and controlling the rate is the job of control rods.

61.s: If control rods are not used in the nuclear reactor, then
o: chain reaction will go out of control.
there will be impact on nuclear reactor.
61.x: Control rods absorb neutrons and regulate the rate; without them the chain reaction goes out of control. It would not stop or slow down.

61.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to?
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons.
61.x: Heavy water acts mainly as a moderator: it slows fast neutrons to thermal speed while absorbing very few. It does not speed neutrons up or stop the reaction. (In PHWRs it also cools, but 'cool down the reactor' is not the key.)

61.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons
61.x: Heavy water is used as a moderator to slow down the neutrons produced in fission so that the chain reaction can be sustained. It does not increase their speed or stop the reaction.

61.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): If control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor, the chain reaction goes out of control.
Reason (R): Control rods made of cadmium, boron or hafnium absorb neutrons and so control the rate of fission.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
61.x: Both are true and R explains A: control rods (cadmium, boron, hafnium, silver-indium) absorb neutrons; without them the chain reaction runs out of control.

61.s:

List-I
(a) Boiling Water Reactor (BWR)

List-II

(ii) PFBR, Kalpakkam

(iv) United Kingdom
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
61.x: Correct matching: (a) Boiling Water Reactor (BWR) – (i) Tarapur units 1-2; (b) Pressurised Water Reactor (VVER) – (iii) Kudankulam; (c) Fast Breeder Reactor (sodium-cooled, no moderator) – (ii) PFBR, Kalpakkam; (d) Gas-cooled Magnox (graphite, CO₂) – (iv) United Kingdom.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India's PHWRs heavy water is used only as the moderator, while light water is the coolant.
2. Light-water reactors, in which light water is both moderator and coolant, make up over 85% of world nuclear capacity.
3. In May 2017 the Union Cabinet approved 10 indigenous 700 MWe PHWRs in 'fleet mode'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is wrong: in PHWRs heavy water is both moderator and coolant. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 2 and 3 only.

61.s: Which Indian nuclear reactor is used for research purposes?
61.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
61.x: Dhruva at BARC, Trombay, is a research reactor (India's largest). Kaiga, Kudankulam and Narora are power stations.

61.s: Expand BARC
61.x: BARC = Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay (Mumbai), named after Homi J. Bhabha in 1967.

61.s: Expand 'BARC'
61.x: BARC stands for Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, India's main nuclear R&D centre at Trombay.

61.s: The first nuclear reactor in the world was built by a/an
61.x: The world's first nuclear reactor, Chicago Pile-1 (1942), was built by Enrico Fermi, an Italian physicist who had moved to the USA, so 'Italian' is the answer.

61.s:
Assertion (A): DHRUVA is India's largest nuclear research reactor.
Reason (R): Advanced Heavy Water Reactor envisages large scale utilization of plutonium bearing spent fuel.
o: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
61.x: A is true: Dhruva at Trombay is India's largest research reactor. R is also true, as the AHWR burns (Th-Pu) MOX, a plutonium-bearing fuel, but it has nothing to do with Dhruva's size, so R does not explain A.

61.s: The Indira Gandhi Atomic Research Centre is located in :
61.x: The Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (1971) is at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu.

61.s:
Arrange the following Nuclear Research Reactors in chronological order of their establishment

A. CIRUS
B. Zerlina
C. Apsara
D. Kamini
61.x: Apsara went critical in 1956, CIRUS in 1960, Zerlina in 1961 and KAMINI in 1996, so the order is C, A, B, D. CIRUS (with Canada) came before the zero-energy Zerlina.

61.s: The first nuclear reactor built in India is
61.src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
61.x: Apsara (BARC, Trombay, critical 4 August 1956) was India's and Asia's first research reactor. CIRUS came in 1960, Dhruva in 1985 and KAMINI in 1996.

61.s: Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research is at
61.src: Common GS for IFS, APLIS, ATT 2012
61.x: The Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (est. 1971) is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu. Trombay houses BARC; Indore has RRCAT.

61.s: The name of the first Nuclear Reactor built with indigenous technology:
61.x: Apsara (1956) was designed and built by Indian scientists at Trombay, making it the first reactor built with Indian effort. KAMINI (1996) and Purnima came later; Rohini is a satellite/rocket series.

61.s: What is common between Dhruv, Purnima, and Cirus?
61.x: Dhruva, Purnima and CIRUS are all research reactors at BARC, Trombay. None of them is a star, a book or a power plant.

61.s: Atomic energy and mineral resources is a subject under
61.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione

61.s: Under the administration of which one of the following is the Department of Atomic Energy?
61.x: The Department of Atomic Energy (1954) works directly under the Prime Minister, who holds the DAE portfolio. It is not part of the Ministry of Power or the Ministry of Science and Technology.

61.s: Who is the present director of 'BARC'?
61.x:
R.K. Sinha left BARC in 2012 — now Director BARC is Vivek Bhasin (14th Director, since 16 Sep 2023) (energetica-india.net, Sep 2023)
R.K. Sinha was Director of BARC from 2010 to 2012 (then AEC Chairman). Satish Dhawan and Madhavan Nair headed ISRO; Raja Ramanna was BARC Director much earlier (1970s-80s). (now Vivek Bhasin, since 16 Sep 2023)

61.s: Who among the following is a member of Atomic Energy Commission?
61.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
61.x: Printed key kept: Dr. P. Rama Rao (metallurgist, ex-DST Secretary) served on the Atomic Energy Commission.

"Parmanu Tech 2019" conference, which was held in February 2019 in India, was organised by

a. Ministry of External Affairs

b. Ministry of Defence

d. Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

61.x: IGCAR at Kalpakkam was set up in 1971 for FBR technology.

61.x: The DAE was set up in 1954; the Atomic Energy Act came in 1948.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear power laws and fleet:

3. The SHANTI Act, 2025 repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.

61.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 22.38 GW target is for 2031-32; 2047 is the year of the 100 GW Nuclear Energy Mission target. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.

61.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SMRs are up to 300 MWe per unit (the refuelling interval of 3–7 years is right). Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.

61.s: Radioactive element which has been found to have large reserves in India is :
61.x: India holds about 25% of the world's thorium but only about 2% of its uranium, so thorium is the radioactive element with large reserves in India.

61.s: The important nuclear fuel available in India in abundance is :
61.x: India has abundant thorium (about 25% of world reserves, in monazite sands) but little uranium.

61.s:
To meet its rapidly growing energy demand, some opinion that india should pursue research and development on thorium as the future fuel of nuclear energy. In this context, what advantage does thorium hold over uranium?

I. Thorium is far more abundant in nature than uranium.

II. On the basis of per unit mass of mined mineral, thorium can generate more energy compared to natural uranium.

III. Thorium produces less harmful waste compared to uranium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: All three are correct: thorium is about 3-4 times more abundant than uranium, gives more energy per unit mass of mined mineral, and produces less long-lived harmful waste (UPSC 2012 key d).

61.s:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option.

Statement B: KPM Uranium project is located in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh.

61.x: The DAE's Atomic Minerals Directorate established the Tummalapalle uranium deposit in YSR Kadapa district; UCIL mines and processes it there. Kamahalapalli, Pagidipalli and Nagulapalli are not uranium sites.

61.s: In which place of Andhra Pradesh given below, are Uranium reserves found by the Department of Atomic Energy?
61.x: The DAE's Atomic Minerals Directorate established the Tummalapalle uranium deposit in YSR Kadapa district; UCIL mines and processes it there. Kamabalapalli, Pagidipalli and Nagulapalli are not uranium sites.

61.s: Which of the following is available in the form of Monazite sand in the Kerala coastal area?
61.x: Kerala's coastal beach sands hold monazite, the principal ore of thorium. Uranium, chromite and graphite are not the monazite mineral.

61.s:
With reference to India, consider the following statements:
1. Monazite is a source of rare earths.
2. Monazite contains thorium. Human and Economic Geography PMF IAS Geo – 50

61.x: Monazite is a source of rare earths and contains thorium (1, 2 correct). It occurs only in some coastal stretches (Kerala, TN, Odisha, AP), not the entire coast (3 wrong), and only the government body IREL may process or export it (4 correct) – so 1, 2 and 4.

61.s: Monazite is an ore of –
61.x: Monazite is the principal ore of thorium (with rare earths such as lanthanum and cerium). Zirconium comes from zircon, titanium from ilmenite/rutile.

61.s: Which of the following caused radioactive pollution along the coast of Kerala?
61.x: The monazite beach sands of Kerala are rich in thorium, which causes the high natural radioactivity along the coast. Plutonium is not natural there; zinc is not radioactive.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of India's three-stage nuclear power programme?
61.x: India's programme begins with PHWRs using natural uranium, proceeds to FBRs using plutonium-based fuel, and culminates in thorium-based AHWRs or other thorium reactors.
61.tq: Use the fuel-cycle sequence to identify the correct order.
xs: **PHWR → FBR → AHWR/thorium reactors** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Stage I **PHWR** (natural uranium) → Stage II **FBR** (MOX) → Stage III **AHWR** (Th-232 + U-233).
xa: Conceived by **Homi J. Bhabha** in the **1950s**.
Aim: **self-reliance through a closed fuel cycle**.
⚠ AHWR is a **bridge from Stage I to Stage III** without Stage II.

61.s: Which body is permitted to process and export monazite in India?
61.x: Only government bodies such as IREL may process and export monazite, found in the beach sands of Kerala and Odisha.
xa: UPSC 2022 had statements **1, 2 and 4** correct on monazite.
Monazite yields **thorium**, **rare earths**, phosphate and a little uranium.

61.s: Jaduguda, India's first uranium mine, is located in which district and State?
61.x: Jaduguda is located in East Singhbhum district of Jharkhand and is India's first uranium mine.
61.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall method and distinguish Jaduguda from Tummalapalle.
xs: **Jaduguda** is in **East Singhbhum, Jharkhand** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**YSR Kadapa** (AP) hosts **Tummalapalle**, not Jaduguda.
xa: Jaduguda = **India's first uranium mine** and **UCIL's seat**.
Domestic reserves: mainly **Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh**.
**AMD** (Hyderabad) explores atomic minerals.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about monazite?
o: It is the principal ore of thorium
It contains rare earths such as lanthanum and cerium
Only IREL-type government bodies may process and export it
It occurs along the entire Indian coast
61.x: Monazite occurs in beach sands of Kerala, TN, Odisha, AP and others, not along the entire coast.

61.s: What is India's rank in the world in thorium reserves?
61.x: India holds about 25% of world thorium and has the third-largest thorium reserve.

61.s: Besides thorium, which of the following is obtained from monazite?
o: Rare earths such as lanthanum and cerium
61.x: Monazite is the principal thorium ore and also gives rare earths (lanthanum, cerium), phosphate and a little uranium.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about India's three-stage nuclear power programme:
1. Homi J. Bhabha planned it to use India's abundant uranium in place of its scarce thorium.
2. Stage I uses Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors fuelled by natural uranium.
3. Stage II uses fast breeder reactors fuelled by MOX of Pu-239 and U-238.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

The recognition of only five nuclear-weapon states
The treaty’s restriction of only atmospheric tests

62.tq: Test the treaty-specific objection rather than the general purpose of the treaty.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound nuclear disarmament** and still allows **subcritical tests** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear test explosions, not just atmospheric ones — so option (4) is wrong.
Recognising **only five** (the **P5**) nuclear-weapon states is India's objection to the **NPT**, not the CTBT — option (3).
xa: **PTBT** (**1963**) bans tests in **air, space and underwater**; India **signed and ratified** it.
**TPNW** (in force **2021**): first binding treaty banning nuclear weapons; India stays out as it **adds nothing to customary law**.
**NPT** (1968; in force **1970**): India **never signed**, calling it **discriminatory**.

2. It regulates radiation safety in medical and industrial uses as well.

62.s:

63.s: Out of the given below items, which is the generally accepted full form of the abbreviation LINAC in scientific terminology?

63.s: Which of the following radioactive elements is used in cancer therapy?

o: It is a robotic image guided system
It delivers an extremely precise dose of radiation
It has the capability of achieving submillimetre accuracy
It can map the spread of tumour in the body
63.x: CyberKnife is a robotic, image-guided radiosurgery system giving a precise dose with sub-millimetre accuracy; it treats tumours but does not map their spread in the body.

63.s: Which one of the following is used in the treatment of blood cancer?

63.s: Which one of the following radio elements is used to measure the speed of the blood flow in the human body?
63.x: Radio-sodium (Na-24) is used to trace blood circulation and measure the speed of blood flow.

63.s: The radioisotope used to control blood cancer (leukaemia) is :
63.x:
Most keys: Phosphorus-32. Some keys (UPPCS answer) accept both P-32 and Cobalt-60 (app notes 5:63).
Phosphorus-32 is the radioisotope used to control leukaemia; Co-60 gives external radiotherapy, I-131 treats thyroid and Na-24 traces blood flow.

63.s: The radioisotope used to detect tumours is :
63.x: Arsenic-74, a positron emitter, is used to locate (brain) tumours; I-131 is for thyroid, Co-60 for radiotherapy and Na-24 for blood flow.

63.s: The radioisotope used in the detection of tumour is :
63.x: Arsenic-74 is used to detect tumours; Na-24 traces blood clots/flow, Co-60 gives radiotherapy and C-14 dates organic remains.

63.x: Cobalt-60 emits powerful gamma rays, which is why it is used in radiotherapy and sterilisation.

63.x: Radon, a radioactive noble gas, is used in the treatment of cancer; krypton, argon and helium are not.

63.x: Cobalt-60 is used in radiotherapy because it emits powerful gamma rays that destroy cancer cells.

63.x: Electron beam therapy is a form of radiation therapy used for certain cancers, e.g. skin lymphoma; it does not treat prostate enlargement or stones.

63.s: Cancer treatment is done by which of the following noble gas?
63.x: Radon, a radioactive noble gas, is used in cancer treatment; helium, krypton and neon are not.

63.s: The Tata Memorial Centre is the Anchor Centre for which IAEA initiative?
63.x: Tata Memorial Centre is the Anchor Centre for the International Atomic Energy Agency’s ‘Rays of Hope’ initiative.

xs: **Tata Memorial Centre** is the **Anchor Centre** for the IAEA's **'Rays of Hope'** — option **(3)**.
'Rays of Hope' is an **IAEA** cancer-care initiative; Tata Memorial anchors it in India.
xa: **National Cancer Grid (2012)**: treats **7.5 lakh+** new patients a year = **>60%** of India's cancer burden.
The **30 MeV Medical Cyclotron, Kolkata** supplies **FDG** to hospitals.
New therapy: **Lutetium-177** targeted radionuclide therapy in routine practice (2026).

63.s: Which of the following techniques is widely used to find out the age of organic matter?
63.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
63.x: Carbon (C-14) dating is widely used to find the age of organic matter (up to about 50,000 years).

63.s: With what is the age of fossils of animals and trees measured?
63.x: Carbon-14 dating measures the age of fossils of once-living animals and trees; uranium dating is for very old rocks.

63.s: Carbon dating is used to determine the age of :
63.x: Carbon-14 dating is used for once-living remains such as fossils (up to about 50,000 years); the Earth and rocks need uranium methods.

63.s: The age of most ancient mountain group is assessed by –
63.x: The age of the most ancient rocks and mountains is found by the uranium-lead method; C-14 works only up to about 50,000 years.

63.s: Which of the following archaeological samples is adopted to determine the age of firewood bone and shell?
63.x: Carbon-14 dates once-living remains such as firewood, bone and shell (up to ~50,000 years); U-238 is for ancient rocks.

63.s: 'Radioactive dating' is a technique which can be used to measure :
63.x: Radioactive (radiometric) dating measures the absolute age of rocks, not their composition, colour or weight.

63.s: Which of the following method is used for measuring the age of the earth?
63.x: The age of the Earth is measured by the uranium(-lead) process (Patterson); carbon dating covers only ~50,000 years.

63.s: Isotope 6C14 is associated with :
o: Determining the age of the earth
63.x: Carbon-14 (6C14) is used to find the age of fossils (time since the death of the plant or animal).

63.s: Carbon dating is used to determine the age of –
63.x: Carbon dating is used for fossils and other once-living remains, not rocks.

63.s: Which of the following technique is not relevant for dating of soil, minerals, rocks etc?
63.x: Radiocarbon, uranium-lead and potassium-argon are all radiometric dating methods; mining is only extraction, not a dating technique.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radiometric dating?
o: Carbon-14 dating is used mainly for volcanic rocks older than a billion years
U-238 to Pb-206 dating is used for the oldest rocks and the age of the Earth
K-40 to Ar-40 dating is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers
Carbon-14 dating covers once-living remains up to about 50,000 years
63.x: Carbon-14 (half-life about 5,730 years) dates once-living organic remains up to about 50,000 years, not ancient volcanic rocks.
xa: **RTG** fuel is **Plutonium-238**; it turns **decay heat** into electricity via **thermocouples**.
⚠ RTG = **Pu-238** (not Pu-239); **C-14** only for once-living remains.
RTGs power deep-space missions: **Voyager**, **Cassini**, **Curiosity**, **Perseverance**.

63.s: What is the half-life of Carbon-14?
63.x: C-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years; 50,000 years is the upper limit of what it can date.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about radiometric dating:
1. Carbon-14 dating can date once-living remains up to about 50,000 years old.
2. Uranium-lead dating of the age of the Earth was pioneered by Willard Libby.
3. The potassium-40 to argon-40 method is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: uranium-lead dating of the Earth was pioneered by Clair Cameron Patterson. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.

63.s: Radiation used in CT scanning
63.x: CT (computed tomography) scans use X-rays to make cross-sectional images.

63.s: Gamma Rays are?
63.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
63.x: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves (photons) and carry no charge.

63.s: Which one of the following pairs of rays is electromagnetic in nature?
63.x: X-rays and gamma rays are both electromagnetic waves; beta and cathode rays are electron streams and alpha rays are helium nuclei.

63.s: The most important indoor air pollutant is –
63.x: Radon, a radioactive gas from soil and building materials (granite, brick), builds up in poorly ventilated rooms and is the key indoor air pollutant (lung-cancer risk).

63.s: The material used for safety from nuclear radiation is
63.x: Lead is dense and absorbs gamma rays and X-rays, so it is used for shielding against nuclear radiation.

63.s: The SI unit of radioactivity is ……… .
63.x: The becquerel (one decay per second) is the SI unit of radioactivity; the ampere is current and the decibel is sound level.

63.s: What is the name of the instrument used to record and measure ionizing radiation in human beings?
63.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
63.x: A dosimeter records the dose of ionising radiation received by a person; a Geiger counter only detects and counts radiation.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about radon:

2. It is a positron emitter used in PET imaging.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Radon comes from soil gas, building materials and uranium mill tailings; it is an alpha emitter, while PET uses positron emitters like F-18.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about radon:
1. It is a radioactive noble gas used in cancer treatment.
2. Long inhalation of radon can cause lung cancer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: Radon is a radioactive noble gas used to treat cancer, and long inhalation of this alpha emitter causes lung cancer.

(ii) Becquerel
(iii) Gray
(iv) Dosimeter

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

An RTG has no moving parts
An RTG is a type of fission reactor

64.s: What are non-conventional sources of energy, by definition?
64.x: Non-conventional sources (solar, wind, etc.) are by definition renewable (UPPSC 2023 key). Non-renewable and fossil-based describe coal, oil and gas, which are conventional; 'imported' is not a classification of energy sources.
xs: Non-conventional sources are by definition **Renewable** (UPPSC 2023 key) — option **(1)**.
**Non-renewable**/**fossil** sources — coal, oil, natural gas — fall under **conventional**.
xa: Conventional also includes **hydel**, **firewood** and **cattle-dung cake**.

**Natural gas is NOT green energy** (APPSC 2019).

64.x: Solar energy is used most in organic form: plants capture it by photosynthesis, and it is stored in food, biomass and fossil fuels. Nuclear, geothermal and tidal energy are not.

64.x: The Sun is the largest storehouse of alternative energy; tidal, nuclear and geothermal resources are far smaller.

64.x: Solar energy is pollution-free in use; coal, nuclear and petrol all create environmental problems.

IREDA was a Mini Ratna (Category I) in Jan 2023 — now a Navratna since April 2024, so all three statements are true today (PMF Environment Part 7 p.118)

66.s: In electrical motor :
o: heat is converted into electrical energy
electrical energy is converted into heat
electrical energy is converted into mechanical energy
mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy
66.x: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the reverse.

66.s: Turbines and Dynamos are used to convert which energy to electrical energy?
66.x: Turbines and dynamos convert mechanical (rotational) energy into electrical energy.

66.s: ‘Dynamo’ is a device, which converts :
66.x: A dynamo converts mechanical energy into electrical energy; a motor does the reverse, and cells handle chemical energy.

66.s: Dynamo is a machine which is used for –
o: Conversion of high voltage to low voltage
Conversion of electrical energy to mechanical energy
Conversion of mechanical energy to electrical energy
Conversion of low voltage to high voltage
66.x: A dynamo converts mechanical energy to electrical energy; voltage changes are done by transformers.

66.s: A generator converts
66.x: A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy, as in a wind turbine.

66.s: Which ratio gives the Capacity Utilisation Factor (CUF) of a power plant?
o: Actual output to output at full rated power over the period
Output at full rated power to actual output
66.x: CUF is actual output divided by the output possible at full rated power over the relevant period.
xa: Wind CUF **36-40%** vs solar ~**21%** vs coal ~**85%** (Aug 2026).
Offshore sites give a **higher capacity factor** thanks to steadier winds.
Power rises with the **cube** of wind speed.

66.s: What is the typical Capacity Utilisation Factor of wind power in India?
66.x: Wind CUF is about 36–40%, above solar (~21%) but well below coal (~85%).
xa: CUF = **actual output / maximum possible output**.
Offshore wind gives a **higher capacity factor**.
Wind is the **2nd-largest RE source** after solar.

66.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of energy conversion in a wind turbine?
o: Kinetic energy - mechanical energy - electrical energy
Potential energy - kinetic energy - electrical energy
Chemical energy - thermal energy - electrical energy
Thermal energy - mechanical energy - electrical energy
66.x: Wind's kinetic energy turns the blades (mechanical energy), and the generator turns this into electrical energy.

66.s:

2. According to the Betz limit, a turbine can capture at most 16/27 (about 59.3%) of the wind's kinetic energy.
3. IEC Class III turbines are designed for low-wind sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statement 1 is wrong: wind power varies with the cube of wind speed, not its square. Statement 2 (Betz limit 16/27, ~59.3%) and statement 3 (Class I high-wind, Class III low-wind sites) are correct.

Reason (R) : Dry cell has a reversible reaction.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
69.x: A dry cell cannot be recharged because its chemical reaction is irreversible. So A is true and R, which calls the reaction reversible, is false.

69.s: In dry cell, which of the following are used as electrolytes?
69.x: The dry (Leclanché) cell uses a moist paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride as electrolyte, with a zinc can and a carbon rod with MnO2.

69.s: In dry cell, which of the following are used as electrolytes?
69.x: A dry cell uses a paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride as electrolyte. Sodium, calcium and magnesium chlorides are not used.

69.s: Nickel-Cadmium (Ni-Cd) battery is used in :
69.x: Rechargeable Ni-Cd batteries (nickel oxide-hydroxide and cadmium, KOH electrolyte) powered calculators, cordless appliances and transistors, so 'all of the above' is correct.

69.s: Which one of the following pairs of materials serve as electrodes in chargeable batteries commonly used in devices such as torchlights, electric shavers etc.?
69.x: Rechargeable torchlight and shaver batteries are nickel-cadmium cells. Zinc-carbon cells cannot be recharged, and lead peroxide/lead is the car battery.

69.s: Traditional ‘battery’ contains which of the following chemicals?
69.x: The traditional lead-acid battery uses sulphuric acid as electrolyte. Ethylene glycol is antifreeze, and sodium bicarbonate and ethanol are not battery chemicals.

69.s:

69.x: Dry (Leclanché) cell – Paste of NH4Cl + ZnCl2; Lead-acid battery – Sulphuric acid electrolyte; Nickel-cadmium battery – KOH electrolyte; NiMH battery – Metal hydride replaces cadmium. NiMH batteries are used in hybrid vehicles; lead-acid in car starting and UPS.

Design and synthesis of molecular machines

1. Cobalt
2. Graphite
3. Lithium
4. Nickel
How many of the above usually make up battery cathodes?
69.x: Cobalt, lithium and nickel make up EV battery cathodes (NMC, LCO chemistries). Graphite is the anode, so only three of the four count.

69.s:
In the context of electric vehicle batteries, consider the following elements :

II. Graphite
III. Lithium
IV. Nickel
How many of the above usually make up battery cathodes?
69.x: EV cathodes contain lithium, nickel and cobalt (e.g. NMC), while graphite forms the anode. Only three of the four are cathode materials.

69.s: Which one among the following metals is prominently used in mobile phone batteries ?
69.x: Mobile phones use lithium-ion batteries, so lithium is the key metal. Copper, zinc and nickel are not the main battery metal.

69.x: ISRO developed space-grade lithium-ion cells and offered the technology for transfer to Indian industry (2017-18). Organic, graphene and hydrogen batteries were not ISRO transfers.

1. Graphite is generally used as the anode.
2. During discharge Li+ ions move from the cathode to the anode.
3. LiFePO4 (LFP) and NMC are cathode materials.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 2 is wrong: on discharge Li+ ions move from the anode to the cathode. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

69.s:

List-I | List-II
a. LFP | i. Solid electrolyte
b. Sodium-ion | ii. No cobalt or nickel; cheaper
c. Solid-state | iii. Liquid electrolytes in external tanks
d. Vanadium redox flow | iv. Safe, long life

69.x: LFP – Safe, long life; Sodium-ion – No cobalt or nickel; cheaper; Solid-state – Solid electrolyte; Vanadium redox flow – Liquid electrolytes in external tanks. Flow batteries let energy and power scale separately (grid-scale, long duration).

69.s:
Consider the following statements about sodium-ion batteries:
1. They use abundant materials, are cheaper and safer, and need no cobalt or nickel.
2. Their energy density is higher than that of Li-ion/LFP batteries.
3. They are being promoted as a replacement for pumped storage.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Only one (statement 1) is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: their energy density is lower than Li-ion/LFP. Statement 3 is wrong: sodium-ion is a safer, mineral-light alternative, not a replacement for pumped storage.

69.s: Which one of the following is the exhaust pipe emission from Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles, powered by hydrogen?
69.x: A hydrogen fuel cell combines hydrogen with oxygen to make electricity, so the only exhaust is water vapour. It gives off no hydrogen peroxide, hydronium or oxygen.

69.s:
Consider the following types of vehicles:
1. Full battery electric vehicles
2. Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles
3. Fuel cell-electric hybrid vehicles
How many of the above are considered as alternative powertrain vehicles?
69.x: Battery electric, hydrogen fuel cell and fuel cell-electric hybrid vehicles do not depend on a conventional ICE, so all three are alternative powertrains.

69.s:
Consider the following types of vehicles:
I. Full battery electric vehicles
II. Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles
III. Fuel cell-electric hybrid vehicles
How many of the above are considered as alternative powertrain vehicles?
69.x: BEVs, FCEVs and fuel cell-battery hybrids are all alternative powertrains (non-ICE), so all three are correct.

69.s: What is the principal energy conversion in a fuel-cell electric vehicle (FCEV)?
o: Hydrogen into electricity on board, with water as the exhaust
Compressed air into electricity, with carbon dioxide as the exhaust
Battery energy into hydrogen, producing water as a by-product
Petrol into electricity through an external generator
69.x: An FCEV converts hydrogen into electricity on board through a fuel cell, and water is its exhaust product.
69.tq: Test the distinguishing conversion pathway and exhaust product of a fuel-cell vehicle.
xs: An **FCEV** converts **hydrogen into electricity on board**, with **water exhaust** — option **(1)**.
It carries a **hydrogen tank + fuel cell + small buffer battery**.
xa: **Fuel cell-electric hybrid** = fuel cell + battery buffer (NiMH/Li-ion).
BEV, FCEV and fuel cell-electric hybrid are **alternative powertrain vehicles**.
**BEV** = large Li-ion pack only.

69.s: Why is energy storage regarded as a major bottleneck in integrating renewable energy into the power system?
o: Renewable energy can never be connected to a grid without coal generation.
Storage helps balance variable renewable generation and supports round-the-clock renewable electricity.
Storage eliminates the need for electricity transmission networks entirely.
Renewable energy is available only during peak electricity demand.
69.x: Storage addresses the variability of renewable generation and helps provide 24×7 renewable electricity. It does not eliminate the need for grids or imply that renewable energy is never grid-compatible.
69.tq: Apply the system-level role of storage to the renewable-integration problem.
xs: **Storage** balances variable RE and **supports 24x7 RE** — option **(2)**; it is the **main bottleneck** in integrating RE.
CEA needs **336 GWh** storage by **2029-30**, vs ~**500 MWh** BESS operating in **Sept 2025**.
xa: Pipeline: **43 GWh** BESS by **2028**.
**Energy Storage Obligation**: **1% (2023-24)** to **4% (2029-30)**.
**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** stresses **BESS** and hybrid RE.

**VGF** for **4,000 MWh** BESS.
**Energy Storage Obligation**: **1% (2023-24)** to **4% (2029-30)**.

**Waaree** is a gigafactory developer and **Rajesh Exports** an ACC-PLI firm — not BESS sites.
xa: ~**500 MWh** BESS operating in **Sept 2025** vs need of **336 GWh** by **2029-30**.
Pipeline: **43 GWh** BESS by **2028**.
Gujarat also hosts **Reliance** (Jamnagar) and **Tata Agratas** (Sanand).

70.s: Indiscriminate disposal of used fluorescent electric lamps causes mercury pollution in the environment. Why is mercury used in the manufacture of these lamps?
o: A mercury coating on the inside of the lamp makes the light bright white
When the lamp is switched on, the mercury in the lamp causes the emission of ultraviolet radiations
When the lamp is switched on, it is the mercury which converts the ultraviolet energy into visible light
None of the statements given above is correct about the use of mercury in the manufacture of fluorescent lamps
70.x: When the lamp is on, mercury vapour emits ultraviolet radiation, and the phosphor coating turns that UV into visible light. Mercury itself does not convert UV to light.

70.s: The most commonly used substance in fluorescent tubes are –
70.x: Fluorescent tubes contain low-pressure mercury vapour and argon (sometimes neon, krypton or xenon). Sodium vapour is used in street lamps.

Reason (R) : Light Emitting Diodes (LED) lamps are more energy efficient as compared to the Compact Fluorescent Lamps (CFL).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explains
70.x:
Books/keys: both true, R explains A. Strictly, an LED's longer life comes mainly from its solid-state design (no filament or electrodes to wear out), so R is at best a partial explanation (general knowledge, not checked).
LEDs last longer and are more energy efficient than CFLs. Books key R as the explanation, since LEDs waste less energy as heat.

70.x: CFL stands for Compact Fluorescent Lamp; it uses about 75% less energy than an incandescent bulb.

It is pleasing to the eyes

70.x: A common fluorescent tube contains mercury vapour; argon is only a buffer gas, and sodium and neon are used in other lamps.

71.s: What is the goal of PM Surya Ghar Yojana?
o: Install rooftop solar panels in urban areas

71.s: 'Net metering' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of promoting the
o: Production and use of solar energy by the households/consumers
Use of piped natural gas in the kitchens of households
Installation of CNG kits in motor cars
Installation of water meters in urban households
71.x: Net metering lets households with rooftop solar feed surplus power into the grid and pay only for the net consumption. It promotes household solar production and use.

71.s: 'Net metering is sometimes seen in the news in the context of promoting the
o: Production and use of solar energy by the households/
Use of piped natural gas in the kitchens of households
Installation of CNG kits in motor-cars
Installation of water meters in urban households

71.s: Which of the following statements are correct about PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana? (i) To install Solar plants on one crore houses to provide upto 300 unit free electricity every month. (iv) Provision of loan at bank interest 4 percent to each applicant.
71.x: (i) 1 crore houses with up to 300 free units and (iii) a 100% online process are correct. CFA is 60% for the first 2 kW and 40% beyond, not 30%. Loans are at about 7% (repo + 0.5%), not 4%.

List-II (Capacity in MW):

72.x: NTPC's 25 MW floating solar project at Simhadri, Visakhapatnam became operational on 1 July 2022.

b. Ananthapuram-I Solar Park | ii. Galiveedu

72.s:
Consider the following statements about renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Of AP's renewable capacity of 10,639.75 MW, wind makes up about 53% and solar about 41%.
2. AP added about 3,865.63 MW of renewable capacity in 2025-26.
3. As on 31 March 2026, AP ranked 6th among States in total renewable capacity including large hydro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
72.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct (3,865.63 MW added in 2025-26; AP 6th with 15,980 MW incl. large hydro). Statement 1 reverses the shares: solar is 5,614.52 MW (~53%) and wind 4,397.67 MW (~41%).

72.s:
Consider the following statements (as on 31 March 2026 / latest estimates):
1. Gujarat leads India in installed solar capacity.
2. AP's share in India's total renewable capacity including large hydro is about 5.8%.
3. The National Institute of Solar Energy estimates AP's solar potential at about 38.44 GWp.
4. NIWE estimates AP's wind potential at about 123.33 GW at 150 m above ground level.
How many of the above statements are correct?
72.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct (5.8% of India's 274.7 GW; NISE 38.44 GWp; NIWE 74.9 GW at 120 m and 123.33 GW at 150 m). Statement 1 is wrong: Rajasthan leads in solar; Gujarat leads in total RE and in wind.

72.s:
Consider the following statements:
